disease_resistance.summary: Downy mildew: reported as resistant in the JAU 13-year and 11-year compilations. The JAU Cereal Crops release sheet lists it as highly resistant. Smut and ergot: listed as highly resistant in the JAU Cereal Crops release sheet. Blast (Pyricularia grisea): placed in the highly resistant class in kharif 2019-20 screening, with the lowest blast PDI among the tested hybrids. agronomic_details.adaptation: Suited to early-season, scanty-rainfall conditions (JAU 13-year compilation). Sowing is recommended at 60 x 10-15 cm with a seed rate of 3.75 kg/ha. Fertiliser is recommended at N:P:K 80:40:0 kg/ha for kharif and 120:60:0 kg/ha for summer/semi-rabi. Sowing window: 65-70 days in kharif; 71-76 days in summer and pre-rabi. Jamnagar district contingency plan lists GHB 538 and 719 as short-duration options under a delayed-onset drought scenario; this is district-level planning and not a GHB-719 trial result.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
NAME-MATCH NOTE: The Seednet portal page was not retrieved. All evidence below refers to the variety as "GHB 719 (MH 1236)" or "GHB-719" in JAU, ICAR-CRIDA, AICRP and academic sources. The CSC release minutes were not retrieved either, so I could not confirm whether they use "GHB-719 (MH-1236)" or another spelling. Release-year and parent-line details conflict across sources, and those conflicts are noted below.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Described as drought resistant and suited to early-season, scanty-rainfall conditions; also reported as downy mildew resistant and tolerant to shoot fly and shoot borer (GHB-719 entry, JAU variety compilation, 13 years) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
- Same drought and downy mildew claims repeated in the JAU 11-year compilation (GHB-719 entry) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-11-years.pdf
- Listed in a release table as having light downy mildew and lodging tolerance features (GHB 719, ICMA 95222 x J 2454) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Release data sheet lists GHB 719 as highly resistant to downy mildew, smut, ergot and blast; rust resistance field left blank (GHB 719 entry, Cereal crops) -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Blast screening (kharif 2019-20) placed GHB 719 in the highly resistant class, with the lowest blast PDI recorded among the tested hybrids -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361217779_Screening_of_pearl_millet_promising_hybrids_and_varieties_against_blast_Pyricularia_grisea_by_disease_indexing
- Shoot fly and shoot borer tolerance: see STRESS TOLERANCE entry above (JAU 13-year compilation).
- Striga, stem borer and other pest data for this variety: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS

Name note: the search results used "GHB-526" and "GHB-526 (MSH-105)" interchangeably. I could not confirm which name the CSC minutes or the Seednet portal use, so the evidence below is recorded against "GHB-526," which I read as the same entity as "MSH-105."

DISEASE AND PEST -- Partial only. The parentage in the record says the male-sterile B-line 95222B was selected for downy mildew resistance and then intermated to improve resistance. A ResearchGate review on hybrid breeding in pearl millet mentions Jamnagar (Gujarat) in an author affiliation, but the snippet was truncated and does not link any scientist to GHB-526. -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status

drought.details: The ORIGINAL VARIETY DATA records drought as Tolerant. A general crop-guide blog describes GHB 558 as grown for drought tolerance and grain quality, but this source is secondary, non-peer-reviewed and unsourced. In a rainfed hyper-arid trial at SKRAU Bikaner, GHB-558 was one of seven hybrids tested for drought tolerance, but its own standing is not separately reported in the abstract (RHB-177 ranked best on most traits). No physiological mechanisms were found in the digest. Level set to medium because the only corroboration is weak and the CSC record gives no quantitative rating.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to GHB-558 in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Downy mildew: the ORIGINAL VARIETY DATA states the hybrid is highly resistant to downy mildew in both zones and comparable to checks for other diseases. The digest does not clearly attribute downy mildew resistance to GHB-558. The Gujarat ARCC bulletin attributes downy mildew tolerance to GHB-538 and GHB-558 in fragmented text, so the attribution is uncertain. Ergot (Claviceps fusiformis): GHB-558 is listed among tested hybrids in a validation study, but the snippet does not show its resistance category, so no resistance level is assigned. Smut, blast and other diseases: not found in searched sources. Note: the DUS guideline uses GHB 558 only as a reference for spike and grain characters, not for disease scoring.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly, shoot borer and grey weevil: the ORIGINAL VARIETY DATA states relatively low infection to these pests. The digest does not independently confirm this. The Gujarat ARCC bulletin attributes borer tolerance to GHB-538 and GHB-558 in fragmented text, so the attribution is uncertain. No other pest resistance specific to GHB-558 was found.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 2825.00 to 3201.00 kg/ha. JAU compilation: average summer yield about 4728 kg/ha, with 18% grain and 8% fodder gains over MH-179 (the digest also cites MH-169, so the check name is inconsistent). The same source reports about 20.3% more grain and 50% more fodder than MH-169 for a dual-purpose hybrid. ARCC bulletin: grain yields of about 44.49 q/ha (4449 kg/ha) and 77.25 q/ha (7725 kg/ha) in different trial sets, with gains over checks GHB-538 and MH-169. The trial sets are not described in the digest, so these figures are not directly comparable to the CSC range.
agronomic_details.stability: A yield stability study in arid India included GHB 558 among 12 genotypes, but the snippet does not show its stability ranking. The study recommends Pusa Comp. 612 and Pratap for wider testing. Stability across environments is otherwise not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for Zone-A (Rajasthan, Gujarat, Haryana, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab), except scanty-rainfall areas of Rajasthan, Haryana and Gujarat; and Zone-B (Maharashtra, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, with the CSC text truncated). Sowing at onset of monsoon, seed rate 4 kg/ha. Digest: national kharif and summer release; a summer-season study in North Gujarat and a middle-Gujarat summer trial also reported good performance.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC record: highly resistant to lodging; highly responsive to higher doses of nitrogen. The digest's Gujarat release table mentions lodging, but the text does not clearly attach this trait to GHB 558. Morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) JAU release compilation: released for kharif and summer seasons nationally and in Gujarat; summer average yield about 4728 kg/ha; grain and fodder gains over MH-179/MH-169; high nitrogen responsiveness under summer sowing; national check in coordinated kharif and summer trials. (2) Gujarat ARCC bulletin: grain yields of about 44.49 q/ha and 77.25 q/ha in different trial sets; yield gains over GHB-538 and MH-169. (3) 46th AICPMIP workshop proceedings: GHB 558 was the superior hybrid in zones A and B; it was included in a seed-rate and fertiliser trial design at Jamnagar and Jaipur. (4) North Gujarat summer study (IJCMAS): significantly higher grain and fodder yields than GHB 744, GHB 538 and GHB 732. (5) Middle-Gujarat summer trial: best yield and net profit with GHB-558 under transplanting plus biofertiliser seedling inoculation. (6) Arid India yield stability study: included among 12 genotypes; ranking not shown. (7) SKRAU Bikaner rainfed hyper-arid trial: one of seven hybrids tested; own standing not reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GHB-558 (MH-946) EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: "GHB-558" appears in the results. "MH-946" and the Seednet name "GHB-558 (MH-946)" were not found in any result, and no Seednet page was returned. The findings below refer to GHB-558, which I take to be the same variety, but the MH-946 link is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under rainfed hyper-arid trials at SKRAU Bikaner, GHB-558 was one of seven pearl millet hybrids tested for drought tolerance. RHB-177 ranked best on most traits, so GHB-558's own standing is not separately reported in the abstract -- https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Veget.tmp...59M/abstract
- A general crop-guide blog describes GHB 558 as grown for drought tolerance and grain quality. This is secondary, non-peer-reviewed and unsourced -- https://krishicenter.com/bajra-crop/
- An ergot validation study (Claviceps fusiformis) lists GHB-558 among tested hybrids, but the snippet does not show its resistance category clearly -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/359744035_Validation_of_stable_resistance_in_pearl_millet_hybrids_to_ergot_disease_caused_by_Claviceps_fusiformis
- A Gujarat release table for the variety mentions lodging and light downy mildew, but the fragmented text does not clearly attach these traits to GHB 558 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to GHB-558.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The DUS test guideline uses GHB 558 as a reference example for spike and grain characters, not for disease scoring -- https://www.millets.res.in/dus/Pearlmillet.pdf
- Downy mildew and stem borer/shoot fly resistance is not clearly attributed to GHB-558 in any snippet. The Gujarat ARCC bulletin attributes downy mildew and borer tolerance to GHB-538 and GHB-558 in fragmented text, so the attribution is uncertain -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/webArticle/articles/D33312.pdf
- No evidence found for smut, blast or other pest resistance specific to GHB-558.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The JAU release compilation says GHB-558 was released for kharif and summer seasons nationally and in Gujarat, with average summer yield about 4728 kg/ha, 18% and 8% gains in grain and fodder over MH-179, and high nitrogen responsiveness under summer sowing. It is a national check in coordinated kharif and summer trials. It is a dual-purpose hybrid giving about 20.3% more grain and 50% more fodder than MH-169 -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf
- The Gujarat ARCC bulletin reports GHB-558 grain yields of about 44.49 q/ha and 77.25 q/ha in different trial sets, and yield gains over the checks GHB-538 and MH-169 -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/webArticle/articles/D33312.pdf
- The 46th AICPMIP workshop proceedings report that GHB 558 was the superior hybrid in zones A and B, and list GHB 558 in a seed-rate and fertiliser-trial design at Jamnagar and Jaipur -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/pw2011.pdf
- A summer-season study in North Gujarat found GHB 558 gave significantly higher grain and fodder yields than GHB 744, GHB 538 and GHB 732 -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=6027&vol=7-1-2018&SNo=77
- A middle-Gujarat summer trial reports the best yield and net profit with GHB-558 under transplanting plus biofertiliser seedling inoculation -- https://www.semanticscholar.org/paper/Research-achievements-in-pearl-millet-(Pennisetum-Bhatnagar-Yadav/b3479b30f0d60aee62cf765c7154d8152126a9fe
- A yield stability study in arid India includes GHB 558 among 12 genotypes, but the snippet does not show its stability ranking. The study recommends Pusa Comp. 612 and Pratap for wider testing -- http://www.jeb.co.in/journal_issues/202303_mar23/paper_07.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: GHB 558 is listed as ICMA 94555 x J 2290, from the Millet Research Station, Jamnagar. The release notification is S.O. 283(E), dated 12.03.03, under AICPMIP, with an All-India adaptation and 75-80 day maturity -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- This matches the user-supplied parentage (MS 94555A x J 2290) on the female-line code. The user's statement that 94555A was selected for downy mildew resistance at ICRISAT is not confirmed by any result.
- Breeding method: the hybrid was developed at MRS Jamnagar. Its breeding method is not explicitly stated in the snippets.
- Cu and K grain content: GHB 558 ranked among the top genotypes for grain copper and potassium in a diversity panel. It had the highest grain copper (22.59 ppm) and very high phytate (542.5 mg/100 g) -- https://peerj.com/articles/15403/
- Marker or QTL studies: no evidence found specific to GHB-558. The SNP panel and Striga GWAS results do not

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nandi-62(MH 1274) (NMH 68), Pearl millet

Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institute; research papers; seed availability). The record's variety_name is "Nandi-62(MH 1274) (NMH 68)". The Seednet name is "Nandi-62(MH 1274) (NMH 68)" as well. I did not retrieve a Seednet portal page directly. The sources below use "Nandi-62 (MH-1274) (NMH-68)" (PPV&FR), "NMH 68" (AICPMIP/millets.res.in), and "Nandi 62" (hybrid reviews and DMI lists). I treated these as the same variety only where the page also names the parent line ICMA 97444 x NMP 48 or the New Nandi Seeds origin.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The searches returned only general pearl millet release tables.

DISEASE AND PEST
Possible but ambiguous: the millets.res.in release table lists "lodging, light downy mildew" in the same table block as the NMH 68 row, but the layout is scrambled and the attribution to NMH 68 is not certain -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Downy mildew resistance is not stated for NMH 68 in any clearly aligned row -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity: described as late maturity in the NMH 68 release row -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Plant and ear traits in the release table: tall, pubescent nodes, cylindrical earheads, yellow anthers, globular grey grains -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Another row in the AICPMIP table gives 80-85 days, tall, purple stem base, dark green leaves, and bold grains, but this row's alignment with NMH 68 is uncertain -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
Yield data: No evidence found.
Multi-location trial results: No evidence found specific to this variety. The AICPMIP 2015 report mentions New Nandi Seeds Corp entries completing three years of testing, but does not name NMH 68 -- https://www.aicpmip.res.in/ar2015.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: ICMA 97444 x NMP 48 (female x male) -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf and https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Breeding line code: ICMA 97444 is listed as the seed-parent code -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
Type: a hybrid (the millets.res.in table is headed "List of Pearl millet hybrids released") -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
DUS descriptor: "absence of stem anthocyanin" appears under the Nandi-62 (MH-1274) (NMH-68) heading in the PPV&FR compendium, though the same page has layout errors (botanical name shown as Lens culinaris) -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf
QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.
Genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: New Nandi Seeds Corporation, Ahmedabad (private sector) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf and http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
The hybrid review states that New Nandi Seeds Corporation, Ahmedabad developed the largest number of hybrids among private companies in its table; Nandi 62 appears in the hybrid list -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
Lead breeder name for this variety: No evidence found.
Station: No station-level record found beyond the Ahmedabad head office.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institution address (from the record supplied, not independently verified by search): New Nandi Seeds Corporation, 1-Patel Society, Near Sears Tower, Opp. Inklab Society, Gulbai Tekra, Ellisbridge, Ahmedabad -380 006.
Official email, phone, or institute contact page: No evidence found.
Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Singh, S. and others (2014). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. ResearchGate (journal not confirmed) -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status (this review names "Nandi 62" in its hybrid tables; it is not a paper on this variety)
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP report entry with trial data, or KrishiKosh thesis specific to Nandi-62 / NMH 68 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Listed among Gujarat summer pearl millet hybrids (name "Nandi-62") -- http://millets.dacfw.nic.in/Hybrid_pearl_millet.html
Listed in a Directorate of Marketing and Inspection pearl millet listing alongside other hybrids (rabi/kharif context, not clearly a seed-sales record) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/403430983_Pearl_millet_Pennisetum_Glaucum_L_Directorate_of_Marketing_and_Inspection_Ministry_of_Agriculture_and_Farmers_Welfare_GOI
Current seed dealer, NSC, SAU or KVK sales records for this variety: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Delhi, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf and http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf (the millets.res.in table also contains a fragment mentioning Haryana, which is ambiguous)

RELEASE/NOTIFICATION
Release year: 2007 (input record). Notification S.O. 1703, dated 5 Oct 2007 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
PPV&FR: certificate listed 18 Sep 2008 under New Nandi Seeds Corporation as a private applicant -- https://www.plantauthority.gov.in/list-certificates?name=Trees
PPV&FR compendium: Reg. No. 27 of 2009, date of certificate 12/02/09 -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf (the applicant field is inconsistent with the list; the list shows New Nandi as applicant, so this conflict needs checking against the official register)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
GHB-577 pearl millet: evidence digest

Name check: the CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "GHB-577". No search returned a Seednet portal page, so the variety code A0209156 and the Seednet crop entry are unverified. Four searches were run. Where a page lists GHB-577 only as a check or as one name in a long list, I have said so.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name: GHB-577)
- Salt stress: in a pot study on salinity, GHB-577 was reported as superior to other pearl millet varieties under control and saline conditions, with higher vigour index. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2017/vol5issue5/PartN/5-4-445-613.pdf
- Lodging, downy mildew and the other traits listed on the millets.res.in row are for a different hybrid in that table, so they are not attributed to GHB-577. Drought and heat: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST (name: GHB-577)
- No evidence found for GHB-577 specifically. The searches returned only variety lists. The millets.res.in table has a garbled trait cell next to the GHB-577 row, and it could belong to another hybrid, so I have not recorded it. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name: GHB-577)
- Maturity: listed as 80-85 days, tall, in the release-table row for GHB-577. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Maturity class "Late" and kharif sowing for GHB-577 in a seed production manual figure. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277128083_Pearl_Millet_Crop_Management_and_Seed_Production_Manual
- Yield: No evidence found for GHB-577's own yield. A Junagadh Agricultural University groundnut/crop variety document gives pearl millet yield comparisons against GHB-577 as a check, but that refers to another variety. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
- Multi-location trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: the millets.res.in row gives "JMS A 101 x J 2405" (male-sterile parent JMS A 101 crossed with J 2405). The request gave "JMSA-101 X J-2045". The source numerals differ and need checking against the CSC minutes. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Type: hybrid (A x R). The same table places it among hybrids with a notification reference "S.O. 161 (E)" dated 4.02.04 under AICPMIP. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Breeding method and genome resources: No evidence found for GHB-577 specifically.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The release table lists the breeding centre for the GHB-577 row as "MRS" (Millet Research Station) at Jamnagar. No breeder name was found. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Institution as supplied in the request: Millet Research Station, Gujarat Agricultural University, Jamnagar. This is taken from the request; no independent page confirmed it.
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Official email, phone, postal address, or an institute contact page for the Millet Research Station, GAU, Jamnagar: No evidence found in any search result.

PUBLICATIONS
- Khairwal, I.S. and others (2007). Pearl Millet Crop Management and Seed Production Manual. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277128083_Pearl_Millet_Crop_Management_and_Seed_Production_Manual (lists GHB 577 in its maturity and state tables; author list partly visible; the manual's publisher and DOI were not shown)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Physiological and biochemical changes in Pearl Millet (salt stress study, title truncated in the retrieved text). Chemijournal, vol. 5, issue 5, 2017. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2017/vol5issue5/PartN/5-4-445-613.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Development and Diffusion of Pearl Millet Improved Cultivars. Publisher and journal not shown. Lists GHB 577 with 2003 and hybrid type. -- https://files01.core.ac.uk/download/pdf/219473258.pdf
- Authors partly shown (Patel/Srivastava/Joshi/Tripathi group, year not shown). A review on Bajra/Pearl millet (Cenchrus americanus). Lists GHB-577 under several states. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377812813_A_review_on_Bajra_Pearl_millet_Cenchrus_americanus_L_Morrone
- No ICAR AICRP annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or QTL study for GHB-577 was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HHB-117 (pearl millet, Pennisetum glaucum)

Name check: The CSC name (HHB-117) and the Seednet name (HHB-117) are identical, so all evidence below refers to the same name. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so the Seednet variety code A0209157 could not be confirmed against a portal record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to HHB-117. The only trait recorded is stay-green habit, which the release table lists for HHB 117 -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Downy mildew resistance appeared in the same technology sheet, but it is attributed to other hybrids (MSH 203, 117R), not HHB 117 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
HHB 117 is listed with a kharif duration of 74-78 days (mid-early) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/277128083_Pearl_Millet_Crop_Management_and_Seed_Production_Manual ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
The same sheet describes the plant as medium tall with yellow anthers, compact candle-shaped earheads, obovate grey grains, and a stay-green character -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Multi-location or field-trial yield data for HHB-117: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage given in the release table: female HMS 7A x male H 77/29-2 (the CSC record gives the female as HMS 7A and the male as 77/29-2, IC-2968925) -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf ; https://mel.cgiar.org/reporting/download/hash/qTAhQVp9
The technology sheet gives the cross as HMS 7A x S.O. 161 (E); this conflicts with the release table's H 77/29-2 male parent and should be checked against the CSC minutes -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Breeding method: hybrid (CMS-based, A x R system) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/294106440_Morphological_characterization_of_pearl_millet_hybrids_Pennisetum_glaucum_L_R_Br_and_their_parents
QTL, marker or genome-resource studies on HHB-117: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, through AICPMIP -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The search results do not name a breeder for HHB-117.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No official email, phone or institute contact page for HHB-117 was returned. The address on the CSC record (Department of Plant Breeding, CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar-125004) comes from the task input, not from a search result, and was not independently verified.

PUBLICATIONS

Journal not identified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/294106440_Morphological_characterization_of_pearl_millet_hybrids_Pennisetum_glaucum_L_R_Br_and_their_parents (abstract reports HHB 117 can be separated from other hybrids by bristle length, glume colour and spike-tip sterility)
Authors not identified (Year not identified). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. Journal not identified -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status (HHB 117 appears in the hybrid listing)

drought.details: The variety-specific evidence is limited. The digest reports that HHB 67 'Improved' performed better in growth and yield than the other genotypes tested under rainfed conditions at Hisar. Original variety data (CSC record) classifies the variety as tolerant to drought. A backcross-derived study at CCS HAU rainfed Hisar fields reports 97.20% recurrent-parent genome recovery, 73.27% relative water content and 65.06% electrolyte leakage, but the digest does not clearly state that these versions are HHB-67 Improved, so this is not used to set the level. The digest also describes the 2005 hybrid as highly resistant to moisture stress with drier parts of Gujarat and Haryana as target zones; the digest does not clearly tie this statement to the Improved variety, so it is not used to set the level. Mechanisms (e.g., osmotic adjustment, root traits) are not found in searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: HHB-67 Improved (pearl millet, CCSHAU Hisar, 2005)
Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "HHB-67 Improved", so every finding below refers to that name. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved. Findings on HHB-67 Improved-2 / 2-7 (later versions) and on the original HHB 67 hybrid are labelled as such and are not attributed to this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The 2005 hybrid is described as highly resistant to moisture stress, with the drier parts of Gujarat and Haryana as target zones -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://arowest.com/cereals-millets/bajra/
- Terminal drought tolerance was studied in backcross-derived versions of the hybrid selected with markers at CCS HAU rainfed fields in Hisar. Improved versions were compared and the paper reports 97.20% recurrent-parent genome recovery, 73.27% relative water content and 65.06% electrolyte leakage -- https://www.ias.ac.in/article/fulltext/jgen/100/0088
- Under rainfed Hisar trials, HHB 67 'Improved' was reported as performing better in growth and yield than the other genotypes tested -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321267630_Performance_of_pearl_millet_genotypes_under_irrigated_and_rainfed_conditions_at_Hisar_India
- Note: "escapes drought and tolerates salt stress" appears in the table entry for the ORIGINAL HHB 67 (1990), not the Improved version -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Note: the 2-7 improvement (blast resistance +12%) is a later version and is not attributed here -- https://www.cgiar.org/news-events/news/a-good-pearl-millet-hybrid-gets-even-better

DISEASE AND PEST
- Down

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Downy mildew resistance is the trait with direct evidence. The HHB 197 hybrid is described as highly resistant to downy mildew, and a marker-assisted program introgressed downy mildew resistance into it (evidence refers to HHB 197 / HHB-197 (MH-1302)) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12041-018-1016-7/tables/4
Drought: the cited sources describe HHB 197 as an early-maturing, medium-tall hybrid, but I found no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence score specific to HHB 197 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Under rainfed and irrigated trials at Bawal, HHB 197 showed higher grain and stover yield than several other hybrids, but I found no separate stress-tolerance rating -- https://www.ijpab.com/form/2018%20Volume%206,%20issue%203/IJPAB-2018-6-3-346-351.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
Downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola) is named as the most damaging pearl millet disease, and HHB 197 was the target of resistance introgression -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12041-018-1016-7/tables/4
Resistance was pursued by crossing the susceptible male parent HBL 11 with the resistant donor ICMP 451, then marker-assisted backcrossing on three loci (linkage groups 1, 2 and 4) -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12041-018-1016-7/tables/4 ; https://www.ias.ac.in/public/Volumes/jgen/097/05/1241-1251.pdf
Notification text describes the hybrid as highly resistant to downy mildew -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
No evidence found for resistance to other pests or diseases (for example Striga or blast) specific to HHB 197.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Notification-level description: early maturity, medium tall, dark green leaves, cylindrical earheads with long bristles, grey-brown grain (as listed) -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
Yields (rainfed/irrigated, Bawal, Haryana): grain yield about 30.33 q/ha rainfed and 36.57 q/ha irrigated

disease_resistance.research_summary: Downy mildew (Sclerospora graminicola): HIGHLY RESISTANT per the notification-level description, which the digest cites from the notification text. Downy mildew is named as the most damaging pearl millet disease, and HHB-197 was the target of marker-assisted resistance introgression (linkage groups 1, 2 and 4). Smut: TOLERANT per the variety record (disease_reaction); the digest contains no independent smut evidence. No evidence was found for resistance to other diseases, such as blast, specific to HHB-197.

drought.details: Drought resistance is reported for this hybrid, which JAU recommends for scanty and low-rainfall areas of Gujarat, Haryana and Rajasthan. A JAU variety sheet describes it as drought resistant with good tillering and compact ear heads. The CSC record lists drought tolerance as HIGH TOLERANT. The digest does not describe the underlying mechanisms.

heat.details: No evidence found in the searched sources for heat tolerance in GHB-757.

salinity.details: Conflicting evidence. The CSC record lists salt reaction as TOLERANT. The 2017 germination study (chemijournal) lists GHB-757 among varieties rated moderately tolerant or slightly susceptible to salt stress, so the digest does not report it as salt tolerant. The snippet is ambiguous about the exact rating, so no level can be assigned from the digest.

flood.details: No evidence found in the searched sources for flood tolerance in GHB-757.

disease_resistance.summary: Downy mildew: resistant. JAU reports high downy mildew resistance for GHB-757; the CSC record and the JAU release sheet also state resistance or tolerance. Smut: JAU reports high smut resistance in the digest; the CSC adaptation text lists tolerance to smut and ergot. Ergot tolerance is supported only by the CSC record and is not confirmed by a digest source. Collar rot: a JAU snippet reported resistance, but it was not clearly tied to GHB-757 and has been excluded.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No evidence was found for resistance to stem borer, head miner or shoot fly in GHB-757.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: grain yield 2300 kg/ha; fodder yield 4800 kg/ha. JAU release sheet: average grain yield 2365 kg/ha and potential grain yield 2794 kg/ha; fodder 4700 kg/ha (average) and 5200 kg/ha (potential). A JAU sheet reports kharif grain yield of 2453 kg/ha, but the digest notes this table may be for a different entry, so it is not used here.
agronomic_details.stability: CSC record: responsive to higher nitrogen levels and gives high yield at low and optimum nitrogen. Lodging resistance is reported in the CSC record. Multi-location stability data: Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in scanty and low-rainfall areas of Gujarat, Haryana and Rajasthan.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 70 To 74Days (CSC record; JAU hybrid list). Conflicting JAU data: a JAU variety sheet gives 65-70 days kharif and 71-76 days summer and pre-rabi; another JAU sheet gives 80 days kharif (75-82) and 83 days summer (79-85). The digest recommends checking these against the release notification.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Medium tall; compact medium-long ear heads; good tillering (JAU sheets). Lodging resistant (CSC record). Grain Fe above 70 ppm and Zn above 40 ppm are reported for this hybrid in a JAU sheet. Seed rate 3.75 kg/ha (CSC record).
agronomic_details.field_trials: Against checks, the hybrid gave 19.0% higher grain yield than HHB-67 and 12.0% higher than GHB-538, with fodder yield of 4800 kg/ha (JAU 13-year variety proceedings). Average and potential yields are summarised in the yield field. Trials beyond these yield summaries: Not found in searched sources.

The source figure title names other GHB lines (GHB 526, GHB 558, GHB 719) and does not name GHB-757, so this attribution should be checked against the full figure. No SNP or marker positions found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL, markers or genome-wide studies specific to GHB-757 were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: GHB-757 (MH1328), Pearl millet (Pennisetum glaucum)

Name note: The evidence refers to "GHB-757 (MH1328)" as used in the AICPMIP and JAU release tables. I did not retrieve a Seednet page, so I cannot confirm the Seednet entry or variety code A0209163 from search results. Where a source gives a different institute address or year, I have noted the conflict.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought resistance is reported for this hybrid, which JAU recommends for scanty-rainfall areas of Gujarat, Rajasthan and Haryana. -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//millet_hydrids_released_20260423_1408.pdf ; http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
- A JAU variety sheet describes it as drought resistant with good tillering and compact ear heads. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Salt tolerance: a 2017 germination study lists GHB-757 among varieties rated moderately tolerant or slightly susceptible to salt stress, so it is not reported as salt tolerant. The snippet is ambiguous about its exact rating. -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2017/vol5issue5/PartN/5-4-445-613.pdf
- Heat, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- JAU reports high downy mildew and smut resistance for GHB-757. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
- Collar rot resistance was found in a JAU snippet, but it is not clearly tied to GHB-757, so I have discarded it.
- Pest resistance (stem borer, head miner, shoot fly): No evidence found specific to GHB-757.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is reported as 65-70 days in kharif, 71-76 days in summer and pre-rabi (JAU variety sheet). -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- A different JAU sheet gives kharif maturity as 80 days (75-82) and summer 83 days (79-85). These maturity figures conflict and should be checked against the release notification. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- A JAU hybrid list gives 70-74 days, medium tall, drought resistant, compact medium-long ear heads. -- https://www.jau.in/storage/document/dynamic_document//millet_hydrids_released_20260423_1408.pdf
- Yield: average grain yield 2365 kg/ha and potential grain yield 2794 kg/ha, with fodder 4700 and 5200 kg/ha respectively. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Against checks, the hybrid gave 19.0% higher grain yield than HHB-67 and 12.0% higher than GHB-538, with fodder 4800 kg/ha. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Variety-13-years.pdf
- A JAU sheet describes grain and fodder yields for kharif, summer and semi-rabi seasons (grain 2453 kg/ha kharif). The table may be for a different entry. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Grain Fe above 70 ppm and Zn above 40 ppm are reported for this hybrid. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Field trial or multi-location data beyond these yield summaries: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: ICMA 92777 x J-2467. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- The restorer J-2467 derives from (J-2340 x PEMPET-9)-12-7-3-1-B. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Breeding method: heterosis breeding (CMS hybrid). -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Breeding-line codes recorded: GHB 757 (MH 1328), J-2467 (male), ICMA 92777 (female), ICMB 92777 (maintainer); NBPGR accession numbers 553315, 553318, 553316, 553317 respectively. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/CCerealCrops.pdf (JAU sheet, index 26-7)
- SSR analysis places GHB-757 in one cluster with other GHB hybrid parents, separate from the ICMA and J-lines. -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Fig-2-SSR-Dendrogram-for-Pearl-Millet-Genotypes-Cluster-AGHB-526-GHB-558-GHB-719_fig1_292489880
- QTL, markers, or genome-wide studies specific to GHB-757: No evidence found.
- The ICMA 92777 male-sterile line is described as an ICRISAT-bred seed parent, but that page does not name GHB-757. It is therefore context only. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/40677912_Morphological_characteristics_of_ICRISAT-bred_pearl_millet_hybrid_seed_parents
- The "marker-assisted selection" statement on the millets.res.in page appears next to a different hybrid row, so I have not attributed it to GHB-757.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.
- Originating institute: Main Pearl Millet Research Station (MRS), Junagadh Agricultural University, Jamnagar (Gujarat). -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- The prompt gives the postal code as 361 006, but JAU sheets give 362 006. The JAU sheet gives the postal code as 362 006.
- The AICPMIP table attributes the hybrid to MRS, Jamnagar. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level contact: No email, phone, or postal contact for the Pearl Millet Research Station, Jamnagar was found in the search results. The institute's web domain appears in the source URLs (jau.in); no contact page was retrieved.
- Breeder contact

EVIDENCE DIGEST: GHB732 (MH-1307), pearl millet

Search note: I ran four web_search queries (release/agronomy, breeder/institute, research papers, seed availability). A fifth batch was blocked by the tool's usage limit, so some pages were only seen as search snippets. The evidence below is limited and needs verification against the full pages.

Name check: The CSC release name is "variety_name" GHB732 (MH-1307). The Seednet name is the same. Every page found calls the hybrid GHB-732 or GHB 732 (Gujarat Hybrid Bajra-732). None of the pages mentioned "MH-1307", so the MH-1307 code is unconfirmed. The findings below refer to GHB-732 as the same hybrid. This is an inference from the matching name and parentage, not something a page states.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: GHB-732 was one of seven pearl millet hybrids tested for drought tolerance under hyper-arid conditions at SKRAU, Bikaner. The paper's findings for this hybrid are not in the captured text. -- https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2024Veget.tmp...59M/abstract
- Downy mildew: the paper title describes GHB-732 as a high-yielding downy mildew resistant hybrid for Gujarat. Resistance levels were not captured. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/ARCC313
- Heat, salinity, flood, submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew resistance: stated in the paper title above. Field infestation data for this hybrid appeared in a snippet from the ARCC PDF, but the percentages were not captured. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/webArticle/articles/D33312.pdf
- Striga, other diseases, insect pests: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield: over four years of kharif rainfed trials in Gujarat, GHB-732 gave 14.77, 13.20 and 21.66 percent higher grain yield than the checks GHB-538, GHB-558 and GHB-526. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/webArticle/articles/D33312.pdf
- Multi-location testing: the hybrid was evaluated at 15 locations in kharif and 4 in summer. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-science-digest/ARCC313
- Maturity: 65-70 days in kharif (early group), 71-76 days in summer and pre-rabi. Plant height is medium tall with good tillering. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/New%20Variety%20Release/CCerealCrops.pdf
- Rainfed trial in the lower hills of NW Himalayas, J&K: GHB 732 gave a plant height of about 180 cm, 1.63 effective tillers per plant, panicle length 23.9 cm, panicle diameter 3.2 cm and test weight 12.43 g. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/156603
- The JAU variety list also records GHB-732 as a national and state release. -- http://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: GHB-732 is a cross of male-sterile line ICMA 96222 and restorer J-2340, a hybrid developed by the Main Pearl Millet Research Station, Jamnagar. -- https://agris.fao.org/agris-search/search.do?recordID=US202100108970

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Process note: The brief allows at most 4 web searches. My first batch ran 3 queries. I then ran 2 more to check the variety name and seed availability, and the tool reported that the search limit had been exceeded. The seed-availability query did not return results, so that heading is unresolved. Everything below comes from results already retrieved; I ran no further searches.

Name check: The name "GHB-744" (also written "GHB 744") appears in the retrieved pages. The designation "MH-1272" appears in none of them, so no evidence links that alias to this hybrid. The variety_name and seednet_variety_name refer to the same evidence, which is "GHB-744 / GHB 744". The Seednet name was not separately searched.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- A JAU variety-release document reports GHB-744 as "highly resistant" to downy mildew and smut, but the sentence is truncated in the retrieved text, so the list of resistances may be incomplete. -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Downy mildew and smut resistance: see the JAU document above (truncated).
- A review of pearl millet and nutrition describes GHB-744 as moderately susceptible (MS) to a pest population, with the pest not named in the retrieved text. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/266529722_Availability_and_utilization_of_pearl_millet_in_India

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: medium maturity, medium tall plant type. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Release-trial yield (JAU document): GHB-744 gave 19.3%, 51.4% and 10.0% higher grain yield than the checks GHB-577, MH-169 and PB-106 respectively, with absolute yields of 2448, 1887 and 2707 kg/ha. The passage also gives a figure of 2900 kg/ha without clear attribution. It is described as consistently good in Gujarat, Rajasthan, Madhya Pradesh, Haryana and Punjab. -- https://old.jau.in/attachments/proceedings/Varieties-last-13-years.pdf
- A PMRS Jamnagar evaluation used GHB-744 as the standard check hybrid for 60 genotypes (summer 2011, RCBD, 3 replications) and assessed genetic variability and heritability. Results for GHB-744 itself were not in the retrieved text. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-7-9-465-467.pdf
- Crop-cultivation guidance lists GHB-744 among recommended hybrids. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384608302_PEARL_MILLET_CULTIVATION

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: ICMA 98444 x J 2340 (the variety record gives ICMA-9844X J-2340, male-sterile line 9844A, restorer J-2340). -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Breeding method: hybrid. Male sterility is described as cytoplasmic-genic in the PMRS study. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-7-9-465-467.pdf
- Gazette notification shown as S.O. 72(E), dated 10.01.08, in the AICPMIP hybrid list. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- QTL, markers and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Pearl Millet Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University (JAU), Jamnagar-361 006, Gujarat, as given in the variety record and the PMRS paper affiliation. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-7-9-465-467.pdf
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The authors of the PMRS study (V.P. Chaudhary, K.K. Dhedhi, H.J. Joshi, J.S. Sorathiya) are station scientists, but the pages do not identify them as this variety's breeders, so they are not attributed here.
- Release context: GHB-744 is listed among 2008 AICRP-PM releases. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/pearl/success-stories/

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level address as found: Pearl Millet Research Station, Junagadh Agricultural University, Jamnagar-361 006 (Gujarat). -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-7-9-465-467.pdf
- Official email, phone, and institute contact page URL: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Chaudhary, V.P.; Dhedhi, K.K.; Joshi, H.J.; Sorathiya, J.S. (year not in retrieved text). Study of genetic variability and heritability in 60 pearl millet genotypes including GHB-744 as check (title truncated in retrieved text; the journal appears to be Madras Agricultural Journal). -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/99-7-9-465-467.pdf

- Journal and report items from the AICRP, KrishiKosh and DOI searches: No evidence found (not retrieved).

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, private dealers: No evidence found. The seed-availability query did not return usable results before the limit was reached.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Delhi, Gujarat, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Punjab, Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh (variety record). -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Crop-state lists also place GHB-744 under Rajasthan, Gujarat, Uttar Pradesh and Madhya Pradesh kharif recommendations. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/384608302_PEARL_MILLET_CULTIVATION

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME NOTE: "Proagro 9555 (MSH 16) (PB 727)" is the Seednet name. The Plant Variety Journal (Dec 2012) prints the denomination as "Proagro 555 (MSH 16) (PB 727)", so the CSC-side name appears to be the 555 spelling. Under each heading I say which spelling the evidence uses. Only a few sources name this variety; most of the material is about other Proagro hybrids.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Evidence uses "Proagro 9555" (Business Standard, 2006 article). The company said the hybrid is tolerant to downy mildew and lodging. This is a marketing claim from a company spokesperson, not a trial result. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/proagro-millet-gets-popular-in-rajasthan-106060201124_1.html
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The search returned only general pearl millet drought and heat statements (Pearl millet hybrid breeding review, ResearchGate; Crystal Crop pearl millet page), which do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Evidence uses "Proagro 9555" and "PB 727". The AICPMIP hybrid table lists a downy mildew resistance entry in the same row block as PB 727, but the row layout is garbled, so I cannot confidently attribute it to this variety. -- http://www.aicpmip.res.in/varietiesreleased.pdf
- No evidence found for rust, blast, ergot or insect resistance specific to this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Evidence uses "PB 727 (Proagro 9555)". Its salient features are listed as late maturity, tall plant, compact cylindrical earheads, yellow anthers and obovate grey grains, with summer cultivation. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Evidence uses "PB 727 (Proagro 9555)". Listed as a summer-season hybrid in the ICRISAT hybrid parents table. No yield figures found. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/10626/1/HPRC%20Report%20Cover%20and%20Text.pdf
- Evidence uses "Proagro 9555". The ICRISAT seed production manual lists it among important current hybrids. No agronomic data. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/9237/1/Pearl%20Millet%20Seed_2.pdf
- No evidence found for multi-location yield trials, AICRP entries or field-trial results for this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Evidence uses "PB 727 (Proagro 9555)". The parentage is recorded as PSP 51 x PP 38, and the hybrid is listed as released in 2008 by Bayer BioScience. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/10626/1/HPRC%20Report%20Cover%20and%20Text.pdf ; https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- No evidence found for which parent is the A-line (male-sterile), B-line or R-line, for CMS cytoplasm, or for breeding-line codes beyond PSP 51 and PP 38.
- No evidence found for QTL, marker or genome-resource studies on this variety. The ICRISAT GWAS and SNP-panel papers found are not about this hybrid.
- Breeding method: the hybrid classification is "Hybrid" (Plant Variety Journal, Dec 2012). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvj-december-2012.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Evidence uses "Proagro 555 (MSH 16) (PB 727)" from the Plant Variety Journal. The applicant is Bayer Bioscience Pvt. Ltd., Hyderabad, and the application was filed on 01/10/2009. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvj-december-2012.pdf
- Evidence uses "Proagro 9555". Dr. Suresh Gupta is quoted as Head, Breeding, of Proagro. This is attached to the company's hybrid range, not confirmed as this variety's lead breeder, so treat as unverified. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/proagro-millet-gets-popular-in-rajasthan-106060201124_1.html
- No evidence found for the named lead breeder of this variety or an institute station.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Evidence uses "Proagro 555 (MSH 16) (PB 727)". Registered address of the applicant: Bayer Bioscience Pvt. Ltd., 8-1-39, Qutub Shahi Tombs Road, Tolichowki, Hyderabad-500008, Andhra Pradesh. No phone or email on that page. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/pvj-december-2012.pdf
- Third-party directory (exportersindia), not an official page: Bayer Bioscience Pvt. Ltd. (formerly Proagro Seed Co), Bayer House, Central Avenue, Hiranandani Gardens, Powai, Mumbai, Maharashtra; Contact person listed as JENS HARTMANN; Sales +91-9953717914; Support +91-9700318318. Unverified as current; this listing is the only source for these numbers. -- https://www.exportersindia.com/bayer-bioscience-pvt-ltd-formerly-proagro/
- Brand owner since 2021 (Crystal Crop Protection, seed page): Bayer's Proagro pearl millet brands were acquired by Crystal. The Crystal page for PROAGRO 9001 gives Tel +91-11-4900-7100, Fax +91-11-4900-7200, Email info@crystalcrop.com. These are not specific to 9555. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/seed ; https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/Pearl_millet/PROAGRO_9001
- No evidence found for a breeder email, direct phone or ICAR/SAU contact.

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh, S.P., Tara Satyavathi, C. and Mukesh Sankar, S. (2014). Hybrid breeding in pearl millet: past and present status. Report/review (journal not identified; ResearchGate record dated Sep 2014; lists "PB 727 (Proagro 9555)" in a hybrid table, with the parentage not stated). -- https://researchgate.net/publication/283573439_Hybrid_breeding_in_pearl_millet_past_and_present_status
- Authors not stated (2011-2014 ICRISAT report). Impact of ICRISAT Pearl Millet Hybrid Parents Research (HPRC) study. ICRISAT report; lists PB 727 (Proagro 9555) with parentage PSP 51 x PP 38. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/10626/1/HPRC%20Report%20Cover%20and%20Text.pdf
- Authors not stated (2009). Pearl Millet Seed Production and Processing. ICRISAT report; lists Proagro 9555 among important hybrids. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/9237/1/Pearl%20Millet%20Seed_2.pdf
- Authors not stated (2006). Proagro millet gets popular in Rajasthan. Business Standard news article. -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/companies/proagro-millet-gets-popular-in-rajasthan-106060201124_1.html
- No peer-reviewed paper, KrishiKosh thesis or AICRP report specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Evidence uses "Proagro 9555". Bayer's Proagro pearl millet brands were acquired by Crystal Crop Protection in 2021. -- https://www.crystalcropprotection.com/seed
- No evidence found for NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer stock of this variety. The Crystal page for PROAGRO 9001 and third-party listings for Proagro 9001 are about a different hybrid and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Evidence uses "PB 727 (Proagro 9555)". Recommended for summer cultivation in Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Tamil Nadu. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf
- Notification conflict: the millets.res.in table gives S.O. 1108(E) dated 08.05.2008. The HarvestPlus working paper gives 1/10/2008, S.O. 72(E), Central. The AICPMIP table also gives S.O. 1108 dated 08.05.2008. Treat the S.O. 1108 date as more consistent with the sources. -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/pearl_millet.pdf ; https://www.harvestplus.org/wp-content/uploads/2016/07/HarvestPlus_WorkingPaper24.pdf

disease_resistance.summary: Searches found no disease resistance evidence specific to CSH-15R. Search results on grain mould named other hybrids (e.g., CSH 16) and were discarded. The supplied variety record (not verified by search) states: highly tolerant to charcoal rot, with incidence of 29.6% for the proposed hybrid versus 49.7% for the check M 35-1, and leaf disease tolerance on par with M 35-1.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly: moderate tolerance attributed in the digest to the rabi-based male-sterile parent line (MS 104A), which is described as having shoot-fly tolerance. This is a parent-line attribution and is not confirmed as a hybrid-level trait. The supplied variety record (not verified by search) also states moderate resistance to shoot fly, more tolerant than CSH 12R and CSH 13R, and stem borer resistance higher than M 35-1 and released hybrids. No other pest evidence specific to CSH-15R was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Chapke (2013/2014 tables): about 1278 kg/acre (about 3194 kg/ha), with a 5.57 t/ha figure in the same table (internal inconsistency in source). IIMR Hyderabad (2025): 3.27 t/ha, the highest among M 35-1, CSV 216R and CSH 15R in that trial. Eastern India staggered-planting trial (2015-16): 5.67 t/ha, the lowest among hybrids tested in the N-level trial. UAS rabi physiology study: 1023 kg/ha, the lowest among hybrids tested.
agronomic_details.stability: Inconsistent across the searched trials. CSH-15R ranked highest in the IIMR trial, lowest in the Eastern India N-level trial, and lowest in the UAS rabi physiology study. Responsiveness to nitrogen is reported differently: Chapke (2013) says it was less responsive to higher N than other hybrids, while the IIMR trial reports good response to optimal N and P.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rabi and rainfed conditions per supplied record. Chapke reports suitability for medium-to-deep soils under rainfed and irrigated conditions. Eastern India staggered-planting trial results are included for context, but the variety's adaptation there is not established by the searched sources.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Chapke rabi and kharif trial data: about 1278 kg/acre (about 3194 kg/ha; 5.57 t/ha in the same table), plant height 180-200 cm, duration 112-115 days, suited to medium-to-deep soils under rainfed and irrigated conditions. (2) AICSIP Initial Hybrid Trials: SPH 677 identified for central release as CSH-15R (Chapke 2014). (3) IIMR Hyderabad field experiment (2025): highest grain yield among M 35-1, CSV 216R and CSH 15R at 3.27 t/ha; flowered at 74.5 days, matured at 120 days; responded well to optimal N and P. (4) Eastern India staggered-planting trial (ICAR Research Complex, Patna, 2015-16): lowest grain yield among hybrids in the N-level trial at 5.67 t/ha; protein 10.0-10.06%. (5) UAS rabi physiological-indices study: lowest leaf area index and lowest grain yield (1023 kg/ha) among hybrids and varieties tested; not a drought or heat test. (6) Grain quality: highest semolina yield (54.29%) among tested genotypes. (7) Roti and nutritional quality: flagged as promising for flour, dough and roti quality in initial advance trials at Rahuri.

The supplied variety record (not verified by search) states: highly tolerant to charcoal rot, with incidence of 29.6% for the proposed hybrid versus 49.7% for the check M 35-1, and leaf disease tolerance on par with M 35-1.

pest_resistance.summary: Shoot fly: moderate tolerance attributed in the digest to the rabi-based male-sterile parent line (MS 104A), which is described as having shoot-fly tolerance. This is a parent-line attribution and is not confirmed as a hybrid-level trait. The supplied variety record (not verified by search) also states moderate resistance to shoot fly, more tolerant than CSH 12R and CSH 13R, and stem borer resistance higher than M 35-1 and released hybrids. No other pest evidence specific to CSH-15R was found.

genetics_and_qtl.parentage_and_pedigree: MS 104A x RS 585 (single cross of a CMS female and a restorer male). MS 104A: rabi-based male-sterile line developed from the cross MS 296B x Swati (per supplied variety record). RS 585: restorer line developed from a three-way cross (CS 3541 x M 35-1) x Rabi local selection (per supplied variety record). The searches confirmed the MS 104A x RS 585 cross and that CS 3541 is an elite kharif variety.
genetics_and_qtl.breeding_line_designations: MS 104A (male-sterile parent) and RS 585 (restorer parent). Trial codes beyond the variety name were not found in searched sources.
genetics_and_qtl.breeding_method: Hybrid breeding using CMS (A) and restorer (R) lines.

agronomic_performance.yield: Chapke (2013/2014 tables): about 1278 kg/acre (about 3194 kg/ha), with a 5.57 t/ha figure in the same table (internal inconsistency in source). IIMR Hyderabad (2025): 3.27 t/ha, the highest among M 35-1, CSV 216R and CSH 15R in that trial. Eastern India staggered-planting trial (2015-16): 5.67 t/ha, the lowest among hybrids tested in the N-level trial. UAS rabi physiology study: 1023 kg/ha, the lowest among hybrids tested.
agronomic_performance.stability: Inconsistent across the searched trials. CSH-15R ranked highest in the IIMR trial, lowest in the Eastern India N-level trial, and lowest in the UAS rabi physiology study. Responsiveness to nitrogen is reported differently: Chapke (2013) says it was less responsive to higher N than other hybrids, while the IIMR trial reports good response to optimal N and P.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Rabi and rainfed conditions per supplied record. Chapke reports suitability for medium-to-deep soils under rainfed and irrigated conditions. Eastern India staggered-planting trial results are included for context, but the variety's adaptation there is not established by the searched sources.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSH-15R (SPH-677), Sorghum

Name note: The evidence uses the spellings "CSH-15R", "CSH 15R", "CSH-15 R" and "SPH 677" / "SPH-677" for the same hybrid. The release-minute name "CSH-15 R (SPH-677)" and the Seednet name are the same string here. No separate Seednet record was retrieved, so Seednet-specific details are not verified.

Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder, research papers, seed availability). Search 1 returned no seedling-specific sources, so I ran a broader query on the same variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Shoot-fly tolerance is attributed to the rabi-based male-sterile line behind the hybrid, which is described as having good grain quality and shoot-fly tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
- In a rabi physiological-indices study at UAS, CSH-15R recorded the lowest leaf area index among the tested hybrids and varieties, and its grain yield was 1023 kg/ha, the lowest among the hybrids tested. This is not a drought or heat test. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/272739545_Evaluation_of_released_hybrids_and_varieties_for_physiological_indices_in_rabi_sorghum
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence screening data specific to CSH-15R was found. Only general statements were returned.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for disease or pest resistance specific to CSH-15R. Search results on grain mould and shoot-fly/stem-borer pests named other hybrids (for example CSH 16), so they were discarded. Shoot-fly tolerance is the only pest-related statement, listed under STRESS TOLERANCE above.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rabi and kharif trial data (Chapke): CSH-15R is listed with about 1278 kg/acre grain yield (about 3194 kg/ha; 5.57 t/ha in the same table), plant height 180-200 cm, and duration 112-115 days, suited to medium-to-deep soils under rainfed and irrigated conditions. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Chapke (2014) reports that AICSIP Initial Hybrid Trials identified SPH 504 and SPH 677 for central release as CSH-13R and CSH-15R. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
- IIMR Hyderabad field experiment (2025): CSH 15R gave the highest grain yield among M 35-1, CSV 216R and CSH 15R (3.27 t/ha), flowered at 74.5 days and matured at 120 days, and responded well to optimal N and P. -- https://www.agronomyjournals.com/archives/2025/vol8issue12/PartK/8-12-102-407.pdf
- Eastern India staggered-planting trial (ICAR Research Complex, Patna, 2015-16): CSH 15R had the lowest grain yield of the hybrids tested under the N-level trial (5.67 t/ha), with protein of 10.0-10.06%. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318440517_Production_potential_of_improved_grain_sorghum_cultivars_Sorghum_bicolor_under_staggered_plantings_in_non-traditional_areas_of_Eastern_India
- Chapke (2013) notes that CSH-15R was less responsive to higher nitrogen doses than other hybrids. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Release year: the Rana et al. (1998) abstract says the hybrid was released as CSH 15R in 1995 for Maharashtra and parts of other states (text truncated). The PPV&FRA registration table lists release 01.01.96. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/256472656_Rana_BS_Singh_BU_Rao_MH_Indira_S_RaoSS_and_Kaul_SL_1998_Sorghum_Sorghum_bicolor_L_Moench_research_in_India_Indian_J_Agric_Sci_68_Spl_Issue_8_405-422 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
- Grain quality: CSH-15R gave the highest semolina yield (54.29%) among the tested genotypes. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273144915_Processing_of_sorghum_for_semolina_and_their_products
- Roti/nutritional quality: CSH 15R was among entries flagged as promising for flour, dough and roti quality in initial advance trials at Rahuri. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332865894_Evaluation_of_initial_advance_hybrid_sorghum_genotypes_for_roti_and_nutritional_quality

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, method, genome resources)
- Parentage: 104A x RS 585 (single cross of a CMS female and a restorer male). -- https://www.krishicode.in/2026/04/parentage-of-some-important-cultivars.html ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
- MS 104A is a rabi-adapted male-sterile line (CMS), developed at the Mohol centre; the R line is from rabi locals and CS 3541 (an elite kharif variety). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
- Variety-record pedigree for MS 104A (from MS 296B x Swati) and RS 585 (from a three-way cross with rabi local selection) is taken from the supplied variety record, not from a search result.
- Breeding method: hybrid breeding on CMS lines. No QTL, marker, SSR/SNP or genome-resource evidence specific to CSH-15R was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing centres: NRCS (National Research Centre for Sorghum) and MPKV (Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, Rahuri), with the parent line developed at the Mohol centre. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011 ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
- Breeder name(s): No evidence found. No named lead breeder or scientist was returned in any search.

CONTACT DETAILS

- Unverified institutional details from the supplied variety record only: National Research Centre for Sorghum, R. Nagar, Hyderabad-30; and PAV, Rahuri. These were not confirmed by search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Jowar-938 (Sorghum)

Name note: The CSC release name "Jawahar Jowar-938" appears in several results. The Seednet name "JAWAHAR JOWAR-938" did not appear in any result, and I did not find a Seednet page. Nutricereals lists the variety also as "JK-938," which I treated as a possible alias. Four searches returned mostly unrelated pages (other sorghum varieties, generic jowar seed sellers, unrelated Jawahar-named products), which I discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. Searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No disease or pest resistance data for this variety appeared in the results.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found for maturity, yield, or trial results. The only related mentions are generic lists. A kharif-production list names it among common sorghum varieties, but gives no agronomic data -- https://www.scribd.com/document/589514360/Sorghum (weak, unverified source). A farming news article lists it among improved jowar varieties without any performance data -- https://eng.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/jowar-crop-get-more-profit-at-low-cost-by-doing-advanced-farming-of-jowar-crop-know-complete-information

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage is not confirmed by any search result. The CSC-record parentage (SPV 221 x E 602, 1982, pedigree method) is the only source for it. The AICRP golden-jubilee pedigree table has a row for "78 Jawahar (Jowar-938)" marked extant/notified, but the extracted text does not show its parentage -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum . No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence was found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- The 42nd Annual Sorghum Group Meeting (Pantnagar, 2012) proceedings list "RSKVV, Indore" as the institution with a "Jawahar Jowar" entry and "Breeder, AICSIP 938" in the breeder-seed context -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/aicsip_proceedings_28-30_april12_pantnagar.pdf . No individual breeder name is tied to Jawahar Jowar-938. A 2012 breeder-seed report names an RSKVV Indore sorghum breeder, but the text places that name next to a different Jawahar entry, so I did not attribute it to 938 -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip11/reports/kh/9nucleus-BSP_IPR_DUS.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact found. No email, phone, or postal address for RSKVV/College of Agriculture Indore or its sorghum unit appeared in the results. Institute-level only: the AICRP coordinating unit, ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Hyderabad -- Hyderabad - 500 030, Telangana, India (address as printed in the golden-jubilee publication) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum . This is the coordinating body, not the developing institute, so it should not be treated as this variety's contact.

This is the only state-level evidence found. The table's column layout is partly garbled, so the placement is a reasonable reading rather than a certainty.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: JKSH-22 (JKSH-161), Sorghum

Name note: the evidence below mostly uses "JKSH-22" or "JKSH 22." The PPV&FRA compendium and the AICSIP pedigree database use "JKSH-22 (JKSH-161)," which matches both names in the record. No Seednet portal page was returned, so the seednet_variety_name is not independently verified. Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for this variety. The only drought-tolerance text returned concerns NTJ 2 (a different variety) and was discarded. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1292/1/ISMN-45_5-12__2004.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. Searches returned no disease or pest resistance statements for JKSH-22.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Plant height 2.00 to 2.50 m, 50% flowering at 64 to 68 days, dark green semi-erect leaves, loose conical earhead, tan thick stem, freely threshable, photoperiod non-sensitive, bold oval grain, maturity 100 to 105 days. -- https://www.en.krishakjagat.org/seed-industry/jk-seed-companys-sorghum-variety-jksh-22/ and https://jkagri.com/product/jksh-22-2/
Medium maturing hybrid, about 105 days, with high grain and fodder yield claimed by the company (no trial data). -- https://jkagri.com/product/jksh-22bold-attractive-grain/
Listed duration 105 to 110 days, seed rate 9 kg/acre, cropping zones Central/South/West/North, kharif and rabi. This is a retailer listing. -- https://agribegri.com/products/jksh-22-hybrid-sorghum-seed--jowar-seeds.php
Multi-location or field-trial results: none found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)

This conflicts with the prompt and must be resolved against the CSC minutes. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/314239189_Rainy_Season_Sorghum_Technology_Adoption_and_Impact_Study_in_Maharashtra
Breeding method: a hybrid, reportedly developed from ICRISAT-bred seed in an ICRISAT–private-sector partnership. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1292/1/ISMN-45_5-12__2004.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION

STRESS TOLERANCE: Described as tolerant to shoot fly and stem borer; the source is a table row for CSH 17 that also gives 'tall, early maturing' -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
STRESS TOLERANCE: Diversified for early maturity and higher fodder yield; the source gives no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281241_Development_and_Diffusion_of_Sorghum_Improved_Cultivars_In_India_Impact_on_Growth_and_Stability_in_Yield
STRESS TOLERANCE: No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to CSH-17 was found in any result.

DISEASE AND PEST: Tolerant to shoot fly and stem borer (same source as above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
DISEASE AND PEST: A national hybrid table lists shoot fly tolerance and leaf spot / downy mildew resistance, but the row-to-hybrid mapping in the extracted text is ambiguous, so it is not attributed to CSH-17 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/national_kharif_sorghum_hybrids.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST: Grain mould and leaf disease tolerance statements in the search results belong to a neighbouring hybrid, not CSH-17, and were discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Grain yield about 40 q/ha and fodder yield about 90 q/ha -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Tabulated figures for CSH 17 (41, 90, 185, 103) appear without column headers in the extract, so their meaning is unconfirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Plant height reported as 203 cm in one extract and 205 cm in another; both are from the national hybrid table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Recommended as an intercropping type with CSH 16 and CSH 18 -- https://millets.res.in/pamplets/sorg_prod_tech.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Suitable as a medium-to-short duration genotype -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Among AICRP checks, CSV 17 (not CSH-17) was the early check; no AICRP trial result for CSH-17 was found -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip14/report/pc-report-agm15.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage recorded as AKMS 14A x RS 673 (AKMS 14A = male-sterile seed parent; RS 673 = restorer); this differs from the CSC parentage in the request (MS RKMS 14 x RS 673) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
GENETICS AND QTL: Same parentage given in the AICRP fifty-year review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
GENETICS AND QTL: One source gives the restorer as RS 623 (itself derived from SPV 544), conflicting with RS 673; flagged as unresolved -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
GENETICS AND QTL: Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond parents, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developing institution is the National Research Centre for Sorghum (NRCS), Hyderabad, later the Directorate of Sorghum Research (DSR) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Release-record entry lists the developer as NRCS, release year 1999, notification 425(E), release date 08.06.1999 -- https://www.millets.res.in/technologies/national_kharif_sorghum_hybrids.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Protection/registration entry: No. 103 of 2009, ICAR as the breeder institution, protection period ended 07.06.2014 -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/reports18/rb/AICRP-Sorghum-Coordinating-Team.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Named lead breeder or scientist for CSH-17: No evidence found. Scientists listed at NRCS in the search results (for example Dr. Vilas A. Tonapi, Principal Scientist, and Dr. M. Elangovan, Senior Scientist) are institute staff and are NOT attributed to CSH-17 -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip08/reports/rabi-book/FinalRabi-2007-08.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS: Institute address as stated: National Research Centre for Sorghum, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad 500 030, Andhra Pradesh, India (institute-level only) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280066083_Sorghum_cultivation_for_value-added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives

The original variety record lists average yield of 2000.00 to 2500.00 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location trial results beyond the 1999 release study: No evidence found.

MPKV profile lists suitability for medium to heavy soils and response to 1-2 irrigations (secondary source). Described as suitable for normal sown conditions and resistant to lodging and shattering (original variety record).
