CSV-216 (Phule Yashoda, SPV-1359) -- EVIDENCE DIGEST
Searches run: 4 (variety/traits; breeder/institution; research/publications; seed availability).
Name note: the CSC release minutes name is "CSV 216 (Phule Yashoda)(SPV-1359)". The Seednet name "CSV-216 (PHULE YASHODA, SPV-1359)" was not retrieved from the Seednet portal itself. Most AICRP reports call it "CSV 216R" or "CSV-216R". All evidence below was matched to this variety by these names. The variety code A0210032 did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE [name matched: CSV 216R / Phule Yashoda / SPV 1359]
Released from a Rahuri landrace selection with reported high tolerance to shoot fly and charcoal rot (figures given as 18.1% and 20.0%) -- https://eurekamag.com/research/011/147/011147746.php
Described as tolerant to shoot fly, charcoal rot, drought and non-lodging in a figure caption for CSV 216R (Phule Yashoda) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
Reported as less damaged by shoot fly and stem borers than several other varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
Drought tolerance is named here only in the same figure caption; no separate drought trial was found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST [name matched: CSV 216R / Phule Yashoda]
Shoot fly and charcoal rot tolerance (see above) -- https://eurekamag.com/research/011/147/011147746.php
Used as a reference or check entry in AICRP pest and pathology trials (entomology and pathology sections of the 2016 report) -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip16/reports16/AICRP_Coordinating_Team.pdf
Used as a reference entry in AICRP rabi and kharif trials, with a 2017 report noting it was not significantly different in a trial -- https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/reports/rb/AICRP_Sorghum_Coordinating_Team_report.pdf
Grain mould, pokkah boeng, stem borer resistance specific to this variety: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS [name matched: CSV 216R / Phule Yashoda / SPV 1359]
Rabi-season, midlate (120-125 days), tall (240-270 cm), medium-bold (about 31 g per 1000 grains), round, pearly-white grain -- https://eurekamag.com/research/011/147/011147746.php

Multi-location trial results beyond the 1999 release study: No evidence found.

agronomic_details.adaptation: The supplied CSC record states the variety is recommended for all forage sorghum growing tracts as an early type, with forage yield and quality best expressed in Rajasthan, Maharashtra, Delhi and Gujarat. It is suitable for early or late planting and for both systems, and is a lodging-non-lodging type. The Udaipur district contingency plan lists the variety among recommended fodder sorghum varieties for change of cropping system and sorghum-plus-cowpea fodder systems. The Rajasthan advisory PDF recommends it for rabi use of residual soil moisture after bhakhar planking.

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Udaipur district contingency plan: lists the variety among recommended fodder sorghum varieties for change of cropping system and sorghum-plus-cowpea fodder systems; no yield data reported. (2) Rajasthan crop advisory PDF: recommends the variety for rabi use of residual soil moisture after bhakhar planking; no trial data reported. (3) Udaipur agronomy department study under nitrogen levels: compared SU-1 with Rajasthan Chari-1 and Rajasthan Chari-2, with Rajasthan Chari-2 as the comparator. SU-1 gave higher plant height, leaves, stem thickness and green and dry fodder yields than Rajasthan Chari-2. The Udaipur district contingency plan lists the variety among recommended fodder sorghum varieties for change of cropping system and sorghum-plus-cowpea fodder systems. agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) Udaipur district contingency plan: lists the variety among recommended fodder sorghum varieties for change of cropping system and sorghum-plus-cowpea fodder systems; no yield data reported. SU-1 gave higher plant height, leaves, stem thickness and green and dry fodder yields than Rajasthan Chari-2. RAJASTHAN CHARI-2 (SU-45) SORGHUM: EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name note: the web sources use "Rajasthan Chari 2 (SU 45)", which matches variety_name. No page using the SeedNet name "RAJASTHAN CHARI-2 (SU-45)" was found, so the evidence below refers to variety_name. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Stem borer resistance, high digestibility and green fodder yield of about 33 t/ha are given for "Raj chari-2" in a sorghum production slide deck (variety_name). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sorghum-255075081/255075081
No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence specific to this variety was found. -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistance to stem borer is stated for "Raj chari-2" in the same slide deck (variety_name). -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/sorghum-255075081/255075081
The supplied release record also states stem borer resistance (supplied record text, no URL).
No foliar disease, shoot fly or other pest data specific to this variety was found. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
The Udaipur district contingency plan lists Rajasthan Chari-2 among recommended fodder sorghum varieties for change of cropping system and for sorghum-plus-cowpea fodder systems (variety_name). -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/Rajastan/MPUA&T,%20Udaipur/RAJ22-Udaipur-9.3.2012.pdf

Supplied record: 65-75 days to flowering, 220-260 cm height, long broad leaves, good leaf-stem ratio (supplied record text, no URL).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Nandyala Tella Jonna-2 (CSC name: Nandyala Tella Jonna-2; Seednet name: NANDYALA TELLA JONNA-2). Both names refer to the same entry. Evidence was found for the Seednet-style name only in one AICSIP pedigree compilation. Searches used: 4.

NOTE ON "NTJ-2": Several AICRP Nandyal reports name "NTJ-2" as a check or major farmers' variety. It is probably an abbreviation of this variety, but no page spells it out. These items are listed below as UNCONFIRMED and are not counted as evidence for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for drought, heat, salinity, flood, submergence or stress tolerance returned nothing that names this variety. A Nandyal AICRP centre slide lists fall army worm tolerance as a priority area for the centre in general, not for this variety. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/presentations/Centre_Presentations/11Nandyal.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for this variety. The only related material is a general statement that a different Nandyal variety (NTJ-5) is tolerant to disease. NTJ-5 is a different variety and is excluded. -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/article/view/569/7-3-122

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
UNCONFIRMED (NTJ-2 abbreviation): Nandyal AICRP reports used NTJ-2 as the local check in Initial Advanced Varietal Trial and Advanced Yield Trial entries, where some entries had grain yields of about 2,993 to 4,104 kg/ha and were on par with the check. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/reports19/Rabi/1-Breeding-Rabi.pdf and https://www.millets.res.in/aicsip17/presentations/Centre_Presentations/10Nandyal.pdf
UNCONFIRMED (NTJ-2 abbreviation): An ICAR-IIMR breeding report says NTJ-2 was developed for food and fodder and is used by ICRISAT as an international check in sweet sorghum trials. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/reports19/Rabi/1-Breeding-Rabi.pdf
Phenology or yield data for Nandyala Tella Jonna-2 itself: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Breeding-line code: The AICSIP pedigree database lists "NANDYALA TELLA JONNA-2" with code 639(E) and date 17.08.90, and "GFS-4" appears on the same row. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011 and https://www.academia.edu/58781371/Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_2011_
Parentage: The supplied record gives a pure line selection from E-1966 (an Ethiopian line, tested as NJ-2122). No search result confirmed this parentage. The supplied parentage is not verified.
Breeding method: Pure line selection is stated in the supplied record only; not confirmed by search.
QTL/markers and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing station: RARS Nandyal, Andhra Pradesh, per the supplied record. The search did not confirm the station from an independent source.
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The Nandyal AICRP in-charge name is truncated in the retrieved slide ("Dr." only), so it cannot be attributed.
Institutional context: The Nandyal sorghum breeding programme is reported under ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (AICRP on Sorghum, Hyderabad). -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip19/Sorghum/reports19/Rabi/1-Breeding-Rabi.pdf
Excluded: The Wikipedia page on N.G.P. Rao concerns hybrid sorghum and CSH varieties. It is not about this variety and is not attributed.

CONTACT DETAILS
No variety-specific or breeder contact found.
Institute-level contact (not tied to this variety): Aruna C, Principal Scientist and PI (Kharif Sorghum Breeding), ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad - 500 030, email aruna@millets.res.in. Director and Project Coordinator, AICRP-Sorghum, ICAR-IIMR, Hyderabad - 500 030, Telangana. -- https://www.millets.res.in/pub/2020/GoldenJubileePublication_50Years_of_Publication.pdf
Phone and RARS Nandyal postal address: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not shown (year not stated in the retrieved snippet). Pedigree database on Sorghum Elite Breeding Stock (AICSIP: 2006-2011). ICAR-Indian Institute of Millets Research (former Directorate of Sorghum Research) compilation; this lists Nandyala Tella Jonna-2 as entry 639(E) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011 (DOI not found)
No peer-reviewed paper, thesis or KrishiKosh record for this variety was found. The On-farm NTJ-5 paper (Jayalakshmi et al., 2024, Int J Agric Extension Social Dev 7(4):520-523, DOI 10.33545/26180723.2024.v7.i4g.569) concerns NTJ-5 and is excluded. -- https://www.extensionjournal.com/archives/2024.v7.i4.G.569
A 1989 paper on Nandyala Tella Jonna-1 (NJ2092) is a different variety and is excluded. -- https://eurekamag.com/research/002/006/002006426.php

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. Results were consumer retail listings for generic "Tella Jonna" or white cholam grain, which are not this variety and are excluded. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale record was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The supplied record gives "Unknown". Searches did not find a notification or state recommendation for this variety. The released varieties Nandyala Tella Jonna 5 (NJ 2647) and Nandyala Pacha Jonna 15 (NJ 2446) were released in 2018 by a Andhra Pradesh state variety release committee, but these are different varieties and are excluded. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip18/presentations/Centre_Presentations/11Nandyal.pdf

RELEASE RECORD (for reference)
Year of release 1990 and CSC/Seednet code A0210123 are from the supplied record. No independent notification gazette or CSC minute was found in the searches.

agronomic_details.yield: Digest figures (sweet sorghum context, varying measures): AICSIP trials cane yield potential about 38 t/ha; Tata Chemicals distillery pilot average stalk productivity 24.75 t/ha; New Delhi 2009-2010 grain-equivalent yield 11.35 t/ha; 2024 sub-tropical study ethanol yield about 2780 L/ha. CSC record average yield: 1750 kg/ha (ground truth; the CSC record marks the average yield field as Unknown in the original data, while the adaptation text gives 1750 kg/ha).
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Performance was reported across several sites and seasons, but no stability analysis (e.g., GxE) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for release and cultivation under assured irrigation in the kharif season in Maharashtra, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Rajasthan and Gujarat. Photo-sensitive. Sowing within June is recommended (CSC). A Hyderabad planting-date study recommended early June to early July sowing. Lodging risk under rain and high wind during harvest (CSC).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: THRESHABILITY (%) : 100%; AWNED OR AWNLESS : AWNLESS; SEED WEIGHT : 4.5 G/100 SEEDS; SEED SIZE : BOLD; SEED SHAPE : ROUND; SEED COLOUR : CREAMY; GRAIN LUSTER : NON-LUSTROUS. Also per CSC: non-shattering, responds to fertilizer, may lodge under rain and high wind at harvest. The digest describes maturity as late for a sweet sorghum variety, but no days-to-maturity figure specific to this hybrid was found in the digest sources.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) 2008-09 Hyderabad planting-date study: CSH 22SS produced significantly more stalk, grain, sugar and ethanol yield than SSV 84 and SSV 74; early June to early July sowing recommended. (2) AICSIP agronomy report: highest cane yield potential (about 38 t/ha) among sweet sorghum trials listed; brix about 15.3%. (3) New Delhi trial, 2009-2010 rainy seasons: 11.35 t/ha grain-equivalent yield for CSH 22SS versus 6.15 t/ha for SSV 84 and 8.53 t/ha for RSSV 9. (4) 2024 sub-tropical biofuel study: ranked third on stalk yield among tested sweet sorghums; ethanol yield about 2780 L/ha. (5) Tata Chemicals distillery pilot: average stalk productivity 24.75 t/ha.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: CSH-22SS(NSSH-104), Sorghum

Name note: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "CSH-22SS(NSSH-104)". The sources use spacing variants such as "CSH 22SS (NSSH 104)" and "CSH-22SS (NSSH-104)", and one source writes "CSH 23 (NSSH 104)". All of these refer to the same hybrid. The Seednet portal itself was not returned by any search, so variety code A0210179 is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this hybrid. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259704440_Developing_a_Sweet_sorghum_Ethanol_Value_Chain (search returned sweet sorghum yield and ethanol papers only)

DISEASE AND PEST
No reliable evidence found. One fragmentary table in a review reads like leaf-disease resistance beside the CSH 22SS row, but the text does not clearly attach it to this hybrid. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288493473_Sweet_sorghum_for_biofuel_and_strategies_for_its_improvement
Pest-resistance statements in the same sources (shoot fly, stem borer, leaf diseases) concern ICSV 93046, not CSH 22SS, and were discarded. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/7491/7/Sweet-sorghum_sugar_tech.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A 2008–09 Hyderabad planting-date study found CSH 22SS produced significantly more stalk, grain, sugar and ethanol yield than SSV 84 and SSV 74, and recommended early June to early July sowing. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/260312145_Sweet_Sorghum_Planting_Effects_on_Stalk_Yield_and_Sugar_Quality_in_Semi-Arid_Tropical_Environment
An AICSIP agronomy report lists CSH-22SS as having the highest cane yield potential (about 38 t/ha) in its sweet sorghum trials, with brix about 15.3%. -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip07/reports/5agronomy.pdf
A New Delhi trial over the 2009–2010 rainy seasons recorded 11.35 t/ha grain-equivalent yield for CSH 22SS, against 6.15 t/ha for SSV 84 and 8.53 t/ha for RSSV 9. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259704440_Developing_a_Sweet_sorghum_Ethanol_Value_Chain
A 2024 sub-tropical biofuel study ranked CSH 22SS third on stalk yield among tested sweet sorghums, with ethanol yield of about 2780 L/ha. -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2024/Feb/22-Feb-24/2024_JSRR_113170/Revised-ms_JSRR_113170_v1.pdf
A Tata Chemicals distillery pilot reported an average stalk productivity of 24.75 t/ha for CSH 22SS. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/7491/7/Sweet-sorghum_sugar_tech.pdf
Maturity is described as late for a sweet sorghum variety. No days-to-maturity figure specific to this hybrid was found. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/7491/7/Sweet-sorghum_sugar_tech.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage is ICSA 38 × SSV 84, a hybrid built from a male-sterile female and a restorer. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
ICSA 38 is an ICRISAT-bred male-sterile line, and SSV 84 served as the restorer. -- https://oar.icrisat.org/2598/1/SweetSorghumFoodFeedFodderAndFuelCrop_2006.pdf
The hybrid's SSV 84 parent derives from a selection from IS 23568, originally from Ethiopia. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
The hybrid was assigned the pedigree "ICSA 38 × SSV 84" in the AICRP pedigree listing. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum
No QTL, marker, gene or genome-resource study for this hybrid was found. -- (search returned none)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
The hybrid was developed at the Directorate of Sorghum Research (DSR), Rajendranagar, Hyderabad, within the AICSIP network, and released for commercial cultivation in 2005. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288493473_Sweet_sorghum_for_biofuel_and_strategies_for_its_improvement

(3) Nitrogen response trial: CSH 23 and CSH 15R were less responsive to higher nitrogen doses than other hybrids. (4) Intercropping trial, sorghum + pigeonpea at six locations: CSH 23 had the highest overall mean grain yield among five genotypes tested; the reported value is 3535 (the source text is truncated). (5) Stability trial: CSH 23 was among genotypes described as stable across kharif, rabi and summer seasons.

Drought tolerance as such is not described for this hybrid. Heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. Searches returned only drought-escape wording.

Grain mould resistance is recorded in the variety description, which gives the hybrid's plant height and seed traits -- Resistant to grain mold. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
A second description also places it among hybrids with grain mould resistance -- Tall, midrib dull green, thick and juicy stem, white medium bold seed, medium maturity, resistant to grain moulds. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
Shoot fly, stem borer, charcoal rot, and other pests or diseases: No evidence found specific to this hybrid.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity and grain yield: the academia review gives about 101-103 days to maturity and about 43 q/ha grain yield -- It takes 101-103 days to mature and yields about 43 q/ha of grain. https://www.academia.edu/56285705/Sorghum_cultivation_for_value_added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
Plant height: about 180 cm, tall, with a dull green midrib and white medium-bold seed -- Tall (180cm), dull green midrib, medium bold, white seed. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives
Trial yield as check: in 2007 AICSIP hybrid trials, three entries gave 9-15% yield gains over CSH 23, which yielded 3,882-3,992 kg/ha as the check -- Three hybrids, 153A x R87, 2295A x R436, and 257A x R84 recorded 14.9, 14.1 and 9.04% increase in yields over the check, CSH 23 (3992 kg/ha). https://millets.res.in/aicsip07/reports/3breeding_report.pdf
Maturity in a 2012 kharif trial: CSH 23 was the early check at 68 days to flowering and 107 days to maturity -- It was earlier than early check, CSH 23 (68 DTF and 107 DTM). https://millets.res.in/aicsip12/reports/kh/3breeding_report.pdf
Nitrogen response: CSH 23 was less responsive to higher nitrogen doses than other hybrids -- Hybrids 'CSH 23' and 'CSH 15R' were less responsive to higher doses of nitrogen as compared to other hybrids. https://www.academia.edu/56285705/Sorghum_cultivation_for_value_added_diversified_products_and_sweet_sorghum_perspectives
Intercropping trial (sorghum + pigeonpea, six locations): CSH 23 had the highest mean grain yield among the five genotypes tested -- Based on over all mean, CSH 23 had the highest grain yield (3535 (truncated in source) https://millets.res.in/aicsip09/report/5agronoomy_report.pdf
Stability trial: CSH 23 was among genotypes described as stable across seasons in a kharif, rabi and summer evaluation -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip17/reports/kh/3-Kharif_breeding.pdf
Release notification: S.O. 1566(E), dated 05/11/2005 -- https://millets.res.in/aicsip09/report/AICSIP_Coordinating_team_report.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: the hybrid was developed through MS 7A x RS 627 -- The grain sorghum hybrid CSH 23 was developed through MS 7A x RS 627. https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011
Breeding line codes: MS 7A (male-sterile line) and RS 627 (restorer line); SPH 1290 is the hybrid code. Source as above.
Breeding method: a male-sterile by restorer cross, i.e. a single-cross hybrid, as shown by the pedigree record. Source as above.
Genome resources, QTL, markers: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: The grain sorghum hybrid CSH 23 was developed through MS 7A x RS 627 at NRCS, Hyderabad (now the Directorate of Sorghum Research, Rajendranagar, Hyderabad). https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384789_Pedigree_database_on_Sorghum_Elite_Breeding_Stock_AICSIP_2006_-_2011

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Haryana Chari-6(S-308) / Sorghum

Name-matching note: the CSC minutes name is "Haryana Chari-6(S-308)" and the Seednet name is identical, so both headings refer to the same string. No page I retrieved names this exact string. The closest hits use "Haryana Chari-6" (no S-308), "Haryana Chari-308", or "HC-308". Those are different entries and are reported below only as unconfirmed leads.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Forage sorghum "Haryana Chari 6" (CCS Haryana Agricultural University, Hisar, 1989) is described as having resistance to lodging and leaf diseases, but the page does not say it is the same entry as Haryana Chari-6(S-308) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281241_Development_and_Diffusion_of_Sorghum_Improved_Cultivars_In_India_Impact_on_Growth_and_Stability_in_Yield (partial name match, unconfirmed)
- Sorghum Vision 2030 lists the same "Haryana Chari 6" as a popular single-cut forage variety with leaf-disease and lodging resistance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/252384766_Sorghum_Vision_2030 (partial name match, unconfirmed)
- A separate candidate, "HC-308" (Haryana Chari-308), is described as tolerant to major foliar diseases and suited to rainfed and irrigated Haryana -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280229288_Improved_sorghum_cultivation_and_value-addition_perspectives (name not matched; discarded for this record)
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found for this variety. The leaf-disease resistance statements above belong to "Haryana Chari 6" or "HC-308" and are not attributed here.
- A stem-borer item appears in a Development and Diffusion table for a Haryana Chari entry, but the row is not clearly tied to this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281241_Development_and_Diffusion_of_Sorghum_Improved_Cultivars_In_India_Impact_on_Growth_and_Stability_in_Yield (discarded: unclear match)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No evidence found for this variety. The search returned general forage-sorghum yield tables for other varieties and hybrids, such as CSH 24 MF and Pant Chari 6, which were discarded.
- Forage-variety database listing "Haryana Chari – 308 (HC–308)" under single-cut varieties, with no yield data for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/348650028_Database_of_Forage_Crop_Varieties_2020 (name not matched; discarded)

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage for "Haryana Chari-308" is given as SPV 8 X IS-4776, released by CCS Haryana Agricultural University in 1996. The record's parentage is "SPV 8 X 1S 4776", which may be the same cross but the name differs from "Haryana Chari-6(S-308)" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281241_Development_and_Diffusion_of_Sorghum_Improved_Cultivars_In_India_Impact_on_Growth_and_Stability_in_Yield (unconfirmed identity)
- Fifty-years AICRP sorghum review lists "Haryana Chari 308" with a pedigree entry, notified 2010 with protection ended -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/361163981_Fifty_years_of_research_and_development_under_All-India_Coordinated_Research_Project_on_Sorghum (name not matched; unconfirmed)

seednet_fields.Parentage: (CSV 20 x Pant Chari 5) x (CSV 20 x PVK 809)- 11-1-1-2-1-1  CSV 20 = SPV 246 x Kh-89-246- Dual sorghum variety Pant Chari 5 = CS 3541 x IS 6935 – Forage sorghum variety PVK 809 = PVK 801 x SPV 881 – Dual sorghum variety
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rainfed Kharif; Zone-II (Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: Suitable for timely sowing (June 15 to July 15 sowing) SPV 2316 showed good response to increasing doses of fertility levels and gave an average gain of 6.8% and 5.7% for green and dry fodder yield respectively at higher dose (125% of RDF) (1010:50:50 kg NPK/ha) of fertilizers. The variety also performed better than CSV 30F Resistant to lodging and seed shattering (visual evaluation) Seed rate: 20-25 kg/ha
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: 1.	Leaf mid-rib colour: Yellow green and dropping leaves 2.	Days to 50% flowering: 70-72 days 3.	Panicle: Semi-compact and well exserted 4.	Panicle: Arista present (Awned apikelet) 5.	Seed size and colour: Medium bold and yellow white. 6.	Seed shape: Elliptic
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Adopted top rainfed Kharif and resistant to leaf.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: SPV 2316 recorded high resistance for grey leaf spot (2.35), shooty stripe (1.0), L:eaf blight (2.63) and Rust (1.30) and moderately resistant to Zonate Leaf spot (4.97), Anthracnose (3.30) and Grain mould (3.50) under natural field conditions on disease scale of 1-10.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: SPV 2316 is tolerant to stem borer (Average Dead heart score=14.83) and Shootly pest (average dead heart score = 34.6) and on par with the checks CSV 21F and CSV30F under natural field conditions.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): Nitrogen 80-100 kg/ha in two split doses (half at the time of sowing as basal and half at 35-40 days after sowing or at knee stage of the crop. Application of phosphorus (P) 40-50 kg/ha and potash (K)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Melghat (AKU-4), Black gram (urd)

Name note: The release-minutes name "Melghat (AKU-4)" and the Seednet name "MELGHAT (AKU-4)" are the same variety. Sources write it as "AKU-4 (Melghat)", "AKU 4 (Melghat)", "Melghat (AKU-4)" or "AKU-4". All evidence below refers to this variety only where the page names AKU-4 or Melghat together with black gram. The searches found very little variety-specific material.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Melghat (AKU-4). The only stress-related text was general black gram crop information, such as the statement that black gram cannot be grown on alkaline and saline soils (https://dpd.gov.in/Urdbean.pdf). This does not name the variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- No evidence found specific to Melghat (AKU-4). The general black gram pest and disease reviews returned do not name it (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10822891/; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5383788/).
- Discarded: the PDKV Directorate of Research circular describes a black gram-adjacent entry as "moderately resistant to Alternaria and leaf hopper", but the entry is not clearly tied to Melghat (AKU-4) and its oil-percentage details do not match black gram. Source: https://www.pdkv.ac.in/Circulars/Recom-2023English.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- No variety-specific field-trial or agronomy evidence found. The PDKV department page lists AKU 10-1 (2014-15) as a black gram release, which is a different variety and was discarded (https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=3119).
- Season suitability (indirect): Melghat (AKU-4) is described as suitable for post-rainy (rabi) season cultivation (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269571420_Identification_of_Photosensitive_Blackgram_and_their_Characterisation). Its listing as a spring-season variety also appears in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigna_mungo.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (from the user-supplied record, not independently verified): selection from local landraces of the Melghat tribal area. No independent web source confirmed this.
- No evidence found for genes, QTL, markers, breeding-line codes or genome resources for Melghat (AKU-4). The genetics and genomics review returned names no AKU-4 line (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC10822891/). The bruchid QTL map uses the BC48 × TC2210 cross, which is unrelated to this variety (https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC6408486/). Both were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Institution (from user record): Pulses Breeder, Pulses Research Unit, Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (PKV/PDKV), Akola. The breeder's name was not found in any search result.
- No evidence found naming the lead breeder or scientist for Melghat (AKU-4).

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder's name, email, phone number or postal address for Melghat (AKU-4).
- Institute-level web presence only (no phone, email or postal address was retrieved): https://www.pdkv.ac.in/ (Department of Agricultural Botany page: https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=3119).

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2013). Identification of Photosensitive Blackgram and their Characterisation. Indian Journal of Plant Genetic Resources 26(1): 47-49 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269571420_Identification_of_Photosensitive_Blackgram_and_their_Characterisation (this paper only lists Melghat (AKU-4) among popular varieties; it does not study it).
- No other publication naming Melghat (AKU-4) was found. The PDKV agricultural botany and cost-of-cultivation items do not concern this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. Seed dealer pages returned (IndiaMart, DesiKheti, KVSSL) list black gram generally or other varieties and do not name Melghat (AKU-4). No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK or SAU seed-sale listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Maharashtra: listed under the AKU-4 (Melghat) entry in a state-wise variety table (https://dpd.gov.in/Urdbean.pdf). The table's Gujarat row also appears to include AKU-4 (Melghat) (https://journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45739.pdf); the PDF table layout is ambiguous, so verify against the official notification.
- Spring-season Maharashtra recommendation: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/ifpri-tecnological-innovation-and-their-potential-niches/30032067 (table layout is hard to read; treat as indicative).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: WBU-108 (Black gram / urd, Vigna mungo)

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "WBU-108". The sources write it as "WBU 108" or "WBU-108". One weed-management paper calls the variety "Sarada" in its text (23-3). I found no evidence of a separate CSC minutes name. The release year (1996) and parentage come from the brief only. No search result confirmed them.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- WBU 108 is listed among black gram genotypes identified as resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic disease (MYMD), with a disease score of 1 cited to Goyal and Khan (2010). -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to WBU-108. The retrieved general urad pages do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- MYMD resistance (see above). -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363/full
- No evidence found for powdery mildew, Cercospora, leaf crinkle, or insect-pest reaction specific to WBU-108.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- A two-season kharif study in 2014 and 2015 used WBU-108 at a farmer's field in Sriniketan, Birbhum, West Bengal, to test herbicides. The spacing was 30 × 10 cm. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319154324_Chemical_weed_management_in_kharif_blackgram_under_lateritic_soil_of_West_Bengal_India
- A companion page describes the same two-year (2014–2015) kharif trial at the Visva-Bharati Sriniketan farm. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265088287_Physicochemical_Functional_Pasting_Properties_and_Nutritional_Composition_of_Selected_Black_Gram_Phaseolus_mungo_L_Varieties. Treat this with caution: its title is about pasting properties of other varieties, so I did not rely on it.
- No evidence found for maturity duration or grain yield specific to WBU-108. One state-table snippet gives yield figures next to a list that includes WBU 108, but the mapping is ambiguous, so I have not recorded it as a finding. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/ifpri-tecnological-innovation-and-their-potential-niches/30032067

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (PANT U26 × B-76 lineage, from the brief): No evidence found in search results. Not independently verified.
- Breeding-line code, breeding method, QTL and marker-trait associations: No evidence found for WBU-108.
- Molecular diversity: In a RAPD study of black gram, WBU-108 and RBU-38 were highly divergent, while LBG-648 and LBG-623 were genetically similar. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5383788/ (DOI 10.1007/s13205-016-0582-8). This paper cites a prior 20-variety RAPD/ISSR comparison, and that study is the source of the WBU-108 result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No evidence found naming a lead breeder or developing institution for WBU-108. The search returned general black gram pages, not variety records.
- The brief's parentage refers to a Behrampore CVT entry. A Burdwan University page lists a "Pulses and Oilseeds Research Institute, Behrampur" for other crops, but it does not name WBU-108. -- https://www.buruniv.ac.in/mobileDemo/Template.php?menu=Facilities&submenu=CRSMF. I have not linked this institute to the variety.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for a breeder contact or a developing-institution contact linked to WBU-108.
- Institute-level address seen in the search, not linked to WBU-108: Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, Mohanpur, Nadia, West Bengal, PIN 741252. -- https://www.bckv.edu.in/images/pdf/Varieties-developed_nw.pdf. No email or phone was found on that page. Verify the developing institution before using this address.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2014–2015 field trial). Chemical weed management in kharif blackgram under lateritic soil of West Bengal, India. Field trial report/journal not identified in retrieved text -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/319154324_Chemical_weed_management_in_kharif_blackgram_under_lateritic_soil_of_West_Bengal_India
- Ramakrishnan M. (2024). Genetics, genomics, and breeding of black gram [Vigna mungo (L.) Hepper]. Frontiers in Plant Science -- DOI 10.3389/fpls.2023.1273363 (also PMC10822891). The review's table lists WBU 108 as an MYMD-resistant genotype.
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (RAPD-assisted selection of black gram, multiple disease resistance). Journal not shown in retrieved text. -- DOI 10.1007/s13205-016-0582-8; https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC5383788/
- No evidence found for AICRP/ICAR annual reports or KrishiKosh theses naming WBU-108. The KrishiKosh thesis that surfaced was about other black gram varieties and did not name this one.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The search did not return any seed-sales page for WBU-108.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Assam: WBU-108 is listed among recommended varieties. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Urdbean.PDF
- Assam, Bihar and Jharkhand, Odisha, Uttarakhand and West Bengal: the state table lists WBU-108 for these states. -- https://journalcra.com/sites/default/files/issue-pdf/45739.pdf
- Odisha: WBU-108 is listed as a kharif recommendation. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/pulses-in-odisha/black-gram/
- Haryana and Karnataka: WBU-108 appears in state lists for kharif. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/ifpri-tecnological-innovation-and-their-potential-niches/30032067
- These are secondary compilations. The release notification and the official state notifications were not found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Goutam (WBU-105), Black gram (urd), variety code A0301093

Names: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical, "Goutam (WBU-105)". Every finding below refers to that name, though the sources use shortened forms: "Goutam" alone (slideshare) and "WBU-105" alone (West Bengal State Seed Corporation list). Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned general black gram descriptions (drought tolerance of the crop as a species, not of Goutam) -- https://www.echocommunity.org/en/resources/759594b3-3c1f-4bdf-b52c-5fe6bc5632ff

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found for Goutam. The only pest/disease resistance statements found concern other varieties: WBU 109 (Sulata) is listed as resistant to MYMV, and NDU-993 and KU 96-3 are described as YMV resistant -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Goutam is listed with a yield of 13-15 (units not stated in the source), a maturity of 69-90 days, origin Berhanpur (sic), and release year 2004 -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749 (note: this conflicts with the 2003 release year in the CSC record; the source's entry is a table row with no methodology).
No multi-location trial results for Goutam were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
No evidence found. The parentage "T9 X CO4" was not found in any source. The searches did return a general statement that T9 (1948) was the first black gram variety developed in India, but it does not link T9 to Goutam -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Vigna_mungo . No QTL or marker studies on Goutam were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Pulses and Oilseeds Research Station, Berhampore (West Bengal). The station is described as a commodity research station under the state Department of Agriculture, with pulse and oilseed research beginning there in 1950 -- https://www.facebook.com/p/Pulses-and-Oilseeds-Research-Station-Berhampore-100069235508417/
No breeder name for Goutam was found in any source.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No official email, phone, postal address or institute contact page was found for Pulses and Oilseeds Research Station, Berhampore. The only institute-level source is its Facebook page, which gave no contact details in the retrieved text -- https://www.facebook.com/p/Pulses-and-Oilseeds-Research-Station-Berhampore-100069235508417/

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. Searches for peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR reports, theses and KrishiKosh records returned no item naming Goutam or WBU-105. Results on black gram generally (genetic diversity studies, weed management using WBU-108) do not name this variety, so they were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
West Bengal State Seed Corporation Limited lists "WBU-105" among urd varieties in its seed availability table (under Pulses, Urd). This entry does not use the name "Goutam", so it is a match on the WBU-105 code only -- https://www.wbsscl.com/availability-of-seeds/
No NSC, KVK, SAU or private dealer listing for Goutam was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
West Bengal -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/black-gram-ppt-black-gram-also-known-as-urad-or-urd-bean-is-an-important-pulse-crop-grown-in-india/271676749 (single secondary source; the CSC record lists recommended states as "Unknown").

drought.details: No evidence found for this variety. The digest's searches returned only general black gram climate notes. The variety record describes the crop as rainfed when grown in post-kharif, with one irrigation possibly required in spring; this describes adaptation and is not a drought-tolerance finding.

heat.details: No evidence found for this variety. The digest's searches returned only general black gram climate notes.

salinity.details: No evidence found for this variety. The digest's searches returned only general black gram climate notes.

flood.details: The digest has no evidence on flood tolerance for this variety. The variety record (not corroborated by the digest) states the variety can withstand waterlogged conditions. The record also states the variety is resistant to lodging and shattering, which is not a flood-tolerance finding.

disease_resistance.summary: Yellow mosaic virus (MYMV): resistant or tolerant. The RCSKB Assam pulses page lists Sulata as resistant to MYMV. A commercial blog variety table lists it as resistant to yellow mosaic virus. The central released varieties table (DPD PDF) lists it as resistant to MYMV. A DPD pulses variety sheet lists it as resistant or moderately resistant to yellow mosaic virus; the page title refers to chickpea, but the entry is for urdbean. The variety record describes it as tolerant to yellow mosaic virus, which differs from the digest's resistant wording. Cercospora leaf spot and leaf crinkle virus: resistant according to the variety record only; the digest contains no corroborating evidence. Web blight: Not found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest found no evidence naming this variety in pest sections for bruchid, aphid, web blight or other pests; the RCSKB pest pages and the DPD pest sheet do not name it. The variety record (not corroborated by the digest) states tolerance to Bihar hairy caterpillar and pod borer and resistance to stem fly.

agronomic_details.yield: The variety record gives 1500-1600 kg/ha. The DPD central release table gives 10-12 q/ha (spring season, NEPZ). A commercial blog (unverified) gives 15-16 q/ha. The digest records these as conflicting; the 10-12 q/ha figure is the one attributed to the official table. The digest's farmer-level report and the agrisilviculture trial are not attributed to this variety by name and were excluded.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-location or AICRP results for this variety were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for spring/post-kharif sowing in West Bengal (NEPZ) per the DPD central release table. The RCSKB Assam page lists kharif suitability. Sowing window per the variety record: last week of February to first week of March. Highest yield recorded at 30 x 10 cm spacing (variety record). The variety record describes the crop as rainfed when grown in post-kharif, with one spring irrigation possibly required.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: GROWS TO A HEIGHT OF 35-40 CM, NORMALLY LOOKS DWARF, COMPACT DETERMINATE GROWTH HABIT, PUTS UP MODERATE FOLIAGE, UNDER GOOD MOISTURES AND SOIL FERTILITY: LIGHT GREEN, SLIGHTLY, LANCE LATE LEAVES, PODS HAIRY SEEDS BOLD (5-6 GM/100 SEEDS) WITH DISTINCT SHINING BLACK SEED COAT.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Summer 2008-2010 sowing-date trial at Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana: WBU 109 was included among summer black gram genotypes, with phenophase durations measured; no numeric results are given in the digest. (2) Nano-phosphorus trial using WBU-109 at 30 x 10 cm spacing, 20 kg/ha seed rate, 5 x 6 m plots (Legume Research); no numeric results are given in the digest. Other trials: Not found in searched sources. Maturity conflicts across sources: 70-75 days (DPD and RCSKB pages), 80-85 days (commercial blog, unverified), and 80-83 days (variety record).

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. The SNP/QTL bruchid map paper (BC48 x TC2210) and the 2023 black gram genetics review concern other materials and do not name this variety.

commercial_info.private_dealers: Not found in searched sources. Generic West Bengal black gram seed shops (DesiKheti) do not name this variety.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus (MYMV) -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/crops/Pulses
Listed as resistant to yellow mosaic virus in a variety table -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/04/high-yield-uradblack-gram-variety.html
Tolerance to heat, drought, salinity, flood or submergence: No evidence found for this variety. The searches returned only general black gram climate notes.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistant to MYMV (listed in the Central released varieties table) -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Resistant to yellow mosaic virus, moderately resistant or resistant to MYMV (dpd pulses variety sheet, Sulata entry, page title refers to chickpea but the entry is for urdbean) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Web%20site.pdf
Resistance to web blight, aphid, bruchid or other pests specific to WBU 109: No evidence found. The pest pages on the RCSKB Assam site and the DPD pest sheet do not name this variety in the pest sections.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Recommended duration 70-75 days and grain yield 10-12 q/ha, suitable for kharif -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/crops/Pulses
Duration 70-75 days and yield 10-12 q/ha, spring season, NEPZ (West Bengal) -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Conflicting claim: duration 80-85 days and yield 15-16 q/ha (commercial blog, unverified) -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/04/high-yield-uradblack-gram-variety.html
Farmer-level report (news article, Ruppur village, West Bengal): matures 15 to 20 days earlier than Kali-50, 60-65 pods per plant versus 30-35, seed rate 30 kg/ha -- https://eng.kisanofindia.com/latest-news/black-gram-cultivation-this-woman-adopted-new-technology-in-the-cultivation-of-urad-dal
Summer 2008-2010 sowing-date trial at Punjab Agricultural University, Ludhiana, included WBU 109 among genotypes, measuring phenophase durations -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-attributes-yield-and-harvest-index-of-summer-blackgram-genotypes-as-influenced-by_tbl1_256492098
Nano-phosphorus trial using WBU-109 at 30 x 10 cm spacing, 20 kg/ha seed rate, 5 x 6 m plots -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5575
Sole crop in agrisilviculture trial (Bijasal-based): grain yield 9.9 q/ha -- https://indianforester.co.in/index.php/indianforester/article/view/170561

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage PANT U-26 (female) x B-76 (male): No evidence found. The parentage in the variety record was not confirmed by any retrieved page.
Breeding-line codes, breeding method, genes, markers, QTL, genome resources for WBU 109: No evidence found. The SNP/QTL bruchid map paper (BC48 x TC2210) and the 2023 black gram genetics review concern other materials and do not name this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: Pulses and Oilseeds Research Station (PORS), Berhampore, West Bengal. The audit lists Sulata WBU-109 (2008) as one of five pulse varieties PORS developed in 2008-2018 -- https://d1jmc0u14z2tmp.cloudfront.net/uploads/download_audit_report/2019/3.%20Chapter_2-062430653813421.12516653.pdf
Originating centre "Berhampore (W.B)" -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute email, phone, postal address, or contact page for PORS Berhampore: No evidence found. The only contact in the results (Dr. K. Pradhan, OUAT Berhampur, Odisha, AICRP Pulses) belongs to a different station and was discarded -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324031547_Seed_A_vital_component_for_enhancing_pulses_productivity
Suggested next step: obtain the station address from the seednet.gov.in or ICAR/West Bengal state agriculture university directories, which were not reached by search.

PUBLICATIONS
Bharti, M., Oraon, P. R., & Singh, B. K. (2025). Growth and Yield of different Blackgram varieties under Bijasal (Pterocarpus marsupium Roxb.) based Agrisilviculture System. Indian Forester, 151(8), 739-744 -- https://doi.org/10.36808/if/2025/v151i8/170561
Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Substitutional Effect of Molecular Phosphorus with Nano Particle on the Performance of Black Gram (Vigna mungo L.). Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5575
Authors not stated in retrieved text (2008-2010 pooled data). Yield attributes, yield and harvest index of summer blackgram genotypes as influenced by sowing time. Punjab Agricultural University trial, journal not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/Yield-attributes-yield-and-harvest-index-of-summer-blackgram-genotypes-as-influenced-by_tbl1_256492098
Author not stated in retrieved text (2019). Chapter 2: Performance Audit, 2.1 Functioning of Agricultural Farms (Government audit report covering PORS Berhampore breeder seed production) -- https://d1jmc0u14z2tmp.cloudfront.net/uploads/download_audit_report/2019/3.%20Chapter_2-062430653813421.12516653.pdf
Authors not stated in retrieved text (year not stated). Physicochemical, Functional, Pasting Properties and Nutritional Composition of Selected Black Gram (Phaseolus mungo L.) Varieties (includes WBU 109 seed measurements). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/265088287_Physicochemical_Functional_Pasting_Properties_and_Nutritional_Composition_of_Selected_Black_Gram_Phaseolus_mungo_L_Varieties
AICRP, ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, field-trial multi-location results: No evidence found for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
PORS Berhampore breeder seed shortfall: production of breeder seed of pulses fell well below target in 2014-15 to 2016-17, and the station could not meet demand for breeder seed for further multiplication as foundation and certified seed -- https://d1jmc0u14z2tmp.cloudfront.net/uploads/download_audit_report/2019/3.%20Chapter_2-062430653813421.12516653.pdf
NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings naming Sulata (WBU 109): No evidence found. Generic West Bengal black gram seed shops (DesiKheti) do not name this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Central release table: West Bengal (NEPZ), spring season -- http://dpd.gov.in/iv)%20Urdbean%20Varieties.pdf
Commercial blog: suitable for UP, Bihar, West Bengal, Assam and Jharkhand in spring (unverified) -- https://www.vantikatech.com/2020/04/high-yield-uradblack-gram-variety.html
Assam (RCSKB) page: suitable for kharif -- https://rkbassam.aau.ac.in/crops/Pulses

heat.details: Heat tolerance: not found for this variety. The ICAR-IIPR report attributes heat tolerance to JG 14, which is a different variety and is excluded from this profile.

salinity.details: Described as a salt-tolerant desi variety recommended for salt-affected areas, selected from GPF 7035 (input record gives GF 7035). A genomics review describes it as tolerant of moderate salinity (ECe about 4 to 6 dS/m). Ranked among the most salt-tolerant genotypes under two salinity levels, with higher WRKY and NAC transcription factor expression in tolerant CSG 8962. Retained maximum filled pods at EC 6 dS/m and showed relatively higher yield-index tolerance in a 2018-19/2019-20 trial, where it served as the salt-tolerant check. Used as the salt-tolerant check in a nodulation/nitrogen study with nine other genotypes and in a seedling-stage proline/root water-relations study. Input record describes suitability for medium salt stress environments.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Karnal Chana-1 (CSG 8962), Chickpea

Name check: The Seednet name "KARNAL CHANA-1 (CSG-8962)" did not appear in any result, so I could not confirm the portal record. All evidence below refers to "Karnal Chana 1 (CSG 8962)", which matches the release-minutes name. Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institute, research papers, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Salt-tolerant desi variety, recommended for salt-affected areas; a 1998 selection from GPF 7035 -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320414296_Milling_properties_of_desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_varieties_released_in_India
- Described as tolerant of moderate salinity (ECe about 4 to 6 dS/m) in a genomics review -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/233969780_Impact_of_Genomic_Technologies_on_Chickpea_Breeding_Strategies
- Ranked among the most salt-tolerant genotypes under two salinity levels, with higher WRKY and NAC transcription factor expression in tolerant CSG 8962 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368543526_Effect_of_Salinity_stress_on_Photosynthesis_and_expression_of_salt_tolerant_genes_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
- Retained maximum filled pods at EC 6 dS/m and showed relatively higher yield-index tolerance; salt-tolerant check in a 2018-19/2019-20 trial -- https://www.mmumullana.org/research_publication/identification-of-salt-tolerant-chickpea-genotypes-based-on-yield-and-salinity-indices/ and https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4519
- Salt-tolerant check in a nodulation/nitrogen study with nine other genotypes -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-19585-4
- Seedling-stage proline/root water-relations study used CSG 8962 as salt-tolerant check -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9527943/
- Wilt resistant (dpd listing) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Heat tolerance: not found for this variety (heat tolerance is attributed to JG 14 in the ICAR-IIPR report) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Wilt resistant; moderately resistant to dry root rot (apnakhetibazar listing; the dpd PDF gives wilt resistance only) -- https://apnakhetibazar.com/chana-gram-chickpea/ and https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Ascochyta blight, pod borer, and other pest-specific resistance: No evidence found for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 140-147 days; average yield 9-11 quintal/acre -- https://apnakhetibazar.com/chana-gram-chickpea/
- Dpd listing gives 22-25 (plant height/yield-range fields, units not stated) and 140-147 days -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Small seed (about 15 g per 100 seeds) with GPF 7035 kabuli parentage in the ICAR-IIPR report -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Haryana district evaluation: farmers still grow it; not yet compared in a systematic yield trial -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5531
- Milling/chaff recovery data for the variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320414296_Milling_properties_of_desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_varieties_released_in_India and https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/74994/31515/189951

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage/selection: "Selection from GPF 7035" (the input gives GF 7035; the sources write GPF 7035) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320414296_Milling_properties_of_desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_varieties_released_in_India
- Breeding-line code CSG 8962 -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Transcription factor expression (WRKY, NAC) associated with tolerance; no QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368543526_Effect_of_Salinity_stress_on_Photosynthesis_and_expression_of_salt_tolerant_genes_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
- Breeding method (selection vs hybridisation): sources differ; the milling paper says "Selection from GPF 7035"; the ICAR-IIPR report lists it as a selection from germplasm for some entries -- see the ICAR-IIPR report above. Conclusive method: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Central Soil Salinity Research Institute (CSSRI), Karnal, Haryana -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/396454403_Maintaining_nitrogen_balance_under_salt_stress_through_enhanced_nodule_function_and_antioxidative_defense_in_chickpea
- Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found in any retrieved page.
- Release year: 1997 in the dpd listing and Legume Research paper; 1998 in the milling paper, the ICAR-IIPR report, and the input record. The input value (1998) is the one used in the ICAR-IIPR report and milling paper -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder contact, official email, phone, or postal address found for CSSRI or this variety. No institute contact page URL was retrieved. Recommended next step: contact ICAR-CSSRI, Karnal (official site cssri.res.in, not verified in this session).

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2018-19 and 2019-20 trial). Identification of Salt Tolerant Chickpea Genotypes Based on Yield and Salinity Indices. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4519
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2021). Evaluation of Promising Cultivars in Major Chickpea Cultivating Districts of Haryana State. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5531
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (2025). Maintaining nitrogen balance under salt stress through enhanced nodule function and antioxidative defense in chickpea. Scientific Reports -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-025-19585-4
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. Getting to the roots of Cicer arietinum L. (chickpea) to study the effect of salinity on morpho-physiological, biochemical and molecular traits. PMC -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9527943/
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. Effect of Salinity stress on Photosynthesis and expression of salt tolerant genes in Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.). ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368543526_Effect_of_Salinity_stress_on_Photosynthesis_and_expression_of_salt_tolerant_genes_in_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L
- Authors not shown in retrieved text. Milling properties of desi and kabuli chickpea (Cicer arietinum) varieties released in India. ResearchGate -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320414296_Milling_properties_of_desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_varieties_released_in_India
- Authors not shown. Marching towards self-sufficiency in chickpea (cites Karnal Chana 1 for mild salinity). Current Science 116(2) -- https://www.currentscience.ac.in/Volumes/116/02/0239.pdf
- Authors not shown. ICAR-IIPR Project Coordinator's Report, Chickpea 2021-22 (variety entry 43). ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or ICAR seed-sale pages. The only commercial result was an exporter's marketing page (https://yeshasviexporters.com/tag/rarechickpeasexport/), which is not a seed source and is not cited as such.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- North-West Plain Zone (NWPZ): Punjab, Haryana, Delhi, north Rajasthan and west Uttar Pradesh -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Apnakhetibazar lists north Rajasthan -- https://apnakhetibazar.com/chana-gram-chickpea/
- Input field "recommended_states_raw" was "Unknown"; the states above come from the sources, not from the input.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The ICAR-IIPR AICRP chickpea report (2021-22) lists "Gulabi Akola 1 (Gulak 1)" in its variety table, but the row gives no stress-tolerance entry. Its drought-tolerance statements belong to other varieties (e.g., BG 4005, Pusa 362 DTIL), so I did not attribute them here. Searched under both names. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The same ICAR report row lists no disease or pest reaction for Gulabi Akola 1 (Gulak 1). Its wilt-resistance note belongs to PDKV Kanchan. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Gulabi Akola 1 (Gulak 1) row, ICAR-IIPR AICRP Chickpea report 2021-22: release year 1997, developing centre Akola, growth habit semi-spreading with white flowers, gulabi (rose-coloured) round seed, large seed (about 26 g/100 seed), and irrigated/rainfed suitability. The table columns are not labelled in the extracted text, so the numeric values (12 and 115) are unverified and I have not interpreted them. Name matched: Gulabi Akola 1 (Gulak 1). Seednet name GULABI AKOLA-1 not found in these results. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
No field-trial or multi-location yield data for this variety was found. -- searched both names

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage (N-59 x D-8)1-88-88A: supplied in the input record only; not confirmed by any search result.
Origin conflict: the ICAR-IIPR report lists the variety's origin as a selection from local germplasm, which does not match the cross-based parentage in the input record. This needs checking against the CSC release minutes. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence: No evidence found. -- searched both names

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth (Dr. PDKV), Akola, Maharashtra, per the input record and the ICAR report row (Akola, 1997). The ICAR report also lists Dr. PDKV as the releasing institution for other chickpea varieties. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Breeder name(s): No evidence found. The search returned no lead breeder or scientist name for this variety. The input record gives only the role "Sr. Research Scientist (Pulses), Pulses Research Unit, Dr. PDKV, Akola," without a name.

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found for a breeder, email, phone, or postal address for GULAK-1 / GULABI AKOLA-1 in these results. Institute-level contact pages for Dr. PDKV were not returned by the searches. Searched both names.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found for a paper, thesis, or report specific to GULAK-1 / GULABI AKOLA-1.
Excluded: the KrishiKosh thesis "Impact Assessment of Chickpea Variety Released by Dr. PDKV, Akola" (https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/e6bbf4ad-03de-4363-9b40-3886f9efb7b4/content). Its abstract covers PDKV chickpea varieties in general, and the snippet did not name Gulabi Akola 1, so I did not attribute it to this variety. Confirm the full text before using it.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for this variety. The ICAR-IIPR 2021-22 report gives only national breeder-seed totals across 65 chickpea varieties, with no per-variety quantities. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer listing for GULAK-1 / GULABI AKOLA-1 was found. -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
Excluded: private-dealer pages for "Gulabi" chickpea (Varsha Seeds "Royal Gulabi", a Malaysian snack, and Amazon listings) are different products and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Maharashtra -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (the table row lists Maharashtra as the state; the input record's "Unknown" is superseded by this single source, which should be confirmed against the CSC minutes).

drought.details: Released as a variety for limited moisture conditions in Punjab (ResearchGate title; CSC adaptation text). A physiological and biochemical screening study describes PDG 4 as drought tolerant, alongside PDG 3, with PBG 1, GPF 2 and others as susceptible comparators. The level is medium because the evidence comes from one screening study and the release description, not from multi-season field drought trials. The CSC adaptation text recommends it for limited moisture conditions in Punjab except the sub-mountainous zone.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Released as a multiple-disease-resistant desi chickpea. In state trials at Ludhiana and Faridkot, the incidence of Ascochyta blight, wilt, root rot and foot rot was very low on PDG4 compared with the check PDG3 (CSC disease reaction text; ICRISAT newsletter). Listed as tolerant to damping off, root rot and wilt (apnikheti page). The CSC text also mentions a wilt/root rot complex, but the sentence is truncated and its PDG4 result cannot be confirmed. Resistance is supported by a newsletter and a web listing; no independent trial data were found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The pod borer damage figures in the CSC pest reaction text refer to PDG3, not PDG-4, so they are excluded.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
PDG-4 Chickpea evidence digest

Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institution; research/publications; seed availability). The Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) did not appear in any result, so Seednet-specific fields are unverified. Under each heading, "PDG-4" means the variety in the CSC minutes and "Seednet name" is the same string; the sources mostly spell it "PDG4" or "PDG 4", and I have treated those spellings as this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Released as a multiple-disease-resistant desi chickpea for Punjab, with a title describing it as grown under limited moisture conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240667055_PDG4_A_new_multiple_disease_resistant_desi_chickpea_variety_for_Punjab_state_India
- Listed as tolerant to damping off, root rot and wilt -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/bengal-gram-chickpea
- Described as drought tolerant (physiological and biochemical screening, alongside PDG 3), with PBG 1, GPF 2 and others as susceptible comparators -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344981361_Evaluation_and_Screening_of_Promising_Drought_Tolerant_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_Based_on_Physiological_and_Biochemical_Attributes_Under_Drought_Conditions
- PDG 4 appears in a list of cultivars with cold tolerance, but the snippet is ambiguous about which trait applies to which cultivar -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea
- Heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found.
- Flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Released as a multiple-disease-resistant variety; disease incidence was tabulated for PDG4 and check cultivars at Ludhiana and Faridkot -- https://oar.icrisat.org/361/1/CO_0020.pdf
- Tolerant to wilt and root diseases (apnikheti page) -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/bengal-gram-chickpea
- Pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Average seed yield of about 1820 kg/ha in trials, with comparisons to PDG3 in Punjab and to AICRP entries -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240667055_PDG4_A_new_multiple_disease_resistant_desi_chickpea_variety_for_Punjab_state_India
- In a Punjab newsletter account, mean yield was about 1906 kg/ha in one comparison with H 208 (1707 kg/ha), and about 1799 kg/ha across 14 trials against 1483 kg/ha for a check; the text is garbled, so treat these figures as approximate -- https://oar.icrisat.org/361/1/CO_0020.pdf
- The newsletter describes the variety as having high yield, medium bold seeds, and performance tested at multiple locations and in AICRP trials -- https://oar.icrisat.org/361/1/CO_0020.pdf
- Maturity/duration: an apnikheti entry gives about 160 days, but the sentence is garbled alongside a yield figure; unverified -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/pulses/bengal-gram-chickpea
- Seed quality: the Legume Science study reports PDG-4 with larger seed dimensions and surface area than other desi lines (a seed-size trait, not a yield claim) -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/leg3.168

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (from the CSC input, not verified by search): (GL769 x GF88421) x GF8976; GL769 is a Punjab-released variety, and GF88421 and GF8976 are advanced lines from Faridkot. No independent source confirmed this pedigree.
- Breeding-line codes GF88421 and GF8976: No evidence found outside the input.
- Breeding method: No evidence found.
- QTL, markers, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The ICRISAT newsletter article names Sarvjeet Singh, R K Gumber and J S Sandhu as authors, for Punjab Agricultural University -- https://oar.icrisat.org/361/1/CO_0020.pdf
- The ResearchGate record lists Sarvjeet Singh as lead author -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240667055_PDG4_A_new_multiple_disease_resistant_desi_chickpea_variety_for_Punjab_state_India
- Institution: Punjab Agricultural University (PAU), Ludhiana, with the Faridkot station involved in the trials and the parent lines. The CSC "Unknown" institution field is therefore filled from these sources, not from the CSC record -- https://oar.icrisat.org/361/1/CO_0020.pdf
- A Punjab Plant Breeding and Genetics department listing mentions PDG 4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/268280312_Chickpea
- Not this variety: the Gates Foundation article on Professor Chellapilla Bharadwaj concerns other chickpea work and does not name PDG-4 -- https://www.gatesfoundation.org/ideas/articles/chickpea-variety-innovator

CONTACT DETAILS
- No breeder email, phone or personal contact was found in the results.
- No PAU institute or Faridkot station address, email or phone was found in the results. Please check the PAU site and the Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics directly.
- Names as found: Sarvjeet Singh, R K Gumber, J S Sandhu (authors; roles and affiliations as listed above).

PUBLICATIONS
- Singh, S., Gumber, R. K., & Sandhu, J. S. (2002). PDG4: A new multiple disease resistant desi chickpea variety for Punjab state, India. ICRISAT International Chickpea and Pigeonpea Newsletter -- https://oar.icrisat.org/361/1/CO_0020.pdf (the ResearchGate listing gives 2002 for the publication, lists Sarvjeet Singh as lead author, and is at https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240667055_PDG4_A_new_multiple_disease_resistant_desi_chickpea_variety_for_Punjab_state_India). Note: the author list above is from the newsletter; the ResearchGate page shows only the lead author and "and others".
- Authors not shown (2007). Characterization of protein isolates from different Indian chickpea cultivars. Food Chemistry, vol. 102 -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0308814606004225 (PDG-4 is one of six desi/kabuli cultivars studied).
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Studies on functional, thermal and pasting properties of flours from different chickpea cultivars. Food Chemistry -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0308814604004650 (PDG-4 among six cultivars).
- Kaur (2023). Characterization and classification of selective Indian chickpea cultivars based on physical and hydration properties, using image and multivariate analysis. Legume Science. DOI 10.1002/leg3.168 -- https://onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/full/10.1002/leg3.168 (full author list not in the retrieved text).
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Evaluation and Screening of Promising Drought Tolerant Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) Genotypes Based on Physiological and Biochemical Attributes Under Drought Conditions -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344981361_Evaluation_and_Screening_of_Promising_Drought_Tolerant_Chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_L_Genotypes_Based_on_Physiological_and_Biochemical_Attributes_Under_Drought_Conditions
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22). Annual progress report, PDG 4 listed among entries -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (the snippet does not show PDG 4's status, so it is listed only as a mention).
- Not counted: a 2022 NDVI paper and a Pakistani chickpea study name PDG 4 only in tables or unrelated work.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The search returned an IndiaMART listing for generic "Bengal Gram Seeds" (Varad Agritech, Hyderabad), which does not name PDG-4, and an AP State Seeds page for other Bengal gram varieties. Neither is relevant.
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales, and private dealer listings for PDG-4 were not found. Punjab Seeds Corporation and PAU seed sales were not searched directly.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Punjab: the variety was developed and released for Punjab -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/240667055_PDG4_A_new_multiple_disease_resistant_desi_chickpea_variety_for_Punjab_state_India
- Other states: No evidence found.

Unresolved gaps: the release notification (CSC or SVRC year and number), the Seednet record, and PAU contact details were not confirmed. The year 2000 comes from the CSC input and the apnikheti page, not from an official notification.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Note: The search tool hit its usage limit after the first four queries, so no further searches were possible. The results below reflect only those four searches. The first search returned a generic recommended-varieties list, but the snippets I could read did not name this variety, so the digest below is largely "No evidence found."

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The variety-specific searches returned no page naming Pusa Kabuli Gram 128 / Pusa Shubhra / BGD 128 with stress-tolerance data. The only general chickpea result seen was a recommended-varieties list (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf) with entries for other varieties, such as Pusa 329 described as moderately resistant to wilt, which is not this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found for this variety. The same DPD list (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf) notes resistance traits for other Kabuli varieties (wilt and Botrytis grey mould), but I could not confirm this variety appears in the list or inherits those traits. Parentage data supplied in the brief (ICCV 2 x ICCV 5, wilt resistant) is from the request, not from a search source.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No trial, yield, maturity or agronomy page for this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found in search results. Parentage (ICCV 2 x ICCV 5) appears only in the user-supplied record, not in any retrieved source.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. The breeder query returned an unrelated Krishi Jagran article (https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/) about seed size and yield in chickpea, which does not name this variety's breeders. The institution in the record is IARI Centre for Pulses Improvement, Dharwad; no search result confirmed this.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder contact or institute contact page for this variety was returned. Institute-level contact should be taken from the IARI or ICAR directory and verified directly.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research query returned a Legume Research article on physiological and biochemical contents in chickpea (https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4265), which does not name this variety, so it is excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found for this variety. The seed query returned a TradeIndia listing for Pusa Manav chickpea seed in Junagadh (https://www.tradeindia.com/products/pusa-manav-chickpea-premium-seeds-c10007418.html). That is a different variety and a private listing, so it is excluded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Not verified by search. The record lists Chhattisgarh, Gujarat, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, but I found no source confirming this. The DPD list (https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf) should be checked for this variety's state-wise recommendation.

RELEASE YEAR -- Unknown in the record and not found in search results.

NAME CHECK -- Under both "variety_name" (Pusa Kabuli Gram 128 (Pusa Shubhra)/BGD 128) and "seednet_variety_name" (Pusa Kubuli Gram 128 (Pusa Shubhra)/BGD 128), none of the retrieved pages named the variety, so no evidence is attributed under either name.

Suggested next steps: check the DPD recommended-varieties PDF directly, search seednet.gov.in with variety code A0302128, and search KrishiKosh for "Pusa Shubhra" or "BGD 128" once the search tool is available again.
