drought.details: The CSC record rates the variety as moderately resistant to drought. In a Durgapura water-stress trial, RSG963 was among the tested genotypes (with GL28151 and PDG3) that maintained higher growth, yield and yield traits, which the authors read as tolerance to water stress. A separate Durgapura experiment used RSG963 as one of two local drought-tolerant checks. The digest gives no mechanism-level data (for example root traits or osmotic adjustment) for this variety.

heat.details: No evidence found in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No evidence found in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Wilt: the Technological Options report describes good resistance; the DPD variety table rates it moderately resistant; the CSC record lists moderate resistance. Dry root rot: the Shekhawat AICRP table lists it as resistant; the DPD table rates it moderately resistant; the CSC record lists moderate resistance. Bengal gram mosaic (BGM) and collar rot: the CSC record lists moderate resistance, but no digest source attributes a BGM or collar rot rating to this variety (the Shekhawat table's BGM entries are for other varieties), so no digest-based rating is recorded. The Durgapura scheme page places the variety among those developed with a strong wilt tradition but gives no rating.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borer: the Technological Options report describes good resistance; the CSC record lists moderate resistance. Nematode: the Shekhawat AICRP table lists resistance; the CSC record lists moderate resistance. No other pest ratings were found in the digest.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 1500-2000 kg/ha. DPD table: average 16-17 q/ha (1600-1700 kg/ha). ICAR AICRP report: 19-20 q/ha under rainfed conditions. Milling study: RSG 963 is among desi varieties giving more than 20 q/ha. KVK front-line demonstration in Churu (Rajasthan, rabi 2014-15 and 2015-16): 1,374-2,000 kg/ha across entries.
agronomic_details.stability: Limited evidence. The Durgapura water-stress trial reported maintained yield under water stress. The Technological Options report says it performs well in normal-sown and rainfed conditions as well as late-sown. No multi-environment stability statistics were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for late-sown, irrigated conditions (CSC). Digest sources also describe good performance in normal-sown and rainfed conditions (Technological Options report) and rainfed conditions (ICAR report). The CSC record describes it as suitable for all conditions.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: ICAR AICRP report: semi-erect growth habit. CSC record: resistant to lodging and shattering; seed rate 60 kg/ha. Grain quality: the milling study reports it as relatively poor in grain quality for pulse millers. Other morphological characteristics: Unknown.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Durgapura water-stress trial: RSG963 maintained higher growth, yield and yield traits, read as tolerance to water stress. (2) Durgapura experiment: used as one of two local drought-tolerant checks. (3) ICAR AICRP chickpea report 2021-22: 130-135 days, semi-erect, 19-20 q/ha under rainfed conditions. (4) Milling study: more than 20 q/ha among desi varieties; relatively poor grain quality for pulse millers. (5) KVK front-line demonstration, Churu, rabi 2014-15 and 2015-16: 60 kg/ha seed rate, productivity 1,374-2,000 kg/ha across entries. (6) Seed-priming and late-sown trials: the Technological Options report says the variety was released for late-sown conditions and performs well in normal-sown and rainfed conditions; no seed-priming data were found.

commercial_info.seed_corporations: Not found in searched sources. Seed-chain strengthening by the Durgapura institute is noted, but no corporation sales were found.
commercial_info.availability_status: Not found in searched sources. The Durgapura scheme page says the institute strengthened the seed chain and distribution system to popularize RSG-963. The ICAR report records breeder seed production for 65 chickpea varieties but gives no figure for this variety. No Seednet listing was retrieved.
commercial_info.kvk: Not found in searched sources as a seed-availability record. A KVK front-line demonstration in Churu used the variety at 60 kg/ha seed rate, but this does not establish current KVK seed supply.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Aadhar (RSG-963), Chickpea (Cicer arietinum)

Name note: the CSC name is "Aadhar(RSG-963)" and the Seednet name is "AADHAR(RSG-963)". No Seednet variety page was retrieved, so every item below comes from sources that use "Aadhar (RSG 963)", "RSG-963", "Adhar" or "AADHAR (RSG-963)" in the PPV&FR compendium. Each entry names the form the source used. Searches were limited to four, so the contact and breeder items are incomplete.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Under water stress, RSG-963 was among the genotypes that kept higher growth and yield in a Durgapura trial, which the authors read as tolerance (source name: RSG963) -- Among the tested genotypes, GL28151, RSG963, PDG3 maintained higher growth, yield and yield traits showing their tolerance to water stress -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261181193_Growth_and_yield_of_chickpeaCicer_arietinum_L_genotypes_in_response_to_water_stress
- A separate study used RSG963 as one of two local drought-tolerant checks in a Durgapura experiment (source name: RSG963) -- https://pub.isprd.in/index.php/jfl/article/download/356/223/827
- Heat and salinity: No evidence found. Flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- The Technological Options report describes the variety as having a good level of resistance to wilt, dry root rot and pod borer (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296805556_Technological_options_for_increasing_pulses_production
- The DPD variety table rates it as moderately resistant to wilt and dry root rot (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- A Shekhawat (AICRP chickpea) table lists it as resistant to dry root rot and nematode, with other entries covering BGM and stunt (source name: RSG 963 (Adhar)) -- https://dokumen.pub/chickpea-gram-status-and-cultivation-technology.html
- The Durgapura scheme page lists it among varieties developed with a strong wilt tradition, but no resistance rating was given -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Chickpea.htm

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity is given as 125-130 days in the DPD table (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- The ICAR AICRP report gives 130-135 days, semi-erect growth, and a yield of 19-20 q/ha under rainfed conditions (source name: Aadhar (RSG 963)) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- The DPD table gives average yield as 16-17 q/ha (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- The milling study reports RSG 963 among desi varieties giving more than 20 q/ha (source name: RSG 963) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/74994/31515/189951
- The milling study also says RSG 963 is relatively poor in grain quality for pulse millers and recommends it over some other desi types (source name: RSG 963) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/74994/31515/189951
- A KVK front-line demonstration in Churu (Rajasthan, rabi 2014-15 and 2015-16) used RSG 963 at 60 kg/ha seed rate; productivity was reported as 1,374-2,000 kg/ha across entries (source name: RSG 963) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-4-2020/Shaukat%20Ali,%20et%20al.pdf
- Seed-priming and late-sown trials: The Technological Options report says the variety was released for late-sown conditions but also performs well in normal-sown and rainfed conditions (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/296805556_Technological_options_for_increasing_pulses_production

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage is RSG 524 × PDG 84-10 (source name: Aadhar (RSG 963)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320414296_Milling_properties_of_desi_and_kabuli_chickpea_Cicer_arietinum_varieties_released_in_India
- The same parentage appears in the Shekhawat table (source name: RSG 963) -- https://dokumen.pub/chickpea-gram-status-and-cultivation-technology.html
- Breeding method, breeding-line codes beyond RSG-963, QTL, marker and genome-resource records: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety is listed as released in 2005 by ARS Durgapura (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- The Durgapura station is now the Rajasthan Agricultural Research Institute, a constituent of Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University, Jobner (source name: RSG-963 (Adhar) in the scheme list) -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Chickpea.htm
- Lead breeder name for this variety: No evidence found. The Durgapura scheme page names Dr. S. K. Jain as in-charge of the AICRP on Chickpea, but it does not link him to this variety's breeding, so he is not recorded as breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. S. K. Jain, in-charge of the AICRP on Chickpea at RARI Durgapura (role as stated on page; not confirmed as breeder). Email and phone are shown on the page, but the number was cut off in the retrieved text and no email was legible. -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Chickpea.htm
- Institute address: Agricultural Research Station, Durgapura, Jaipur, Rajasthan - 302 018 (institute-level address from the book's front matter; no email found in legible form). -- https://dokumen.pub/chickpea-gram-status-and-cultivation-technology.html
- Official email for the variety or division: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Kaur (2023). Characterization and classification of selective Indian chickpea cultivars based on physical and hydration properties, using image and multivariate analysis. Legume Science -- https://doi.org/10.1002/leg3.168
- Authors not shown in retrieved text (year not shown). Milling properties of desi and kabuli chickpea (Cicer arietinum) varieties released in India. Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/download/74994/31515/189951
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Growth and yield of chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) genotypes in response to water stress. Full Length Research Paper -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/261181193_Growth_and_yield_of_chickpeaCicer_arietinum_L_genotypes_in_response_to_water_stress
- Shaukat Ali et al. (2020). Impact of Front Line Demonstration on Productivity and [truncated title]. IJCMAS -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-4-2020/Shaukat%20Ali,%20et%20al.pdf
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (2021-22). Annual progress report. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Shekhawat, S. S. Chickpea (Gram): Status and Cultivation Technology. Scientific Publishers (year not shown) -- https://dokumen.pub/chickpea-gram-status-and-cultivation-technology.html
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Evaluation of Genistein Content in Chickpea (Cicer arietinum). Dergipark -- https://dergipark.org.tr/tr/download/article-file/783617
- Theses (KrishiKosh) and conference papers specific to this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- The Durgapura scheme page says the institute strengthened the seed chain and distribution system to popularize RSG-963 (source name: RSG-963 (Adhar)) -- https://raridurgapura.org/Scheme-Chickpea.htm
- The ICAR report records breeder seed production for 65 chickpea varieties, but the retrieved text does not give a figure for this variety (source name: Aadhar (RSG 963)) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Seednet listing, NSC, state seed corporation, SAU sales, and private dealers: No evidence found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Rajasthan, Haryana, Punjab and Delhi (source name: Aadhar (RSG-963)) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- The NWPZ rainfed zone is also named (source name: Aadhar (RSG 963)) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/320414296_Milling_properties_of_

drought.details: The digest describes Pusa 2024 as moderately resistant to soil-borne diseases and drought (release 2008, Delhi area). It is listed alongside drought and soil-borne disease tolerance in the DPD variety table. In a restricted soil-moisture study, Pusa 2024 was among the top seed-yield performers of 12 IARI cultivars, with membrane stability and relative water content also assessed. The digest notes an inconsistency: the same study is described as a 6-kabuli-cultivar set that includes Pusa 2024, so the size of the comparison set is unclear. The input record describes the variety as tolerant to drought; the digest supports this only at the moderate level. No drought mechanism-level data were found.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to soil-borne diseases is reported in the digest (DPD tables, IARI-cited variety table, a slideshare variety deck and a Krishi Jagran summary). No pathogen-level data were found, and the digest does not name specific soil-borne pathogens. The input record states resistance to F. wilt race 4. The digest does not confirm this claim, so it is unverified here. No other disease evidence was found.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. The digest states that no specific pest, including pod borer (Helicoverpa), is named for Pusa 2024 in the retrieved text. The input record reports moderate tolerance to Helicoverpa pod borer, but the digest does not confirm it, so it is unverified here.

agronomic_details.yield: Average seed yield is reported as about 30 q/ha (Krishi Jagran and a slideshare variety deck). The DPD variety table gives 25-28 q/ha, and a secondary slide deck gives 20-25 q/ha. The input record lists average yield as Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: The digest reports Pusa 2024 as a top seed-yield performer under restricted soil moisture, and its ranking was with Pusa 1105, Pusa 1053 and BGD 72. No multi-environment stability analysis was found. Trial data are not clearly summarised across environments.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Released in 2008 for the National Capital Region of Delhi, suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions (Krishi Jagran). The DPD table describes it as suited to timely-sown irrigated rabi conditions in Delhi. A state-level table lists Pusa-2024 against a West Bengal row (values 1450, 1100 and 31.81), but the column meaning is not stated, so this is treated as unverified and is not used to infer adaptation to West Bengal. Pusa 2024 is cited in a review as a high-yielding, well-adapted kabuli variety (IARI annual report context).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: WIDE ADAPTATION, DROUGHT TOLERANCE AND STABLE HIGH YIELD; LIGHT GREEN AND BROAD LEAVES WITH ERECT GROWTH HABIT. Digest additionally reports kabuli seed type and 100-seed weight of about 30 g (Krishi Jagran).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Restricted soil-moisture trial (IJPGR): Pusa 2024 was among the top seed-yield performers of 12 IARI cultivars and ranked with Pusa 1105, Pusa 1053 and BGD 72 as superior for seed yield; the design details are inconsistent in the digest (6-kabuli set versus 12 cultivars). (2) DPD variety table: 25-28 q/ha, 145 days, timely-sown irrigated rabi, Delhi. (3) Slideshare variety deck: about 30 q/ha average yield, kabuli type. (4) Secondary slide deck: 20-25 q/ha, 140-145 days. (5) State-level table: Pusa-2024 entry for West Bengal (1450, 1100, 31.81), column meaning not stated and unverified. No AICRP or ICAR trial reports specific to Pusa 2024 were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderately resistant against soil-borne diseases and drought, release year 2008, Delhi area -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Listed alongside drought and soil-borne disease tolerance; 25-28 q/ha, 145 days, Delhi, timely-sown irrigated rabi -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Under restricted soil moisture, Pusa 2024 was among the top seed-yield performers of 12 IARI cultivars, with membrane stability and relative water content also assessed (note: the study is on a 6-kabuli-cultivar set that includes Pusa 2024) -- https://www.ispgr.in/index.php/ijpgr/article/view/1800
- Moderately resistant to soil-borne diseases (kabuli, 2008, about 30 q/ha) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/varieties-of-chickpea/87189800
- Moderately resistant to soil-borne diseases and drought, 140-145 days, 20-25 q/ha (secondary slide deck) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/pulsesbhupptppt/258972759

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to soil-borne diseases; no specific pathogen or pest (wilt, dry root rot, pod borer) named for Pusa 2024 in the retrieved text -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Same moderate soil-borne disease resistance statement in the IARI-cited variety table -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Krishi Jagran summary: moderately resistant to soil-borne diseases; no pathogen-level data -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Released 2008 for the National Capital Region of Delhi; suitable for rainfed and irrigated conditions; 100-seed weight about 30 g; average yield about 30 q/ha -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- Kabuli type; average seed yield 30 q/ha -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/varieties-of-chickpea/87189800
- Restricted-moisture trial: Pusa 2024 ranked with Pusa 1105, Pusa 1053 and BGD 72 as superior for seed yield -- https://www.ispgr.in/index.php/ijpgr/article/view/1800
- A state-level table lists "Pusa-2024" at 1450 (first column), 1100 and 31.81 for a row labelled West Bengal; the column meaning is not stated, so treat this as unverified -- http://dpd.gov.in/Chickpea.pdf
- Review: Pusa 2024 cited among high-yielding, well-adapted kabuli varieties (IARI annual report context) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9654780/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (BG 261 x ICC 88503) x (GL 920 x BG 1003) is taken from the input record only; no retrieved page confirmed it -- No evidence found
- Breeding-line code, QTL, marker or genome-resource records for Pusa 2024 -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: ICAR-Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi, per the input record; the DPD tables also list IARI, Delhi as the source -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names -- No evidence found

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder names, roles, emails, phones -- No evidence found
- Institute contact page or postal address for the IARI pulses division -- No evidence found in the retrieved results

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Evaluation of IARI chickpea cultivars including Pusa 2024 under restricted soil moisture. Indian Journal of Plant Genetic Resources (IJPGR) -- https://www.ispgr.in/index.php/ijpgr/article/view/1800
- Authors not retrieved (year not retrieved). Chickpea (Cicer arietinum L.) Biology and Biotechnology: From Domestication to Biofortification and Biopharming (review; Pusa 2024 mentioned in passing) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9654780/
- No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis, or field-trial paper specifically on Pusa 2024 was retrieved -- No evidence found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Private dealer listing: "Pusa 2024" offered as chickpea (gram) seed, 40 kg packs, minimum order 10 bags (not an official source; not verified) -- https://www.prdf-agri.com/product-page/chickpea-gram-seeds-3-varieties-available
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or seednet.gov.in listing -- No evidence found

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Delhi (NCR), per the 2008 release description and DPD tables -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/improving-chickpea-productivity-by-breaking-unholy-alliance-between-seed-size-yield/
- The input record says "Unknown"; no other state recommendation was found -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf

SEARCH NOTE
- Four searches were run (variety, breeder/institution, research, seed). The "Pusa 2024" name is generic and most results were on other chickpea varieties, so the breeder, contact, QTL and official seed-source fields remain empty. The seednet portal record (variety code A0302179) was not retrieved.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: LAM SHANAYA (LBeG 7), Chickpea

Name check: The CSC/DPD sources use "Lam shanaya (LBeG 7)", and the Seednet name is the same, so one name covers both. The seednet_crop_name "Bengal gram" was searched as chickpea. Seednet itself was not reached in these searches. Only four searches were run, so the seed-availability and contact results are thin.

Release year conflict: DPD tables give 2007 and the ICAR-IIPR AICRP report gives 2006. The brief says 2006.

Parentage conflict: The brief gives (ICCL 81101 x ICCC 32) x (ICCC 49 x FLIP 82-K) x ICCV 3. The AICRP report fragment reads "ICCL 8001" with "x ICCC 32", which does not match "ICCL 81101". The full pedigree could not be verified.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Tolerant to wilt and root rot complex, rainfed conditions, per DPD recommended-variety tables -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- Same tolerance (wilt and rot) recorded in the AICRP chickpea report entry for Lam Shanaya -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found for this variety. The drought-tolerance text in the AICRP report belongs to another line (ICC 4958 source), so it was discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Tolerant to wilt and rot condition (listed in DPD tables; see stress entry above) -- https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pest resistance (pod borer, bruchid, YMV, MYMV, ascochyta blight): No evidence found for this variety. Pest and disease text found in the searches was about other varieties and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity about 90 days and yield 20-25 q/ha, rainfed, per DPD tables -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- Early kabuli type (plant 40-60 cm, pearly white bold seed) with 2006 release, listed in a short-duration chickpea technology page -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281025_Short-Duration_Chickpea_Technology_Enabling_Legumes_Revolution_in_Andhra_Pradesh_India
- Large-seeded class (30-40 g) with LBeG 7 named as an example -- https://tropicallegumeshub.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/ChickpeaManual_full.pdf
- Large-seeded class (31-45 g/100 seed) with LBeG 7 named among examples -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313852048_An_overview_of_chickpea_improvement_research_program_in_Ethiopia
- Multi-location yield trial data: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage (as given in the AICRP report fragment): "(ICCL 8001 ... x ICCC 32)"; this conflicts with the brief -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Source/breeding line listed as ICCV 96329 (kabuli, ICRISAT/ANGRAU, 2006) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281025_Short-Duration_Chickpea_Technology_Enabling_Legumes_Revolution_in_Andhra_Pradesh_India
- Breeding method, breeding-line codes, QTL/markers, genome resources for this variety: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by ANGRAU, Regional Agricultural Research Station (RARS), Lam, Guntur -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf (also https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf)
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute contact (email, phone, postal address, or contact page for ANGRAU RARS Lam): No evidence found in these searches. Search the ANGRAU website for RARS Lam, Guntur-34.
- Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not stated in retrieved page (Year not stated). Short-Duration Chickpea Technology: Enabling Legumes Revolution in Andhra Pradesh, India. ResearchGate (listing of LBeG 7 release data) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/281281025_Short-Duration_Chickpea_Technology_Enabling_Legumes_Revolution_in_Andhra_Pradesh_India
- Asnake Fikre (2014). An overview of chickpea improvement research program in Ethiopia. Legume Perspectives, Issue 3 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313852048_An_overview_of_chickpea_improvement_research_program_in_Ethiopia
- ICAR-AICRP on Chickpea (year not stated; report period 2021-22). Annual progress report, PC report on chickpea. ICAR-IIPR -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf
- Tropical Legumes Hub. Chickpea Seed Production Manual. Tropical Legumes Hub -- https://tropicallegumeshub.com/wp-content/uploads/2020/07/ChickpeaManual_full.pdf
- KrishiKosh theses and peer-reviewed papers on this variety: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY

RECOMMENDED STATES

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Gram-226 (JG-226), Chickpea
Names: variety_name "Jawahar Gram-226 (JG-226)"; seednet_variety_name "JAWAHAR GRAM-226 (JG-226)". No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so all evidence below refers to the variety name as written in the release listings. Release year: the user record says 2006, but the DPD release tables give 2007 (see RECOMMENDED STATES).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as resistant to wilt and root rot complex, rainfed Madhya Pradesh, released 2007 by JNKVV -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Same DPD listing, alternate copy: resistant to wilt and root rot complex -- http://dpd.gov.in/Varieties/Chickpea%20varieties.pdf
- No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data specific to JG-226 were found. The ICAR-IIPR 2021-22 AICRP report's drought and abiotic-stress text refers to other varieties (GJGK 1617 and a variety derived from ICC 4958), not JG-226 -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf (discarded for JG-226)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to wilt and root rot complex (see STRESS TOLERANCE) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf
- Seed-borne mycoflora study screened 30 chickpea varieties including JG 226; the snippet gives no JG-226-specific fungal results -- https://www.ijcmas.com/abstractview.php?ID=15146&vol=8-11-2019&SNo=52
- Pulse beetle (Callosobruchus chinensis) study: JG 226 not among the varieties with reported infestation values in the snippet; the snippet names other JG lines only -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/368607274_Study_the_germination_percentage_of_chickpea_seeds_infested_by_pulse_beetle_Callosobruchus_chinensis_under_laboratory_condition (not used for JG-226)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield 20-22 q/ha, 112-115 days maturity, rainfed MP (DPD release table) -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf ; https://dpd.gov.in/VARIETIES-Website.pdf
- Pharma Innovation Journal 2023 (vol 12, issue 9, pp 603-607) cultivar trial: JG-226 recorded the lowest seed protein (19.42%) among the ten cultivars tested; the table gives stover yield of 1922 kg/ha -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2023/vol12issue9/PartE/12-8-480-502.pdf
- Asian Jr. of Microbiol. Biotech. Env. Sc. (2023) biofertilizer trial, JG-226 treatment: 50% flowering at 56.33 days, 100-seed weight 20.2 g, seed yield 1052.86 kg/ha, straw 1303.1 kg/ha -- https://www.envirobiotechjournals.com/AJMBES/VOL2512023/AJ-11.pdf
- Listed among varieties in the ICAR AICRP Chickpea 2021-22 report (no JG-226 trial values in the snippet) -- https://www.icar-iipr.org.in/wp-content/uploads/2023/07/PC-report-Chickpea_2021-22.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage JG-74 x JG-315 was NOT confirmed for JG-226 in any result. The JG-74 x JG-315 pairing is not stated for JG-226 anywhere in the evidence. No parentage evidence found.
- Results on JG 74 and JG 315 (for example, the Fusarium wilt MABC work on JG 74 with WR 315 donor, and JG 315 as a selection from line P 315) concern other varieties and were not attributed to JG-226 -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6308216
- No QTL, marker, breeding-line code, or genome-resource data for JG-226 were found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: J.N. Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, Madhya Pradesh, per the DPD release listing -- https://dpd.gov.in/i)%20Chickpea%20Varieties.pdf

seednet_fields.Parentage:
It is developed from a cross between widely adopted annigeri variety and ICC 4958.
The cross was made at ICRISAT for incorporating good rooting traits of ICC 4958 into widely adopted Annigeri variety and the advance breeding lines were sent to RARS, Nandral.  Promising selection was identified at RARS, Nandyal for high yield with bold and attractive seeds.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Rabi season and in all chickpea growing districts of Andhra Pradesh.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: NBeG 49 has not responded to application of higher doses of N. Recommended fertilizers are 20 kg N and 50 kg P2Os per ha.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: Semi spreading and medium in height, green stem with anthocyanin pigmentation on the stem, pink flowers with medium sized leaf lets and pods.  Seeds medium bold, angular, brown colour seeds with rough testa with uniform size.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Performs well compared to JG11 under receding moisture conditions.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: At RARS, Nandyal during 2013-14 to 2015 16, NBeG 49 is found be on par with resistant check JG 315 with respect to its reaction to Fusarium wilt and dry root rot. In All India Coordinated trials (AVT I of 2011-12), it recorded resistant reaction to Fusarium wilt in one location and moderately resistant reaction in one location out of 14 locations tested. It also recorded resistant reaction to collar rot, in one location out of 5 locations tested.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: NBeG 49 is on par with tolerant check ICCL 86111 in its reaction to Helicoverpa.
seednet_fields.Fertiliser Dosage (Kg/Ha): 20 kg N and 50 kg P per ha. (50 kg urea and 300 kg SSP or 125 kg DAP at the final preparation of field).

seednet_fields.Parentage: THE VARIETY WAS ISOLATED AS A SINGLE PLANT SELECTION FROM GENETIC  VARIABILITY SYSTEM IN THE PARENT VARIETY PUSA PHALGUNI WITH CHEMICAL MUTAGENS.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR FRLEASE AND CULTIVATION  FOR NORTH WESTERN PLANTS OF CENTRAL AND PEN-NINSULAR ZONE OF INDIA. ASLO RECOMMENDED FOR ALL TYPE OF SOIL STRUCTURES ( SANDY,LOAM AND CLAY), HOWEVER, IT MANIFESTOS BETTER YIELDS POTENTIAL IN RICH SANDYLOAM SOI
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: THOUGH THE VARIETY V-240 IS INDETERMINATE, IT PRODUCES FEW TRAILING BRANCHES UNDER OPTIMUM CONDITIONS. THE TRAILING BRANCHES ARE CONTIONUSLY MORE UNDER EXCESS WATER SUPPLY, IT RESPONDS WELL TO 20-25 KG N AND 50 KG P2O5/HA
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : TALL (60-70 CM EXCLUDING TRAILING BRANCHES) B. DISINGUISHING MORPHOLOGICAL CHARACTERS (I) GROWTH HABIT : TALL, INDETERMINATE GROWTH, WITH TRAILING BRANCHES PRODUCED UNDER HIGH WATER SUPPLY. (II) LEAF CHARACTERS SHAPE : BROAD TRIFOLIATE LEAF, COLOUR : DARK- GREEN, PUBESCENCE/GLABROUS : GLABROUS, WAXY/NON-WAXY : NON  WAXY (III) STEM : STEM THICK AND ANGULAR, GREEN (IV) FLOWER STRUCTRE : STANTARD AND WINGS HAVAING PURPLE STREAKS, KEEL LIGHT YELLOW. (V) POD : 1-3 POD/PEDUNCLE, MEDIUM SIZE (10-15 CM), STRAIGHT AND DROOPING TYPE. (VI)  SEED : BOLD (96G/1000 SEEDS), UNIFORM RED. LY
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: TOLERANT TO MOISTURE STRESS
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: MOST SERIOUS DISEASES IN NORTH-WESTERN AND SOUTHERN PARTS OF INDIA IS YELLOW MOSAIC VIRUS (YMV). IN CO-ORDINATED PATHOLOGY TRIALS, THE YMV INFECTION IN V-20 AS WELL AS IN THE SHECKS ( C-152 & V-16) WAS SIMILAR AT COIMBATORE. THE PERCENTAGE OF INFECTION IN V-240 RANGES BETWEEEN 3.7- 20.8% WHEREAS C-152 THE ESTABLISHED YMV RESISTANT VARIETY, HAD INFECTION IN THE RANGE OF 6.6-19.0. V-240 HAS SHOWN COMPLETE RESISTANCE TO YMV IN CENTRAL PART OF INDIA. THE PROPOSED VARIETY ASLO DISPLAY BETTER RESISTANCE TO BACTERIAL BLIGHT IS COMPARED TO THE CHEEKS AT ALL THE LOCATIONS EXCEPT DURGAPURA, WHICH WAS AT PAR. V-240 HAS ALSO SHOWN A GREATER RESISTANCE TO TIP BLIGHT, ANTHROCNOSE AND MACROPHOMIA BLIGHT AS COMPARED TO THE CHECKS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: IN THE ENTOMOLOGICAL TRIALS CONDUCTED DURING 1982-83, THE SEED DAMAGE CAUSED BY THE POD BORER IN V-240 WAS SLIGHTLY LESS (1.2-5%) THAN IN C-152 (1.7-6.5%) AND V-16 (1.0-8.2%)

disease_resistance.summary: Variety record (ground truth, not corroborated by retrieved sources): yellow mosaic virus (YMV) was the most serious disease in north-western and southern India. In co-ordinated pathology trials at Coimbatore, V-240 showed 3.7-20.8% YMV infection versus 6.6-19.0% for the resistant check C-152, and V-240 showed complete resistance to YMV in central India. V-240 showed better resistance to bacterial blight than the checks at all locations except Durgapura, where it was at par. It also showed greater resistance than the checks to tip blight, anthracnose and macrophomina blight. Digest-retrieved evidence: Boukar et al. (2018) list a 'V240 India 1984' cultivar developed by DMS mutagenesis with high yield and resistance to fungal, viral and bacterial diseases. This is a review table entry, not a field-trial report, and its 1984 date differs from the 1993 release year, so it is unverified for this variety. Its citation is inconsistent in the digest: it is attributed to researchgate 336354732 in the disease and genetics sections, while the publications section attributes the DMS table to researchgate 325061470.

pest_resistance.summary: Variety record (ground truth, not corroborated by retrieved sources): in entomological trials conducted in 1982-83, seed damage by pod borer in V-240 was slightly lower (1.2-5%) than in C-152 (1.7-6.5%) and V-16 (1.0-8.2%). No digest source independently confirms this.

agronomic_details.adaptation: Variety record (ground truth): recommended for cultivation in the north-western plains of the central and peninsular zones of India. Also recommended for all soil types (sandy, loam and clay), with better yield potential in rich sandy loam soil. Responds well to 20-25 kg N and 50 kg P2O5/ha.

agronomic_details.field_trials: No yield, maturity or multi-location field trial data for V-240 were found in the digest. The only quantitative result retrieved is a seed-protein compositional study (not a field trial) in which V-240 had total protein of 25.6% versus 26.0% for the check CS-88. The variety record separately reports co-ordinated pathology trials at Coimbatore (YMV infection 3.7-20.8% in V-240 versus 6.6-19.0% in C-152) and 1982-83 entomological trials (pod borer seed damage 1.2-5% in V-240 versus 1.7-6.5% in C-152 and 1.0-8.2% in V-16). These come from the variety record and are not corroborated by the digest.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Boukar et al. (2018) list a "V240 India 1984" cultivar developed by DMS mutagenesis, with main attributes given as high yield and resistance to fungal, viral and bacterial diseases -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336354732_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_Breeding. This is a table entry in a review, not a field-trial report, and its 1984 date differs from the 1993 release year. Treat it as unverified for this variety until checked against the original release notification.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The V-240 check was used in a seed-protein study, with total protein of 25.6% reported for V-240 versus 26.0% for CS-88 -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s12298-010-0007-9. No yield, maturity or multi-location trial data for V-240 were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- The user-supplied parentage (single-plant selection from the mutagenised Pusa Phalguni population) was not confirmed by any search result. The only mutagen-origin evidence is the DMS entry in https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336354732_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_Breeding. No QTL, marker or gene data for V-240 were found. Electrophoretic and marker characterisation of V-240 appears in https://www.researchgate.net/publication/269742026_Cowpea_Vigna_unguiculata_L_Walp_seed_proteins_Heterogeneity_in_total_proteins_and_protein_fractions, but this is biochemical profiling only.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: UPC-607 (Cowpea)

Name check: the CSC release name (variety_name) and the Seednet name (seednet_variety_name) are both "UPC-607", so every search covered one name. Searches run: 4 (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed availability). Only two results name UPC 607, and neither is a primary record for it.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches on drought, heat, salinity, flood, and submergence returned no page that names UPC 607. The results were general cowpea pages and a Pantnagar grain-cowpea paper about other varieties.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The only pest and disease material returned was about other Pantnagar lines (Pant Lobia series, UPC 628) and was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found. The Phytojournal 2019 paper (grain cowpea nutritional comparison) concerns Pant Lobia/PGCP lines, not UPC 607. Discarded. -- https://www.phytojournal.com/archives/2019/vol8issue5S/PartH/SP-8-5-12-110.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "(L 212 x Singapore)-48-2-9" is from the input record only; no search result confirms it. No QTL, marker, or genome study names UPC 607. The genome and transcriptome papers returned refer to IT97K-499-35, IT86D-1010, and other lines, so they were discarded. -- https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/518969.full.pdf (discarded: different genotype)

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution per the input record: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology (GBPUAT), Pantnagar. Lead breeder: No evidence found.
Name-listing evidence: UPC 607 appears in a list of cowpea varieties in a slideshare presentation. The snippet does not show the category or the breeding institution for UPC 607. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshare/cowpea-88527040/88527040
Pantnagar release list: UPC 607 appears in the Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding list of varieties released to June 2023. The snippet is truncated and does not state the crop category, so it is not treated as confirmed. -- https://www.gbpuat.ac.in/colleges/COA/D7/08.06.2023_Varieties_Released.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No institute email, phone, or contact-page URL for UPC 607 was returned. The only address on record is the one given in the input: G.B. Pant University of Agriculture and Technology, Pantnagar-263 145, Distt. Udham Singh Nagar. This is an input-supplied address, not a search finding, and no phone or email was verified.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, AICRP report, or KrishiKosh thesis names UPC 607. The GBPUAT AICRP vegetable crops report (https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/13%20AICRP%20-%20VEGETABLE%20CROPS.pdf) mentions Pantnagar cowpea work in general terms only, so it is not listed as evidence for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. The seed-supplier results were US and commercial cowpea sellers and do not name UPC 607. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or Seednet listing was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The input record says "Unknown". The ICAR 2010 notice on recommended states covers UPC 628, a different forage variety, so it was not used.
Note: the Pantnagar release list and the slideshare entry are the only sources naming UPC 607. Both are truncated or lack detail, so the crop category, release year, and recommended states still need checking against the CSC release minutes and the Seednet record (https://seednet.gov.in).

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
IT-38956-1 (CSC name) and IT-38956-1 (Seednet name) are identical, so every heading below refers to the same name. The evidence is thin. Four searches returned only secondary mentions of the variety, and none of the official Seednet, ICAR, or UAS Bengaluru pages were found.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data for IT-38956-1. Generic cowpea drought-tolerance pages were discarded because they do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No resistance data for this variety was returned. A seed-storage study on IT-38956-1 treated seed with neem-based products against storage damage, which is seed protection and not varietal resistance. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue10/PartS/10-9-307-864.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- A Cowpea 12 slide deck lists IT-38956-1 among major Indian varieties and gives a yield figure of 12.5 q/ha, without trial details or location. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/cowpea-12/64120107
A dryland study of 14 cowpea genotypes in early and late kharif found that IT-38956-1, KBC-1, KBC-2 and TVX-944-02E performed better across both seasons and suited double cropping. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292584817_Genetic_variability_and_character_association_studies_in_cowpea_in_early_and_late_kharif_seasons
The same study reported that yield traits were mainly governed by additive gene action. This applies to the 14-genotype trial as a whole, not specifically to IT-38956-1. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292584817_Genetic_variability_and_character_association_studies_in_cowpea_in_early_and_late_kharif_seasons

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage "introduction from IITA, Nigeria" comes only from the supplied record. No search result confirmed it. No QTL, marker, genome, or breeding-method evidence was found for IT-38956-1. The IITA genome and transcriptome papers returned by the search concern IT97K-499-35 and IT86D-1010, which are different lines, so they were discarded. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found for a named breeder of IT-38956-1. The search returned IITA cowpea breeders (Boukar, Kano) and other programmes, but these are not linked to this variety and were discarded. The institution recorded for the variety is UAS GKVK, Bangalore. A 2021 study says its seed was obtained from the AICRP-NSP (Crops) at UAS Bangalore, which supports a UAS Bangalore link. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue10/PartS/10-9-307-864.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page for IT-38956-1, UAS GKVK Bangalore, or the AICRP-NSP (Crops) unit was returned by the searches. The only contact details seen (an IITA breeder address and email) belong to a different programme and were excluded.

PUBLICATIONS --
Authors not stated in the search snippet (2021). Study on the influence of neem-based azadirachtin products on seed storability of cowpea variety IT-38956-1. The Pharma Innovation Journal 10(10): 1261-1263 -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue10/PartS/10-9-307-864.pdf
Authors not stated in the search snippet (year not stated). Genetic variability and character association studies in cowpea in early and late kharif seasons. Journal/report not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/292584817_Genetic_variability_and_character_association_studies_in_cowpea_in_early_and_late_kharif_seasons
Note: the two items above are listed from the snippets only; authors, journal and year must be checked on the source pages before use.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Seed of IT-38956-1 was obtained from the AICRP-NSP (Crops) at UAS Bangalore for a 2021 study. This does not show current sale. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, or private dealer listing for this variety was found. -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2021/vol10issue10/PartS/10-9-307-864.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES -- Karnataka. A DPD publication lists IT-38956-1 for Karnataka alongside KBC-2, PKB-4 and PKB-6. -- http://dpd.gov.in/Cowpea.PDF
The same Karnataka recommendation appears on a farm-advisory site. -- https://krishisewa.com/crop-cultivation/cultivation-of-multi-purpose-crop-cowpea/

RELEASE AND MATURITY (not a requested heading, recorded for completeness) -- The 2006 release year, CSC notification, and maturity were not confirmed by any search result. The "Recommended states: Unknown" field can be updated to Karnataka, based on the DPD source above.

seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: The proposed variety HC 98-46 has been found consistently least susceptible to both leafhopper and white fly. No bruchid infestation was observed in the field conditions in this genotype.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Ganga-8 (Gangotri) / GANGA-8 (GANGOTRI), green gram (mung)

SEARCH STATUS: Three searches ran. A fourth was attempted but the tool-call limit was reached, so seed-availability and contact searches were not completed. The search results were also not stored, so I could only review the short excerpts printed in the first batch. The records below are therefore incomplete, and no finding can be confirmed for this variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The release-list search returned no stress-tolerance text naming Ganga-8 in the excerpts I reviewed.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The only disease-related excerpt was for a different variety, "Gg 8" from TNAU Coimbatore (resistant to YMV, released 2015). That is a different variety and is discarded. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No trial or yield data naming this variety was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage given in the input (K-851 x Pusa-105) is from the input record only and is not confirmed by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found naming a breeder for this variety. The institution-level page returned is for the Agricultural Research Station, Sriganganagar, a zonal centre under Rajasthan Agricultural University. It describes the station's remit for the Irrigated North Western Plain Zone (1b) but does not mention Ganga-8 in the excerpt I reviewed. -- https://raubikaner.org/ars-sriganganagar/

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. The station page was returned, but no email, phone, or postal address appeared in the excerpt I reviewed. The page should be opened directly to check its contact section.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The research search returned only unrelated results (for example, a paper on the Ganga and Yamuna rivers), which are discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Not searched (search limit reached). No evidence collected.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The input lists "Unknown". The central/state mungbean release list PDF (https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf) is a lead worth checking manually for a Ganga-8 row with its recommended zone and state, but the excerpt I saw did not show that row.

NEXT STEPS FOR A HUMAN REVIEWER: Open the dpd.gov.in mungbean PDF and search for "Ganga" to confirm the release year, zone, and yield. Check the RAU Bikaner and ARS Sriganganagar contact pages directly. Search seednet.gov.in for variety code A0305029. Search KrishiKosh and the AICRP on MULLaRP annual reports for "Ganga-8" for papers and trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Trombay Pesara (TM 96-2), Green gram (mung)

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are identical ("Trombay Pesara(TM 96-2)"), so one set of searches covered both. The sources also use "TM-96-2" and "TM 96-2". Release year: the input says 2006, but the DPD and IANCAS sources give 2007. Seednet was not reached in these searches, so no Seednet-specific evidence was found.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. Searches 1 and 3 returned only general green gram statements, which were not used. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf (search returned variety table only)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to powdery mildew, and listed as resistant to Corynespora leaf spot. -- https://www.iancas.org.in/bulletins/41_oct07.pdf
- Powdery mildew resistance is listed for this variety in the DPD central-release table. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- Powdery mildew resistance is also listed for TM-96-2 in a general list of green gram varieties. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/green-gram-245042946/245042946
- Not used: the IANCAS and ResearchGate pages mention Pm1 and Pm2 genes, but they do not tie these genes to TM-96-2, so they are excluded. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236889514_Mutation_experiments_and_recent_accomplishments_in_Trombay_groundnuts

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 65-70 days, and yield 9-10 q/ha, per the DPD central-release table. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- The same maturity and yield values appear in a commercial farming guide, which is a secondary source. -- https://tractorkarvan.com/blog/green-gram-farming-in-india
- The IANCAS bulletin gives a table with M: 69-73 and Y: 1250, with the column meanings unclear. Treat these as unverified. -- https://www.iancas.org.in/bulletins/41_oct07.pdf
- Suitable for rice-fallow and rabi/summer cultivation. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- No evidence found for multi-location trial data specific to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: Kopergaon x TARM-2. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Greengram.pdf
- Breeding method: No evidence found. The ANGRAU table lists the method for TM 96-2 only in truncated form.
- Breeding-line code and genome resources: No evidence found beyond the TM-96-2 designation.
- Excluded: the ANGRAU LGG 127 and LGG 407 entries are mutant varieties, and these are not this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developed by BARC, Mumbai, and ANGRAU, Lam. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- The BARC Trombay crop-variety bulletin lists TM-96-2 (Trombay Pesara) as a Trombay-released crop variety. -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found in any search result.
- ANGRAU's Regional Agricultural Research Station, Lam, is the institution named in the input. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Greengram.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, role, email and phone: No evidence found.
- Institute address and phone for RARS Lam or BARC: No evidence found.
- Institute contact page URL: No evidence found in these searches. The ANGRAU crop-variety PDF is the closest official source for the institute. -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Greengram.pdf

PUBLICATIONS
- Editorial (Tomar, B.S., Ed.) (2007). Editorial, IANCAS Bulletin Vol. VI No. 4, November 2007. IANCAS Bulletin -- https://www.iancas.org.in/bulletins/41_oct07.pdf
- Trombay Crop Varieties: Released and Notified by the Government of India (BARC bulletin, undated, author not given). BARC -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf
- No evidence found for a peer-reviewed paper, AICRP or ICAR annual report entry, KrishiKosh thesis, or QTL/marker study specific to this variety.
- Excluded: the KrishiKosh wilt-of-green-gram thesis lists Trombay Pesara only in a general cultivar list, so it is not evidence about this variety. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/a086eb5b-d8d0-4f04-bb2a-36804e187055/content

SEED AVAILABILITY
- A private seed company's product page lists "Green Gram (LGG-460, TM-96-2)". The label mixes two varieties, so treat this listing with caution. -- https://www.swastikseeds.com/greengram.php
- NSC, State Seed Corporation, SAU, KVK and Seednet seed-availability records: No evidence found. A fourth search for seed availability returned no results.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Andhra Pradesh, listed under state-wise recommended pulse varieties (2007). -- https://dpd.gov.in/1.%20Final%20State-wise%20within%2010%20Yrs.%20Pulses%20(Compile).pdf
- Andhra Pradesh, as a state-released variety for rabi and summer seasons and rice fallows. -- https://www.dpd.gov.in/iii)%20Mungbean%20varieties.pdf
- The input's recommended_states_raw ("Unknown") is superseded by these entries.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: OBGG-52 (green gram / mung bean)

Name note: The CSC release name and the Seednet name are both "OBGG-52." I found no Seednet portal page for it, so the Seednet-name evidence below comes from other sources. The PPV&FR registration compendium lists it as a registered variety, which is the closest official record.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- OBGG-52 was scored as resistant in a mungbean yellow mosaic virus screen, where it was used as a check variety. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/8354daf7-d1d9-46cd-857a-b653c3432282/content
- OBGG-52 was one of the checks in a powdery mildew tolerance marker study, but the snippet gives no resistance score for it. -- https://www.arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4472
- Drought and heat: No evidence found for OBGG-52 specifically. The only drought statement I found is a general one about the crop, not about this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
- OBGG-52 was rated resistant to mungbean yellow mosaic virus in the Odisha marker-validation study. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/8354daf7-d1d9-46cd-857a-b653c3432282/content
- Whitefly, Cercospora, Macrophomina and other pests: No evidence found for OBGG-52.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In an Angul district trial, OBGG 52 recorded the highest seed yield of 13.6 q/ha among the tested varieties. -- http://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/9_427-430.pdf
- That trial compared OBGG 52 with OUM 11-5, IPM 02-14, Pant M-5, TARM 1 and a local variety, Kala mung. -- http://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/9_427-430.pdf
- A separate multi-genotype field trial at KVK Puri and Centre for Pulse Research, Berhampur recorded OBGG-52 at 870 kg/ha. -- https://www.arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4472
- Another mungbean accession trial, using material from the Centre for Pulses Research, Berhampur, was conducted at KVK Sakhigopal, Puri and at field station EB-1, Bhubaneswar. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/8354daf7-d1d9-46cd-857a-b653c3432282/content

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: The SDS-PAGE study lists OBGG-52 as a mutant of K-851 (EMS at 0.375%), developed at OUAT. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274252126_Estimation_of_Seed_Storage_Protein_and_Molecular_Weight_Determination_in_Micro_Mutant_Lines_of_Green_Gram_Vigna_radiate_L_Wilczek_by_SDS-_PAGE
- Breeding method: OBGG 52 seed was treated with gamma rays, EMS, NG and MH, and progenies were evaluated over M3 to M5 generations in 2009-10. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/30319
- Twelve OBGG 52 mutant cultures showed significantly higher yield than the parent. -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/30319
- Breeding lines derived from it: The thesis lists V2-series mutants described as mutants of OPBGG-52 (NG and EMS treatments), and crosses such as OBGG-52 X Pant-M-4 and OBGG-52 X Kendrapada. -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/867ec82f-6ae7-4cec-a59f-1726771d209b/content
- Combining ability: OBGG-52 was among the best general combiners in an F2 cross study. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4803
- Genome resources: No evidence found for OBGG-52 genome, QTL or marker-trait associations beyond the MYMV and powdery mildew marker papers.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: OUAT's pulse programme has OBGG-56 and OBGG-58 proposed for SVRC release; the same page does not name OBGG-52. -- https://ouat.nic.in/collegeofagriculture
- Developer named in the variety record: OUAT is listed as the developing institution in the SDS-PAGE study. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274252126_Estimation_of_Seed_Storage_Protein_and_Molecular_Weight_Determination_in_Micro_Mutant_Lines_of_Green_Gram_Vigna_radiate_L_Wilczek_by_SDS-_PAGE
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level page only: OUAT College of Agriculture, Bhubaneswar -- https://ouat.nic.in/collegeofagriculture (no email, phone, or address for the Centre for Pulses Research was found in the search results).
- Centre for Pulses Research, OUAT, Berhampur (address from submission): P.O. Krupasindhupur via Nimakhandi, Dist. Ganjam, Odisha 761 001 -- from the supplied record; not verified by a web source.
- Breeder email/phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Das, T. R. & Baisakh, B. (2026). Efficacy of physical and chemical mutagenic treatments for developing superior mutants in greengram (Vigna radiata). Indian Journal of Agricultural Sciences 83(6) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IJAgS/article/view/30319 (year as printed on the page)
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Studies on yield and stress tolerance in greengram. OUAT thesis, KrishiKosh -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/867ec82f-6ae7-4cec-a59f-1726771d209b/content
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Identification and validation of molecular markers for MYMV. OUAT thesis, KrishiKosh -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/8354daf7-d1d9-46cd-857a-b653c3432282/content
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Genetic Diversity Analysis and Validation of Microsatellite Markers Linked with Tolerance to Powdery Mildew Disease in Mungbean. Legume Research -- https://www.arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4472
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Combining Ability Studies for Seed Yield and Its Quantitative Traits in F2 Crosses of Mungbean. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-4803
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Evaluation of growth and yield parameters of green gram. Research journal -- http://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/9_427-430.pdf
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Estimation of Seed Storage Protein and Molecular Weight Determination in Micro Mutant Lines of Green Gram by SDS-PAGE -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/274252126_Estimation_of_Seed_Storage_Protein_and_Molecular_Weight_Determination_in_Micro_Mutant_Lines_of_Green_Gram_Vigna_radiate_L_Wilczek_by_SDS-_PAGE

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Odisha State Seeds Corporation: OBGG-52 is listed among moong varieties in the Odisha State Seeds Corporation availability list. -- https://ossc.nic.in/Marketing/AvailabilityofSeeds
- Odisha seed distribution report: The report gives a moong requirement and availability table in which OBGG-52 shows a shortfall. -- https://pc.odisha.gov.in/sites/default/files/2020-03/7.Seed_Distribution_System.pdf (the table's district and year are unclear)
- Seednet portal listing: No evidence found.
- KVK, SAU and private dealers: No evidence found for OBGG-52.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- OBGG 52 is listed as a rabi green gram variety for Odisha. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/pulses-in-odisha/green-gram/
- Registration and notification record: The PPV&FR compendium lists OBGG-52 as Reg. No. 50 of 2009, Crop: Green gram, Category: Public, with the certificate dated 16/04/09. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf (the botanical name field in this entry is garbled in the extract)
- Other state recommendations: No evidence found. The supplied field "Unknown" was not resolved.

Discarded: a Seednet-style "OBGG-52 (Durga)" mention appears in a single slideshow and is unverified; I did not attribute it. OBGG-56 and OBGG-58 results were excluded because they name other varieties.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for Maru Kulthi-1 / Maru Kulthi (Seednet: MARU KULTHI-1) returned no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data. Crop-level horse gram pages that mention stress tolerance were discarded because they do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for variety-specific agronomy or multi-location trials. The CAZRI adaptation paper below discusses horse gram for arid Rajasthan in general, and its text does not tie trial results to this variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289335335_ADAPTATION_AND_SELECTION_OF_CROP_VARIETIES_FOR_HOT_ARID_CLIMATE_OF_RAJASTHAN

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
No evidence found in search results. The parentage recorded in the input ("selection of plants from germplasm entry collected from Pali-Marwar region") comes from the supplied record, not from any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution: Central Arid Zone Research Institute (CAZRI), Jodhpur, per the input record. A CAZRI-affiliated author (V. K. Manga) appears on a paper about variety adaptation and selection for hot arid Rajasthan that lists Maru Kulthi as a 1989 release. No search result names the breeder or lead scientist for Maru Kulthi-1, so no breeder is attributed here. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289335335_ADAPTATION_AND_SELECTION_OF_CROP_VARIETIES_FOR_HOT_ARID_CLIMATE_OF_RAJASTHAN

CONTACT DETAILS
No evidence found. No official email, phone, postal address or CAZRI contact page specific to this variety was returned. Institute-level contact details were not found in the results either.

PUBLICATIONS
Manga, V. K. (year not captured). Adaptation and Selection of Crop Varieties for Hot Arid Climate of Rajasthan. Central Arid Zone Research Institute, Jodhpur. The text names Maru Kulthi in its reference list with the note "Released in 1989 for all India", so the variety is only mentioned, not studied. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/289335335_ADAPTATION_AND_SELECTION_OF_CROP_VARIETIES_FOR_HOT_ARID_CLIMATE_OF_RAJASTHAN
Review on medicinal and traditional importance of horse gram (authors and year not captured). Journal not captured. Its variety table lists "Maru kulthi" with Rajasthan as the place of release. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366698009_Review_on_medicinal_and_traditional_importance_of_horse_gram
No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or QTL study specific to this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for Maru Kulthi-1 was returned. The Roys Farm growing guide lists "Maru Kulthi-1" among varieties but does not sell it. -- https://www.roysfarm.com/growing-horse-gram/
Retail horse gram listings (Amazon, eBay, tradeindia, others) are generic or unrelated and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Rajasthan: a review table lists "Maru kulthi" under Rajasthan as its place of release. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/366698009_Review_on_medicinal_and_traditional_importance_of_horse_gram
Rajasthan: a horse gram blog lists "Marukulti 1" among Rajasthan varieties. -- https://www.agrifarming.in/horse-gram-seed-germination-and-sowing-a-full-guide
Conflict: the CAZRI paper says "Released in 1989 for all India". The Seednet recommended-states field is "Unknown". The Odisha pulses page lists Maru Kulthi-1 in a general variety list with no state assignment, so it was not used. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/pulses-in-odisha/horse-gram/

MATURITY, YIELD AND OTHER TRAITS
No evidence found for maturity or yield of this variety.

NAME NOTE
CSC release name: Maru Kulthi-1. Seednet name: MARU KULTHI-1. Search results use "Maru Kulthi" and "Maru kulthi-1", and all matches above refer to this variety. Searches run: 4 (the maximum).

drought.details: The digest describes CRIDA 18R as a drought-tolerant selection for rainfed South India. In a Vellore on-farm trial it was reported as more promising under drought than the local check. The digest gives no physiological mechanisms and no quantitative drought data. The Croptrust item lists recent varieties with improved stress resistance but gives no variety-specific data, so it is not used to set the level. The 2021 review refers to CRIDA 18-R and related lines for stress resilience without variety-specific data. The level is medium because the evidence is qualitative and from one on-farm comparison.

disease_resistance.summary: Tolerance to Yellow Mosaic Virus (YMV) and powdery mildew is reported for a group of selected mutants that includes CRIDA-18R. The digest states that the trait does not belong to CRIDA-18R alone, so this is group-level evidence and not variety-specific confirmation. The CRIDA-1-18R ground-truth record also lists tolerance to leaf blight and root rot, but the digest does not verify these, so they are not treated as confirmed here.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerance to mites is reported in the same mutant-group sentence that names CRIDA-18R, with the same group-level caveat. No evidence found for insect pest resistance in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Multi-location AICRP-Arid Legumes trials: 750-1150 kg/ha, with 20.94% higher yield than the best check. Farmer-field yield about 40% above local varieties (same source). Vellore district OFT (KVK Vellore, 2014-15): 900 kg/ha for CRIDA 18R vs 680 kg/ha for local Paiyur 2 (32.35% higher). Ground-truth average yield is listed as Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location AICRP-Arid Legumes trials gave a yield advantage over the best check. The digest does not give stability statistics (e.g., variance or stability indices) across environments. A review lists CRIDA 18-R among lines used to improve crop stability, without variety-specific data.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for rainfed conditions in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Karnataka (ground truth). Suitable for normal dates of sowing (ground truth). Field evidence is from Tamil Nadu (Vellore, Dharmapuri context) and multi-location AICRP trials.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Matures in 85-87 days with high pod number and synchronous podding (per ResearchGate scientific-contributions source). Tallest of four varieties in a sowing-date trial, at 88.2 cm. Seeds are brownish-red and bold, and fetch a premium over local seed (Vellore source). Ground-truth record: tolerant to shattering; seed weight 2.6-4.5 g/100 seed; seed colour brown; seed shape normal, flat. Digest also notes a non-shattering habit in the mutant group sentence.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Multi-location AICRP-Arid Legumes trials: 20.94% higher yield than the best check, 750-1150 kg/ha. (2) Farmer-field trials: about 40% above local varieties. (3) Vellore district OFT, KVK Vellore, 2014-15: 900 kg/ha vs 680 kg/ha for local Paiyur 2 (32.35% higher), benefit-cost ratio 2.4. (4) Vellore 2015-16 frontline demonstrations: 29.7% higher net return than local. (5) Sowing-date trial with four varieties including CRIDA 18R: CRIDA 18R was tallest at 88.2 cm (no yield data given in digest). The Dharmapuri 2020 frontline demonstration (7.15 q/ha, 40.6 pods per plant) is excluded because the digest does not explicitly attribute it to this variety. The Maruthi et al. management package is a reference to a publications file and is not a trial result for this variety in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Name: evidence refers to "CRIDA 18R" / "CRIDA 1-18 R" (variety_name CRIDA-1-18R). No Seednet page was returned, so seednet_variety_name is unverified.
- Described as a drought-tolerant selection for rainfed South India, and the Vellore on-farm trial found it more promising under drought than the local check -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318824395_Popularization_of_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_in_Vellore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
- Listed among recent varieties with improved yield stability and stress resistance, without specific stress data -- https://www.croptrust.org/knowledge-hub/crops/crop/horse-gram/
- A 2021 review says CRIDA 18-R and related lines were used to improve seed yield, stress resilience and crop stability, without variety-specific data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/399487637_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_Nutritional_Composition_Genomic_Resources_and_Breeding_Prospects
- Tolerance to Yellow Mosaic Virus, powdery mildew and mites is reported for a set of selected mutants, including CRIDA-18R; the sentence does not state that the trait belongs to CRIDA-18R alone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324941322_Genetic_improvement_in_horse_gram_Macrotyloa_uniflorum_lam_verdec_syn_Dolichos_biflorus_L_through_induced_mutations
- Flood, submergence, salinity and heat tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
Name: "CRIDA 18R" / "CRIDA-18R" (variety_name CRIDA-1-18R; seednet name not verified).
- Yellow Mosaic Virus, powdery mildew and mite tolerance are listed for the mutant group, with CRIDA-18R named in that group -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324941322_Genetic_improvement_in_horse_gram_Macrotyloa_uniflorum_lam_verdec_syn_Dolichos_biflorus_L_through_induced_mutations
- Non-shattering habit is listed in the same group sentence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324941322_Genetic_improvement_in_horse_gram_Macrotyloa_uniflorum_lam_verdec_syn_Dolichos_biflorus_L_through_induced_mutations
- Insect pest resistance: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name: "CRIDA 18R" / "CRIDA-18R" (variety_name CRIDA-1-18R; seednet name not verified).
- Matures in 85-87 days and yields 750-1150 kg/ha, with high pod number and synchronous podding -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/P-Raghu-Ram-Reddy-2163191464
- Multi-location AICRP-Arid Legumes trials gave 20.94% higher yield than the best check, with 750-1150 kg/ha -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Farmer-field yield was about 40% above local varieties (same source) -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Vellore district OFT (KVK Vellore, 2014-15): 900 kg/ha for CRIDA 18R vs 680 kg/ha for local Paiyur 2, 32.35% higher, BCR 2.4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318824395_Popularization_of_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloa_uniflorum_in_Vellore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
- Vellore 2015-16 frontline demonstrations: higher net return (29.7%) than local -- https://www.academia.edu/81269178/Popularization_of_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_in_Vellore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
- Dharmapuri 2020 frontline demonstration with integrated management: 7.15 q/ha grain yield, 40.6 pods per plant -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2024/Dec/18_Dec_24/2024_CJAST_125122/Rev_CJAST_125122_Muk_A.pdf
- Sowing-date trial (four varieties incl. CRIDA 18R): CRIDA 18R was tallest (88.2 cm) -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-11-2020/K.%20Ramani,%20et%20al.pdf
- Agronomic management package for monsoon-matched sowing (Maruthi et al.): see PUBLICATIONS -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/assets/files/Publications_KSR.pdf
- Seed traits: brownish-red, bold seeds fetching a premium over local seed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318824395_Popularization_of_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_in_Vellore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Name: "CRIDA-18R" / "CRIDA 1-18 R" (variety_name CRIDA-1-18R; seednet name not verified).
- Derived from K-42 by physical mutagenesis with gamma irradiation; mutant derivative of K-42 -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Developed by mutation breeding (gamma rays) and released for South India in 2009 -- https://www.researchgate.net/scientific-contributions/P-Raghu-Ram-Reddy-2163191464
- Parental use: CRIDA 1-18R was irradiated with gamma and electron-beam doses in a BRNS-funded mutant programme (mutant generation, not a QTL study) -- https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-024-67282-5
- Cross HPKM 320 x CRIDA 18-R assessed for breeding potential (transgressive segregation, usefulness criterion) in an F2:3 study -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/399487637_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_Nutritional_Composition_Genomic_Resources_and_Breeding_Prospects
- Same cross in a second study with CRIDA 18-R x Palem 1 comparisons -- https://www.old.uasbangalore.edu.in/images/2021-4th-Issue/11.pdf
- QTL, gene markers, SSR or genome sequence specific to CRIDA-1-18R: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name: "CRIDA 18R" (variety_name CRIDA-1-18R; seednet name not verified).
- Developed by the Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA), Hyderabad, and released by CVRC in 2009 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Release-paper authors: P. Ragh

drought.details: The CSC variety record states tolerance to drought: the crop faced moisture stress in the test year and still recorded high yields. The digest adds one CRHG-4-specific observation: in a 22-genotype yield and physiology assessment, CRHG-4 showed the lowest canopy temperature and the highest SPAD value. The digest does not state the year or the stress condition, so this is supportive but not a confirmed drought trial. The 2010 release statement (up to 33% higher grain yield and 10-25 days earlier maturity than local checks) is a combined statement for CRIDA 18R and CRHG 4 and is not used to rate CRHG-4 alone. The digest notes that drought tolerance is a general horse gram trait and that no CRHG-4-specific drought trial was found.

heat.details: No heat-specific evidence found for CRHG-4. Lower canopy temperature in the 22-genotype assessment may be relevant, but the digest does not link it to heat stress.

salinity.details: No evidence found for CRHG-4 (digest: Salinity, flood, submergence and heat: No evidence found for CRHG-4).

flood.details: No evidence found for CRHG-4 (digest: Salinity, flood, submergence and heat: No evidence found for CRHG-4).

disease_resistance.summary: CSC variety record states tolerance to Yellow mosaic virus, powdery mildew, leaf blight and root rot ('Tolerant to major diseases viz., Yellow mosaic VIrus, Powdery Mildew, Leaf Blight, Root rot etc.'). No CRHG-4-specific disease evidence was found in the digest. Yellow mosaic virus, powdery mildew and mite tolerance described in the digest belongs to CRIDA-18R and is excluded. The 2016 abstract's powdery mildew, anthracnose and whiteflies tolerance is not assigned to CRHG-4 because it sits between CRIDA-18R and CRHG-4 text. The 2023 YMV screening did not include CRHG-4 among its checks. Resistance status is therefore based on the CSC record only and is not independently confirmed in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC variety record states better tolerance to mites than the check AK-21 ('It showed better tolerance to mites than the check AK-21'). The digest attributes mite tolerance (brown seed, non-shattering) to CRIDA-18R, which is excluded. No independent CRHG-4-specific pest evidence was found. Whitefly tolerance from the 2016 abstract is not assigned to CRHG-4.

agronomic_details.yield: Mutant derivative of Hyderabad Local averaged 785 kg/ha, 33.1% above the best check, with a range of 700-1100 kg/ha across locations. The CSC record gives an average yield of 7.84 Qtl./ha, which is consistent with the 785 kg/ha figure. A 34% yield gain over local varieties in farmers' fields is reported in the same source, but its attribution is unclear and should be verified.
