search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Cridalatha (CRHG-4), Horse gram (Macrotyloma uniflorum)
Name matching: CSC name "Cridalatha (CRHG-4)"; Seednet name "CRIDALATHA (CRHG-4)". Sources use CRHG-4, CRHG4, or "CRIDALATH A (RHG 4)". Pages that name only CRIDA 18R or CRIDA 1-18R are a different variety and are excluded.

STRESS TOLERANCE (name matched: CRHG-4)
- In a 22-genotype yield and physiology assessment, CRHG-4 showed the lowest canopy temperature and the highest SPAD value; the page does not state the year or the stress condition -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/Crops_and_cropping_systems.html
- The 2010 release description says CRIDA 18R and CRHG 4 gave up to 33% higher grain yield and matured 10-25 days earlier than local checks in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu and Kerala (combined statement, not split by variety) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/318824395_Popularization_of_Horse_Gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_in_Vellore_District_of_Tamil_Nadu
- Drought tolerance is a general horse gram trait in the crop literature; no CRHG-4-specific drought trial was found -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Macrotyloma_uniflorum
- Salinity, flood, submergence and heat: No evidence found for CRHG-4

DISEASE AND PEST (name matched: CRHG-4)
- A 2016 mutation-breeding abstract lists tolerance to powdery mildew, anthracnose and whiteflies, but the paragraph sits between CRIDA-18R and CRHG-4 text, so it cannot be safely assigned to CRHG-4 -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Yellow mosaic virus, powdery mildew and mite tolerance (brown seed, non-shattering) is described for CRIDA-18R, not CRHG-4 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324941322_Genetic_improvement_in_horse_gram_Macrotyloma_uniflorum_lam_verdec_syn_Dolichos_biflorus_L_through_induced_mutations
- Yellow mosaic virus screening (2023) used PAIYUR 2 and CRIDA 1-18 R as checks; CRHG-4 was not among them -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9960754/
- No CRHG-4-specific pest or disease evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (name matched: CRHG-4)
- Mutant derivative of Hyderabad Local averaged 785 kg/ha, 33.1% above the best check, with a range of 700-1100 kg/ha across locations -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- The same source reports a 34% yield gain over local varieties in farmers' fields and a black-seeded, non-shattering type; this paragraph's attribution is unclear and should be verified -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Multi-location testing under AICRP on Arid Legumes (IVT, then AVT I and II) led to release; the 2014 release date given in the same source appears to refer to CRHG-19 -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- CRHG-4 was a check in a 108-germplasm augmented trial at Vijayapur, kharif 2021-22 -- https://www.researchgate.net/figure/List-of-horse-gram-Macrotyloma-uniflorum-Lam-Verdc-genotypes-used-in-the-evaluation_tbl1_357974527
- Sowing and package-of-practices details are generic horse gram guidance, not CRHG-4-specific -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/pulses/horse-gram?lgn=en

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: derivative of Hyderabad Local, from an induced mutation program -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Mutagen discrepancy: the Seednet-linked parentage text says V-ray irradiation, while the 2016 abstract says gamma-ray irradiation of seeds of K-42 and Hyderabad Local -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Breeding method: stable lines were selected from M1 to M6 generations, with superior mutants identified by multi-location evaluation -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html
- Breeding-line codes: CRHG-4, CRHG4 and CRIDALATH A (RHG 4) all appear for this variety -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/356086546_HORSEGRAM-A_SUPREMACY_NUTRITIONAL_SOURCE_A_REVIEW
- Genome resources and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found for CRHG-4. The 2025 NIRS study covers 139 accessions but does not name CRHG-4 -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12081650/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (name matched: CRHG-4)
- Institution: ICAR-Central Research Institute for Dryland Agriculture (CRIDA), Hyderabad, which released CRIDA 18R and CRHG 4 for peninsular India -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/assets_c/img/Vision_2050.pdf
- Mutation work on horse gram was carried out at CRIDA, Hyderabad -- https://www.walshmedicalmedia.com/proceedings/genetic-improvement-of-horsegram-through-mutation-breeding-15199.html

agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Nepal, Central Terai, 2019: maturity 121 days, grain yield 1728 kg/ha, highest among tested genotypes that year. (2) New Alluvial Zone, West Bengal (Kalyani), 2014-16: 1704 kg/ha, ranked among the promising varieties. (3) Rice-lentil cropping system, eastern India, 62 front-line demonstrations (FLDs): technology gap 754 kg/ha and technology index 41.8%, the highest of the varieties compared. (4) Cluster front-line demonstrations: mean 952 kg/ha over three years against a local check of 675 kg/ha. (5) Lower Gangetic Plains, late-sown trial, 2019-2020: 731 kg/ha in normal sowing, the lowest of the genotypes tested, attributed to delayed emergence and flowering. (6) Review table (BHU, 2005): about 130 days to maturity and about 14.0 q/ha average yield.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Malaviya Vishwanath (HUL-57), Lentil (Lens culinaris)

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "Malaviya Vishwanath (HUL-57)". The sources spell it "HUL 57", "HUL-57", "Malviya Vishwanath" or "Malavia Vishwanath". All findings below refer to this variety. Only four web searches were run, so the Seednet portal, KrishiKosh and ICAR/AICRP sites were not queried directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: a physiological study on drought-stressed lentil reports HUL-57 (microsperma) as more drought resistant than IPL-406 (macrosperma), with higher soluble sugar and proline accumulation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/304169848_Physiological_and_Biochemical_Adaptations_in_Lentil_Genotypes_under_Drought_Stress_1
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rust and wilt: a review table lists this variety (BHU, 2005) with the remark "Resistant to rust & wilt, small seeded" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review. The table row layout is ambiguous, so treat this as indicative until checked against the notification.
- Pod borer: the same review table has a pod-borer tolerance remark, but it is not clearly attached to this variety's row; not attributed here -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- General disease tolerance: a production guide describes HUL-57 as "high-yielding; disease tolerant" with no specific diseases named -- https://agridots.com/courses/bsc-agriculture/agronomy/practical-crop-production-ii-rabi/09-lentil-production-technology

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity and yield (review table, BHU 2005): about 130 days to maturity and about 14.0 q/ha average yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- Maturity in a Nepal trial (2019): 121 days, grain yield 1728 kg/ha, the highest among tested genotypes that year -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370051423_32_nd_National_Winter_Crop_Workshop_Proceedings_of_Evaluation_and_Identification_of_Appropriate_Lentil_Genotypes_under_Central_Terai_Region_of_Nepal
- New Alluvial Zone, West Bengal (Kalyani, 2014-16): 1704 kg/ha, ranked among the promising varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324517328_Performance_of_Different_Lentil_Varieties_in_New_Alluvial_Zone_of_West_Bengal
- Rice-lentil system, eastern India (62 FLDs): technology gap 754 kg/ha and technology index 41.8%, the highest of the varieties compared -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358911834_Performance_of_Lentil_Lens_Culinaris_Varieties_under_Rice-Lentil_Cropping_System_in_Eastern_Part_of_India
- Cluster front-line demonstrations: mean 952 kg/ha over three years against a local check of 675 kg/ha -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5574
- Lower Gangetic Plains, late-sown trial (2019-2020): 731 kg/ha in normal sowing, the lowest of the genotypes tested, attributed to delayed emergence and flowering -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5444

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage "mutant of HUL-11": No evidence found. None of the pages checked the HUL-11 parent.
- Mutagenic origin: a mutagenesis study treated HUL-57 seed with gamma rays (10, 20, 30 kR) and EMS (0.3%), singly and in combination, and scored morphological mutants -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344667700_Effect_of_mutagens_on_growth_parameters_of_Lentil_Lens_culinaris_L_Medikus
- Seed type: described as microsperma (small-seeded) -- https://agridots.com/courses/bsc-agriculture/agronomy/practical-crop-production-ii-rabi/09-lentil-production-technology
- Breeding-line codes, QTL/marker studies, genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: Banaras Hindu University, Institute of Agricultural Sciences, which the BHU lentil programme page credits with the release in 2004 for the NEPZ rainfed condition. The review table gives 2005 -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/ias/genetic_plant_b/ and https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found. The breeding page does not list names in the captured text.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level page: Banaras Hindu University, Institute of Agricultural Sciences, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding programme page -- https://www.bhu.ac.in/ias/genetic_plant_b/ (captured text contains no email, phone or postal address).
- Breeder email, phone, address and official institute contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- Sharma, V. and Shukla, V. (2019). Scenario of Lentil in India – A Review. Journal/report not confirmed from the snippet. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review (authors and year taken from the page; journal not captured)

- Authors not captured (year not captured). Performance of Lentil (Lens culinaris) Varieties under Rice-Lentil Cropping System in Eastern Part of India. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358911834_Performance_of_Lentil_Lens_Culinaris_Varieties_under_Rice-Lentil_Cropping_System_in_Eastern_Part_of_India
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Effect of mutagens on growth parameters of Lentil [Lens culinaris L. Medikus]. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344667700_Effect_of_mutagens_on_growth_parameters_of_Lentil_Lens_culinaris_L_Medikus
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Physiological and Biochemical Adaptations in Lentil Genotypes under Drought Stress. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/304169848_Physiological_and_Biochemical_Adaptations_in_Lentil_Genotypes_under_Drought_Stress_1
- Authors not captured (2019 trial). Evaluation and Identification of Appropriate Lentil Genotypes under Central Terai Region of Nepal. 32nd National Winter Crop Workshop Proceedings -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/370051423_32_nd_National_Winter_Crop_Workshop_Proceedings_of_Evaluation_and_Identification_of_Appropriate_Lentil_Genotypes_under_Central_Terai_Region_of_Nepal
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Lentil Varieties (Legume Research, LR-5444 and LR-5574 pages) -- see Agronomy and Trials URLs above.
- KrishiKosh theses, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, DOIs: No evidence found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporations, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. A review notes that non-availability of certified seed of high-yielding varieties is a major constraint in lentil -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0005193. A 2012 ICAR-CRIDA district report lists "Malaviya Vishwanath" among lentil varieties grown in Ghazipur, UP, which is cropping-practice evidence, not seed availability -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/CP/Uttar_Pradesh/UP12-Ghazipur-28.08.12.pdf

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Review table (BHU, 2005): Eastern and Central U.P., Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Assam -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/332698671_Scenario_of_Lentil_in_India_-A_Review
- Government of India state-wise list (DPD): HUL-57 appears under Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Jammu & Kashmir -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil.PDF
- Discrepancy: the input lists Uttarakhand, which none of the captured sources attributes to HUL-57. Assam, Jharkhand and Jammu & Kashmir also appear in the sources but not in the input list. Verify against the CSC notification.

drought.details: The digest describes Moitree as sensitive to high temperature and moisture stress, especially during reproduction. No drought tolerance rating was found in the retrieved pages. The input data claims the variety can stand terminal drought and is sustainable for delayed sowing, but the digest does not confirm this claim. Foliar micronutrient sprays were tested on Moitree under rainfed heat and moisture stress and late sowing (2021 study), which alleviated late-sowing stress; these studies do not establish intrinsic drought tolerance.

heat.details: Digest describes Moitree as sensitive to high temperature stress, especially during reproduction. A 2021 study tested micronutrient foliar sprays to offset heat and moisture stress on this variety, and a rainfed study found foliar micronutrient sprays alleviated late-sowing stress. The level is rated low on the basis of the reported sensitivity; the digest does not provide a tolerance rating.

salinity.details: No salinity tolerance rating for Moitree was found in the retrieved pages.

flood.details: No flood tolerance rating for Moitree was found in the retrieved pages.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: listed as resistant in the DPD central-release table (digest). Stemphylium blight: used as a moderately susceptible local control in a BCKV screen under natural epiphytotic conditions (digest); a 2025 pathosystem study validated a disease-yield-loss model on Moitree grown in West Bengal. Wilt and grey mould: the input data lists resistance to wilt and grey mould under field conditions, but the digest does not verify this claim.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No pest-resistance rating for Moitree was found. The input lists pest reaction as unknown.

agronomic_details.yield: Input data gives an average yield of 1500 kg/ha. Digest reports 16-18 q/ha (1600-1800 kg/ha) average seed yield in West Bengal and NEPZ trials, and 14-15 q/ha in the DPD table. These figures differ and are reported as given by each source.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources for multi-environment stability. Digest reports yield performance in West Bengal and NEPZ trials and in the New Alluvial Zone; no stability statistics were retrieved.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Input data recommends rainfed cultivation in Eastern Uttar Pradesh, Bihar, Jharkhand, Assam and West Bengal. The DPD central-release table lists Moitree for NEPZ (Assam, Bihar, Jharkhand, West Bengal). The NWPZ entry is truncated in the digest. Sowing-date trials at Berhampore identified early November sowing as best for WBL 77 and B 77.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: - Leaf pubescence: Absent; - Leaflet size: Medium; - Plant growth habit: Erect; - Flower colour of standard: Blue; - Tendril length: Absent; - Biomass score: High; - Pod pigmentation: Absent; - Seed size: Medium (2.2-2.3 g); Seed coat colour: Grey; - Maturity Group: Medium (118-120 days); - Seed testa mottling: Present; - Cotyledon colour: Orange.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Sowing-date trials at Berhampore (2004-06): early-November sowing identified as best for WBL 77 and B 77. (2) Micronutrient-spray and thermal-time trials at BCKV (2018-20) on Moitree under normal and late sowing; the digest does not report numerical results. (3) New Alluvial Zone trial: WBL77 gave the highest seed yield of 1831 kg/ha among 15 varieties, with the most branches and pods per plant. (4) KVK Kokrajhar cluster frontline demonstration on WBL-77 in 2020-21 and 2021-22; the digest reports no results. (5) West Bengal and NEPZ trials: average seed yield 16-18 q/ha. (6) DPD table: 14-15 q/ha and 115-120 days to maturity. (7) 2021 rainfed heat and moisture stress studies with foliar micronutrient sprays; late-sowing stress was alleviated. (8) 2024 BCKV Stemphylium blight screen: Moitree used as a moderately susceptible local control. (9) 2025 pathosystem study: disease-yield-loss model validated on Moitree in West Bengal.

(3) New Alluvial Zone trial: WBL77 gave the highest seed yield of 1831 kg/ha among 15 varieties, with the most branches and pods per plant. (4) KVK Kokrajhar cluster frontline demonstration on WBL-77 in 2020-21 and 2021-22; the digest reports no results. (5) West Bengal and NEPZ trials: average seed yield 16-18 q/ha. (8) 2024 BCKV Stemphylium blight screen: Moitree used as a moderately susceptible local control. (9) 2025 pathosystem study: disease-yield-loss model validated on Moitree in West Bengal.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Moitree WBL-77 (lentil, Lens culinaris)

Name note: The searches used "Moitree WBL-77" and "WBL 77". Both spellings appear in the retrieved pages, and they match both the variety_name ("Moitree WBL-77)") and the seednet_variety_name ("MOITREE WBL-77)"). No retrieved page used the stray-parenthesis form, and no seednet.gov.in page was retrieved. Findings below refer to the variety under either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE: Moitree is described as sensitive to high temperature and moisture stress, especially during reproduction; a 2021 study tested micronutrient foliar sprays to offset heat and moisture stress on it -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8342000/ ; https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/plant-science/articles/10.3389/fpls.2021.679469/pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE: A rainfed heat-and-moisture stress study with Moitree found foliar micronutrient sprays alleviated late-sowing stress -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9021876/
STRESS TOLERANCE: No drought, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance rating for Moitree was found in the retrieved pages -- No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST: In a BCKV screen under natural epiphytotic conditions, Moitree was used as a moderately susceptible local control against Stemphylium blight (SB) -- https://www.bdbotsociety.org/public/article/2024%20June/1823_11.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST: A 2025 pathosystem study validated its disease-yield-loss model on Moitree grown in West Bengal -- https://www.tandfonline.com/doi/full/10.1080/03235408.2025.2530793
DISEASE AND PEST: The DPD central-release table lists Moitree as resistant to rust -- http://dpd.gov.in/5.%20Lentil%20%20varieties.pdf
DISEASE AND PEST: No pest-resistance rating for Moitree was found -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Average seed yield in West Bengal and NEPZ trials is given as 16-18 q/ha for Moitree (WBL 77) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/259675093_Lentil_varieties_in_India
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The DPD table gives 14-15 q/ha yield and 115-120 days to maturity -- https://dpd.gov.in/Lentil%20%20Varieties.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: In a New Alluvial Zone trial, WBL77 gave the highest seed yield of 1831 kg/ha among 15 varieties, with the most branches and pods per plant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324517328_Performance_of_Different_Lentil_Varieties_in_New_Alluvial_Zone_of_West_Bengal
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A KVK Kokrajhar cluster frontline demonstration on WBL-77 ran in 2020-21 and 2021-22 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/324517328_Performance_of_Different_Lentil_Varieties_in_New_Alluvial_Zone_of_West_Bengal
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Sowing-date trials at Berhampore (2004-06) identified early-November sowing as best for WBL 77 and B 77 -- https://cwss.in/Journal/Complete_jurnal/Vol5_2__23.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: Micronutrient-spray and thermal-time trials at BCKV (2018-20) on Moitree under normal and late sowing -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347596099_Effect_of_micronutrients_foliar_spray_on_thermal_Indices_phenology_and_yield_of_Lentil_in_new_Alluvial_Zone_of_West_Bengal

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage (ILL7723 x BL x 84176), breeding-line code, breeding method and QTL/marker data: the parentage given in the input was not confirmed by any retrieved page -- No evidence found
GENETICS AND QTL: Karyological and seed-protein profiling placed WBL 77 (Moitree) among five Berhampore varieties; the highest similarity index (0.690) was with B 77 (Asha) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC6299895
GENETICS AND QTL: Gamma-irradiation mutagenesis (0-350 Gy) was applied to Moitree seed to induce variability -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/347596099_Effect_of_micronutrients_foliar_spray_on_thermal_Indices_phenology_and_yield_of_Lentil_in_new_Alluvial_Zone_of_West_Bengal
GENETICS AND QTL: In vitro regeneration protocols were reported for clonally true-to-type Moitree plants -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360739617_Global_status_of_lentil_production_with_special_reference_to_India

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Moitree was developed at the Pulses and Oilseeds Research Station (PORS), Berhampore, and was identified for release by the Central Varietal Release Committee -- https://cwss.in/Journal/Complete_jurnal/Vol5_2__23.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: A CAG performance audit lists Moitree WBL-77 (2009) among five pulse varieties developed by PORS, Berhampore, 2008-2018 -- https://d1jmc0u14z2tmp.cloudfront.net/uploads/download_audit_report/2019/3.%20Chapter_2-062430653813421.12516653.pdf
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Lead breeder or scientist name(s) -- No evidence found

seednet_fields.Parentage: VL 7 HAS BEEN DERIVED FROM A CROSS BETWEEN TWO RELEASED GARDEN PEA VARIETY viz., PANT UPHAR (IP 3) AND ARKEL. SELECTION FOR YIELD, EARLINESS AND OTHER DESIRABLE CHARACTERS WAS FOLLOWED IN THE SEGREGATING GENERATIONS AND F6 WAS BULKED DURING 1983 FOR EVALUATION.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR RLEASE AND CULTIVATION IN ZONE IV SUBJECT TO THA CONDITION THAT THE ZONE IV STATES NAME ARE TO BE INFORMED PROJECT  CO-ORDINATOR FOR GARDEN PEAS BEFORE NOTIFICATION. IRRIGATED CONDITIONS DURING RABI IN ZONE-IV AND ZONE-I
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: THE AGRONOMICAL TRIALS RELATED TO FERTILIZER RESPONSE, SOWING TIME, SPACING AND SEED RATES WERE CONDUCTED DURING 1992-93 AT ALMORA FOR COMPARING VL 7 WITH ARKEL. THE VARIETY VL 7 WAS FOUND TO BE SIGNIFICANTLY SUPERIOR THAN ARKEL AS IT PRODUCED 15.3% HIGHER GREEN POD YIELD. VL.7 RESPONDED VERY WELL TO FYM APPLICATION AND CHEMICAL FERTILIZERS. APPLICATION OF 20 KG N 60 KG P2O5 AND 40 KG K2 O PER HECTARE ALONGWITH 20T/HA FYM WAS FOUND TO BE THE OPTIMUM DOSE WHICH PRODUCED 177.0 Q/HA GREEN POD YIELD.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : 65-70 CM PLANTS ARE DWARF WITH DETEMINATE GROWTH HABIT, DARK GREEN FOLIAGE, WHITE FLOWERS AND TWO PODS PER PEDUNCLE. IT CAN BE EASILY DISTINGUISHED FROM THE ARKEL BY ITS EXTREMELY FASTER GROWTH AND LIGHT FOLIAGE COLOUR AT EARLY VEGETATIVE PHASE. THE PODS ARE LIGHT GREEN SLIGHTLY IN CURCED TO WARDS SUTURE AT THE DISTAL END. MEDIUM IN SIZE ( 8CM) WITH COMPLETE FILLING. THE PODS COMTAIN 6-7 SEED/POD WITH 42% SHELLING GREEN GRAINS ARE BLOD (41.2 G/100, GRAIN) AND DIMPLED. SEED IN LIGHT GREEN, WRINKLED WITH 1000 SEED wt.OF 220-225 GMS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: THE INCIDENCE OF POWDERY MILDEW AND WHITE ROT DISEASE IS SIMILAR TO ARKEL UNDER NATURAL CONDITIONS. HOWEVER, IT SHOWED LESS INCIDENCE OF ALTERNARIA BLIGHT THAN ARKEL. THE INCIDENCE OF LEAF MINOR AND POD BORER HAS BEEN OBSERVED TO BE SIMILAR TO RELEASED VARIETIES.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: THE INCIDENCE OF POWDERY MILDEW AND WHITE ROT

drought.details: The digest's PEG-induced drought study describes Pusa 992 as moderately drought-sensitive and early-maturing, with higher ROS and TBARS and lower proline than the tolerant Pusa Arhar 16. This conflicts with the original variety record, which states the variety is tolerant to moisture stress conditions. The digest study is the only independent physiological evidence found, so the rating reflects it, and the conflict is unresolved in the searched sources.

heat.details: No evidence found. The search returned no page naming Pusa 992 for heat tolerance.

salinity.details: No evidence found. The search returned no page naming Pusa 992 for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: In a seed-stage waterlogging/submergence screen of 60 genotypes, Pusa-992 showed the least reduction among the tolerant genotypes. The same screen reports hastened senescence under waterlogging for Pusa-991 and Pusa-992. The rating is medium because of this mixed result. The original record's statement that the variety has no problem with lodging or shattering does not address flooding.

disease_resistance.summary: Sterility mosaic disease (SMD) and Phytophthora blight are the two important diseases in the North-West zone for which the variety was identified. The original variety record states the variety shows relatively lower susceptibility to these diseases compared with control varieties. The digest does not confirm this with trial data. For SMD and Fusarium wilt, a review cites a 2023 source (Raje and Singh) on Pusa 992, but the extracted sentence is truncated and does not state the result, so it is treated as unverified. No evidence was found for Phytophthora resistance specifically in Pusa 992. A commercial seller page claims resistance to common pests and diseases, but this is marketing text and is not treated as trial evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: Pod borers are the major pests of this crop. The original record states that no variety is resistant to them because of their polyphagous nature, and that pest reaction was similar across locations. In a pod fly (Melanagromyza obtusa) screen of 31 genotypes with Pusa 992 used as a check, none was rated resistant. No Helicoverpa-specific evidence was found for Pusa 992.

agronomic_details.yield: The original record gives an average yield of 1643.00 to 2434.00 kg/ha. The digest contains no Pusa 992-specific yield figure. A 2016 review table lists unlabelled values (8.5; 145-150; 14-18) against Pusa 992, which cannot be interpreted. The IARI entry reports that Pusa Arhar 2017-1 yields up to 22.75 q/ha, 'considerably higher than the national check Pusa 992'. This is a comparison with a different variety and is not a yield figure for Pusa 992.
agronomic_details.stability: The AMMI stability analysis (kharif 2007-08 to 2009-10) named Pusa-992 among the best genotypes. The original record states the variety provides stability when sown early and is less prone to monsoon vagaries.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh (western UP) per the original record. The digest describes the variety as a North-West zone variety. Field vacating is possible if sown by the first week of June.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Fertigation field trial, kharif 2015, Water Technology Centre: drip at 100% WRc with 100% RDF through water-soluble fertilizer gave the highest grain yield. The digest lists this under the Pusa 992 section but does not state the variety in the trial summary, so the attribution is not confirmed. (2) AMMI stability analysis (kharif 2007-08 to 2009-10): Pusa-992 was named among the best genotypes. (3) Intercropping and nutrient study (kharif 2015): Pusa 992 was grown with black gram, green gram and sesame. 125% RDF gave a slight seed-yield gain that was statistically equal to the standard dose. (4) Madhya Pradesh FLDs listed Pusa 992 with JKM 189 and TJT 501. The 1394 kg/ha vs 1078 kg/ha result applies to the combined varieties, not Pusa 992 alone, so it is excluded from Pusa 992 performance. (5) Waterlogging screen at the seed stage: Pusa-992 showed the least reduction among tolerant genotypes, with hastened senescence noted. (6) Pod fly screen: Pusa 992 was used as a check; none of 31 genotypes was rated resistant.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Pusa 992 is included among the varieties in a 62K genic-SNP chip study. No marker positions or SSR details for this variety were found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: No evidence found for Pusa 992 specifically. The QTL mapping work found used Pusa Dwarf and H2001-4 recombinant inbred lines.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The 2025 BMC Plant Biology study of Pusa 992 under drought is a physiological and molecular study. It reports higher ROS and TBARS and lower proline than Pusa Arhar 16. No specific genes or pathways were named for Pusa 992 in the digest.

- Heat and salinity tolerance: No evidence found. The search returned no page naming Pusa 992 for heat or salinity.

DISEASE AND PEST
Name matched: Pusa 992 / Pusa-992
- Pod fly (Melanagromyza obtusa) screen of 31 genotypes with Pusa 992 as a check: none was rated resistant; Pusa 992 was among the checks used -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jer-42-4-007
- Fusarium wilt and sterility mosaic disease: a review cites a 2023 source (Raje and Singh) on Pusa 992, but the extracted sentence is truncated and does not state the result. Treat as unverified -- https://era.dpi.qld.gov.au/id/eprint/15166/1/1.+Review+paper_50+Yr_R.pdf
- Commercial seller page claims Pusa 992 has resistance to common pests and diseases. This is marketing text, not trial evidence -- https://eruvaakamart.com/product/pusa-992/
- Helicoverpa and Phytophthora resistance: No evidence found for Pusa 992 specifically. The IARI entry for Pusa Arhar 2018-4 (a different variety) reports Phytophthora, SMD and Fusarium tolerance -- https://www.iari.res.in/sci_db/sci_details.php?scid=M2hXRUEyUnF5SldwVGluRUZ1RUZhUT09

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Name matched: Pusa 992 / Pusa-992
- Fertigation field trial, kharif 2015, Water Technology Centre: drip at 100% WRc with 100% RDF through water-soluble fertilizer gave the highest grain yield -- https://www.phytojournal.com/special-issue?year=2018&vol=7&issue=2S&ArticleId=4420
- AMMI stability analysis (kharif 2007-08 to 2009-10): Pusa-992 was named among the best genotypes -- https://oar.icrisat.org/10756/1/Stability%20analysis%20of%20pigeon%20pea.pdf
- Intercropping and nutrient study (kharif 2015): Pusa 992 was grown with black gram, green gram and sesame; 125% RDF gave a slight, statistically equal seed-yield gain -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-3947
- Madhya Pradesh FLDs listed Pusa 992 with JKM 189 and TJT 501; the 1394 kg/ha vs 1078 kg/ha result is for the combined varieties, not Pusa 992 alone -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/agricultural-reviews/R-2343
- Yield potential: No Pusa 992-specific yield figure was found in the extracted text. A 2016 review table lists unlabelled values (8.5; 145-150; 14-18) against Pusa 992 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309136303_Breeding_Improved_Cultivars_of_Pigeonpea_in_India
- Comparison: IARI reports Pusa Arhar 2017-1 yields up to 22.75 Q/ha, "considerably higher than the national check Pusa 992" -- https://www.iari.res.in/sci_db/sci_details.php?scid=M2hXRUEyUnF5SldwVGluRUZ1RUZhUT09
- Maturity: the 2016 review describes Pusa 992 as early maturing, ensuring timely harvest for wheat in the rotation -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/313234414_Pigeonpea_improvement_through_conventional_breeding
- Quality: sensory dal evaluation in NWPZ used Pusa 992 as a control because of its wide market availability -- https://academicjournals.org/journal/JPBCS/article-full-text/195B18363901

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Name matched: Pusa 992 / Pusa-992
- Parentage: pure-line selection from the 90306 population (plain zone). Breeding table lists "Selection from 90306" -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309136303_Breeding_Improved_Cultivars_of_Pigeonpea_in_India ; also https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Dinkar-Dinkar/publication/373171560_Pigeon_pea_Genetic_Resources_and_it's_utilization_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects/links/64de3030caf5ff5cd0c33df8/Pigeon-pea-Genetic-Resources-and-its-utilization-Current-Status-and-Future-Prospects.pdf . - Breeding line code: "Pusa 992 A" was developed as a short-duration A (CMS) line, using a cytoplasmic source from C. -- https://www.iari.res.in/files/Publication/annual_report/IARIANNUALREPORT2018_19_30072019.pdf
- Genome resources: Pusa 992 is among the varieties in the 62K genic-SNP chip study (resequencing of 45 diverse varieties) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/340016950_A_62K_genic-SNP_chip_array_for_genetic_studies_and_breeding_applications_in_pigeonpea_Cajanus_cajan_L_Millsp
- QTL mapping: No evidence found for Pusa 992 specifically. The mapping work found used Pusa Dwarf/H2001-4 RILs.
- Breeding method: pure-line selection (parentage above). No further method detail was found.
- Transcriptome: the 2025 BMC Plant Biology study of Pusa 992 under drought is a physiological/molecular study -- https://link.springer.com/content/pdf/10.1186/s12870-025-07174-6.pdf

drought.details: Described as tolerant to drought in the variety record, which states it recorded high pod yield in drought years and ranked first with 2222 kg/ha pod yield in the National Drought Nursery trials. The ICAR compendium lists K-134 among drought-tolerant groundnut releases in India, while noting these were not bred specifically for drought. A drought-stress EST study on K-134 reports higher relative water content and proline than the comparison cultivar under soil-moisture stress. The ICAR-CRIDA rainfed booklet recommends K-134 for kharif seasons with scarce rainfall.

heat.details: The ICAR compendium lists K-134 among heat-tolerant genotypes. No mechanism, test conditions or quantitative data for heat tolerance were found in the digest.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance in the searched sources.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Late leaf spot: tolerant per the variety record (CSC ground truth, no URL in digest). Leaf spots (general): described as tolerant in the ICAR compendium entry. Peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND): described as tolerant in the ICAR compendium entry. The ANGRAU pathology work reviewed in the digest does not tie K-134 to a specific resistance test result.

pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests: tolerant per the variety record (CSC ground truth, no URL in digest). Thrips, jassids and aphids: No evidence found in the searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: ICAR compendium: pod yield 1677 kg/ha (kharif) and 2338 kg/ha (rabi-summer); kernel yield 1191 kg/ha and 1613 kg/ha; oil content 46.0%. Variety record: average yield 1650 to 2850 kg/ha. Drought nursery: 2222 kg/ha pod yield, ranked first.
agronomic_details.stability: High pod yield recorded even in drought years (variety record). Ranked first in National Drought Nursery trials. No multi-environment stability analysis found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended to Andhra Pradesh, particularly Rayalaseema and Mahaboobnagar district (variety record). Suitable for kharif and rabi (variety record). Recommended for kharif seasons with scarce rainfall and for rainfed production in Chitradurga and Tumkur (CRIDA booklet).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DARK GREEN FOLIAGE. REMAINS GREEN EVEN AT THE TIME OF MATURITY. Dark green elongated leaves, profuse pod bearing, very low leaf drop, normal spacing 30 x 10 cm (variety record). Compendium: dark green, medium, elongated leaflets; 106 days to maturity.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) ICAR compendium: pod yield 1677 kg/ha kharif and 2338 kg/ha rabi-summer; kernel yield 1191 and 1613 kg/ha; oil 46.0%; 106 days to maturity. (2) National Drought Nursery trials: ranked first with 2222 kg/ha pod yield. (3) Thresher-modification trial, Agricultural Research Station, Anantapur (2002 to 2004): 22 x 11 mm sieve suitable for K-134 (Vemana) shelling, broken kernels about 3.9%. (4) CRIDA booklet: recommended for rainfed production in Chitradurga and Tumkur, seed rate 100 kg/ha, spacing 30 x 10 cm. (5) Slideshow listing Vemana (K134) for kharif and rabi: no trial data.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. The drought EST study uses K-134 as a material but reports no QTLs or markers.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The drought EST study identifies drought stress-responsive genes from K-134 (subtracted EST analysis). Specific gene names and pathways were not retrieved in the digest.

agronomic_performance.stability: High pod yield recorded even in drought years (variety record). Ranked first in National Drought Nursery trials. No multi-environment stability analysis found.
agronomic_performance.adaptation: Recommended to Andhra Pradesh, particularly Rayalaseema and Mahaboobnagar district (variety record). Suitable for kharif and rabi (variety record). Recommended for kharif seasons with scarce rainfall and for rainfed production in Chitradurga and Tumkur (CRIDA booklet).
agronomic_performance.plant_characteristics: DARK GREEN FOLIAGE. REMAINS GREEN EVEN AT THE TIME OF MATURITY. Dark green elongated leaves, profuse pod bearing, very low leaf drop, normal spacing 30 x 10 cm (variety record). Compendium: dark green, medium, elongated leaflets; 106 days to maturity.
agronomic_performance.field_trials: (1) ICAR compendium: pod yield 1677 kg/ha kharif and 2338 kg/ha rabi-summer; kernel yield 1191 and 1613 kg/ha; oil 46.0%; 106 days to maturity. (2) National Drought Nursery trials: ranked first with 2222 kg/ha pod yield. (3) Thresher-modification trial, Agricultural Research Station, Anantapur (2002 to 2004): 22 x 11 mm sieve suitable for K-134 (Vemana) shelling, broken kernels about 3.9%. (4) CRIDA booklet: recommended for rainfed production in Chitradurga and Tumkur, seed rate 100 kg/ha, spacing 30 x 10 cm. (5) Slideshow listing Vemana (K134) for kharif and rabi: no trial data.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vemana (K-134), Groundnut

Name note: variety_name "Vemana (K-134)" and seednet_variety_name "VEMANA (K-134)" are treated as the same variety. No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so the Seednet evidence is limited to the name and parentage supplied in the input record. Most sources below use "K-134" or "Vemana" alone; I counted these as this variety only where the page links them to groundnut.

STRESS TOLERANCE: The ICAR compendium lists K-134 among drought-tolerant groundnut releases in India, though it notes these were not bred specifically for drought. Some of the drought tolerant varieties released in India are: Kadiri-3, K-134 -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
STRESS TOLERANCE: The same compendium also lists K-134 among heat-tolerant genotypes. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
STRESS TOLERANCE: A drought-stress EST study on K-134 reports that it keeps higher relative water content and proline than the comparison cultivar under soil-moisture stress, supporting its drought tolerance. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237008483_Identification_of_drought_stress-responsive_genes_from_droughttolerant_groundnut_cultivar_Arachis_hypogaea_L_cv_K-134_through_analysis_of_subtracted_expressed_sequence_tags
STRESS TOLERANCE: The ICAR-CRIDA rainfed groundnut district technology booklet recommends K-134 for kharif seasons with scarce rainfall. -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/assets/img/Books/2004-05/Groundnut.pdf
STRESS TOLERANCE: Flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. Salinity tolerance: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST: The compendium entry describes K-134 as tolerant of leaf spots, peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND) and drought. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
DISEASE AND PEST: Pest resistance (thrips, jassids, aphids): No evidence found.
DISEASE AND PEST: The Kadiri-based ANGRAU pathology work on groundnut virus and fungal screening was reviewed, but none of the retrieved pages tie K-134 to a specific resistance test result. Kuruba Vemana (ANGRAU, Kadiri) is a plant pathologist and is not linked to K-134 in any source, so this is name resemblance only. -- https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Kuruba-Vemana

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The compendium reports K-134 pod yield of 1,677 kg/ha in kharif and 2,338 kg/ha in rabi-summer, kernel yield of 1,191 and 1,613 kg/ha, oil content of 46.0%, and 106 days to maturity. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The compendium describes dark green, medium, elongated leaflets as the distinct morphological feature. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A thresher-modification trial at the Agricultural Research Station, Anantapur (2002–2004) found a 22 x 11 mm sieve suitable for K-134 (Vemana) shelling, with broken kernels around 3.9%. -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/webArticle/articles/asd301006.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: The CRIDA booklet lists K-134 as a recommended variety for rainfed production in Chitradurga and Tumkur, with a 100 kg/ha seed rate and 30 x 10 cm spacing. -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/assets/img/Books/2004-05/Groundnut.pdf
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A slideshow on suitable groundnut varieties for kharif and rabi lists Vemana (K134) but gives no trial data. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/suitable-groundnut-varieties-for-kharif-and-rabi/251178470

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage in the compendium is Kadiri-3 x JL-24, with the modified bulk method as the breeding method. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
GENETICS AND QTL: The Seednet record gives female parent K 3 and male parent JL 24. These appear to be the same parents as Kadiri-3 and JL-24, but the sources do not confirm this equivalence. -- input record
GENETICS AND QTL: Breeding-line code, genes, QTL/marker studies and genome resources: No evidence found. The drought EST study uses K-134 as a material but does not report QTLs or markers. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/237008483_Identification_of_drought_stress-responsive_genes_from_droughttolerant_groundnut_cultivar_Arachis_hypogaea_L_cv_K-134_through_analysis_of_subtracted_expressed_sequence_tags

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: The compendium credits the release to APAU (now ANGRAU), Kadiri. No individual breeder is named. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The retrieved pages name no breeder for K-134.
BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Developing station: Agricultural Research Station (ARS), Kadiri, Anantapuramu district, ANGRAU. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: THIS VARIETY IS SUITABLE FOR LATE SOWN CONDITIONS ALSO IN ANDHRA PRADESH DURING THE KHARIF SEASON.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : THE HEIGHT OF MAIN AXIS RANGES FROM 12-15 CM; KADIRI-3 (ROBOUT 33-1) IS OF VIRGINIA BUNCH HABIT. REACTION OF THE VARIETY TO DISEASES WAS NOT TESTED UNDER CONTROLLED CONDITIONS.

drought.details: The digest reports better tolerance of drought imposed from flowering to pod filling (PMD_30). It is also described as adapted to low-input rainfed cultivation (agropedia). The digest gives no quantitative drought measure, so the level is an inference from the qualitative statement. The original CSC data states the variety can tolerate mid-season drought.

flood.details: Flood tolerance: no evidence found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Rust: resistant (PMD_30 and the IPM review list rust resistance; the compendium lists it as resistant; the CSC data describes it as highly resistant). Late leaf spot (LLS): resistant/tolerant (PMD_30; compendium lists it as resistant; CSC data describes it as tolerant). Peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND): the compendium lists it as resistant, while the Purdue table records moderate resistance; the CSC data describes it as field tolerant, so the level is inconsistent across sources. Stem and pod rot (Sclerotium rolfsii) and peanut mottle virus under artificial inoculation are reported as tolerant in the CSC data only; not found in searched sources. The variety was advanced in rainy-season disease nurseries with infector rows where rust and LLS occur naturally (agropedia).

pest_resistance.summary: Groundnut leaf miner: moderately resistant under field conditions, with lower larval counts than TMV 2 (PMD_30); CSC data describes it as less susceptible than national varieties. Other insects: reaction similar to other national varieties (CSC data only). Aphids: listed as aphid-resistant in a commercial grower booklet; this is a low-reliability source and the name is misspelt there as '1CGV-87160', so this attribution is unverified.

agronomic_details.yield: Compendium: pod yield 2,200 kg/ha; kernel yield 1,475 kg/ha. Average pod-yield advantage of about 20% over JL 24 in AICRPO trials (Zone V, rainy seasons 1983-86), with larger gains over other checks. CSC data gives an average yield of 2,500 to 4,200 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Pod-yield superiority over local cultivars was reported in Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the Philippines and Niger (agropedia). No multi-environment stability statistic was found in the digest.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for kharif (rainy) season in the peninsular zone where rust and late leaf spot are a problem (CSC data). Adapted to low-input rainfed cultivation (agropedia). Recommended for Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka and part of Maharashtra during the rainy season (CSC data).
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 105 To 124Days (CSC data). The digest gives about 115 days in the rainy season (PMD_30 and compendium).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Seed colour: tan (CSC data). Mainly 2-seeded stubby pods; 100-seed mass 36 g; 67% average shelling outturn (PMD_30). Oil 47.8% (compendium, PMD_30). Protein 27% (PMD_30; CSC data 26.6%). Being foliar-disease resistant, it is reported to produce better fodder both qualitatively and quantitatively (CSC data). Pods are not attractive to farmers in some regions, which limited acceptance (germplasm enhancement report).
agronomic_details.field_trials: AICRPO trials, Zone V, rainy seasons 1983-86 (Table 1, PMD_30): about 20% average pod-yield advantage over JL 24 and larger gains over other checks. Compendium pod yield 2,200 kg/ha and kernel yield 1,475 kg/ha. Multi-location trials in Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the Philippines and Niger showed pod-yield superiority over local cultivars (agropedia). Foliar disease scores (rust, LLS) were recorded in field tables (PMD_30). Groundnut leaf miner larval counts were lower than TMV 2 (PMD_30). Trial-level data beyond these summaries was not found in searched sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Rust resistant and tolerant of late leaf spot (LLS) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf
- Rust resistance is also cited in the IPM review, which lists it among varieties with disease resistance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/226951051_Integrated_pest_management_in_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_in_India
- Shows better tolerance of drought imposed from flowering to pod filling -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf
- Adapted to low-input rainfed cultivation, and was advanced in rainy-season disease nurseries with infector rows where rust and LLS occur naturally -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/groundnut-variety-icgv-87160-icgfdrs-10
- Compendium lists it as resistant to rust, LLS and peanut bud necrosis disease (PBND) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- Salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: no evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST
- Moderately resistant to groundnut leaf miner under field conditions, with lower larval counts than TMV 2 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf
- Moderate resistance to PBND is tabulated for this cultivar -- https://caps.ceris.purdue.edu/wp-content/uploads/2025/12/Radhakrishnan-2023.pdf
- Listed as an aphid-resistant variety in a commercial grower booklet. This is a low-reliability source and the name is misspelt there ("1CGV-87160") -- https://www.jains.com/PDF/Crop%20Knowledge/Groundnut.pdf
- Foliar disease scores (rust, LLS) in field tables -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration about 115 days in the rainy season, with 67% average shelling outturn -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf
- Compendium gives pod yield 2,200 kg/ha, kernel yield 1,475 kg/ha, oil 47.8%, 115 days -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- Average pod-yield advantage of 20% over JL 24 and larger gains over other checks in AICRPO trials. Table 1 covers Zone V, rainy seasons 1983–86 -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf
- Pod-yield superiority over local cultivars in Bangladesh, Myanmar, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the Philippines and Niger -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/groundnut-variety-icgv-87160-icgfdrs-10
- Pods are not attractive to farmers in some regions, which limited acceptance -- https://oar.icrisat.org/3214/1/germplasm_enhancement_in_groundnut.pdf
- Seed traits: mainly 2-seeded stubby pods, 100-seed mass 36 g, 48% oil, 27% protein -- https://oar.icrisat.org/537/1/PMD_30.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Pedigree (Ah 65 × NC Ac 17090) F2-B1-B1-B2-B1-B1-B1-B2, with NC Ac 17090 a rust-resistant Valencia germplasm line -- http://agropedia.iitk.ac.in/content/groundnut-variety-icgv-87160-icgfdrs-10
- Compendium records the pedigree as Ah-65 × NCAc-17090 and the breeding method as bulk pedigree -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- Derivative: SG 99 (PAU Ludhiana, 2007) was bred from ICGV-86829 × ICGV-87160 -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- QTL, marker, genome-sequence or breeding-line code evidence: no evidence found. The QTL-seq result found concerns different lines (ICGV 00350 × ICGV 97045) and was discarded.

drought.details: The digest reports that Abhaya withstands a dry spell of up to 35 days and is water-use efficient (ANGRAU groundnut varieties sheet and RARS research varieties document). It is also listed as tolerant of early-season and mid-season moisture stress (Springer groundnut breeding chapter). Low-light tolerance is reported in the ANGRAU sheet. A drought field trial at Perambalur under flowering-stage moisture stress tested Abhaya among six genotypes, but Dharani gave the highest seed yield under stress, so Abhaya was not the top performer. The level is rated medium because the tolerance claims are consistent across sources, but the only field comparison did not place Abhaya first.

disease_resistance.summary: Late leaf spot (LLS): reported as tolerant (Springer groundnut breeding chapter; ANGRAU groundnut varieties sheet; RARS research varieties document). Rust, rosette, YMV and other diseases: no evidence found for Abhaya specifically. The RARS document reports a YMV-resistant line TBG 104 identified by marker-assisted selection, but that is a different line and is not attributed to Abhaya.

pest_resistance.summary: Tolerant of sucking pests (jassids and thrips) and Spodoptera litura (Springer groundnut breeding chapter). No other pest evidence found.

agronomic_details.yield: Input record (commercial product): Kharif 2300 kg/ha; Rabi 3756 kg/ha. Digest yield potential (ANGRAU sheet): 16-26 q/ha in kharif and 37-43 q/ha in rabi. Other traits: 100-seed weight 40-43 g; shelling out-turn 75-77% (RARS table); high sound mature kernel (SMK) percentage with uniform maturity.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. Responds to increased plant population to a moderate degree (input record). Comes up well under low-input conditions (input record).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for kharif (rainfed and irrigated) and rabi (irrigated) seasons (input record; ANGRAU sheet). Reported popular in several states (see variety_profile).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: COMPACT PLANT TYPE, LEAFLETS NARROW AND DARK GREEN AND LEAFLETS MARGINS ARE WAVY ; PODS ARE SLENDER MOSTLY 3-SECONDS AND RETICULATED. Digest also lists moderate stature and attractive pods. Maturity conflict: the ANGRAU sheet gives 90-95 days (very early), while the RARS table and input record give 105-110 days. Recheck before recording.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Drought field trial, Perambalur (flowering-stage moisture stress): Abhaya was among six genotypes tested. Dharani gave the highest seed yield under stress, so Abhaya was not the top performer. (2) Early kharif trial with plant populations: Abhaya gave lower pod and oil yield than Kadiri-6 and Dharani, and had a lower harvest index. (3) Seed quality study (Legume Research, PCA and path analysis): Abhaya is among the best genotypes for shelling percentage, alongside TAG-24. (4) A land configuration (ridge and furrow) comparison using TPT-25 was reported in a case study, but the page gives no clear Abhaya-specific result and the name match is unclear, so it is excluded. (5) A nutritive value study of commonly used groundnut varieties in Andhra Pradesh drylands is listed in the publications, but no Abhaya-specific results were given in the digest.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought: withstands a dry spell of up to 35 days, and is water-use efficient -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf ; https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/Research_Varieties.pdf
- Moisture stress: listed as tolerant of early and mid-season moisture stress -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23112-5_8
- Low light: tolerant of low-light conditions -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf
- Drought field trial (flowering-stage moisture stress, Perambalur): Abhaya was among six genotypes tested; under stress, Dharani gave the highest seed yield, so Abhaya was not the top performer -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/349813832_Studies_on_Drought_Tolerant_and_High_Yielding_Groundnut_Varieties_in_Perambalur_District

DISEASE AND PEST
- Late leaf spot (LLS): tolerant -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23112-5_8 ; https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf ; https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/Research_Varieties.pdf
- Sucking pests (jassids and thrips) and Spodoptera litura: tolerant -- https://link.springer.com/chapter/10.1007/978-3-030-23112-5_8
- Rust, rosette, YMV and other diseases: No evidence found for Abhaya specifically. The RARS document reports a YMV-resistant line TBG 104 identified by marker-assisted selection, but that is a different line and is not attributed to Abhaya -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/Research_Varieties.pdf

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity: very early, 90-95 days -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf
- Maturity conflict: a second RARS table gives 105-110 days for the same variety. Recheck before recording -- https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/Research_Varieties.pdf
- Yield potential: 16-26 q/ha in kharif and 37-43 q/ha in rabi -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf
- Other traits: uniform maturity, high sound mature kernel (SMK) percentage, attractive pods, moderate stature, and 100-seed weight 40-43 g. The RARS table also lists shelling out-turn 75-77% -- https://angrau.ac.in/downloads/CropVarities/Groundnut.pdf ; https://www.rarstpt.org/files/rars/Research_Varieties.pdf
- Seed quality: Abhaya is among the best genotypes for shelling percentage, alongside TAG-24 -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5075
- Early kharif trial with plant populations: Abhaya gave lower pod and oil yield than Kadiri-6 and Dharani, and had a lower harvest index -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/377500562_Growth_Characters_and_Yield_of_Early_Kharif_Groundnut_As_Influenced_By_Varieties_and_Plant_Populations
- Land configuration trial: the ridge and furrow comparison was run with TPT-25 and reported in a case study under broad-bed and furrow systems. The page does not give a clear Abhaya-specific result -- https://aaj.net.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/2010_article_572-5.pdf (name match unclear; treat as unverified)

drought.details: Multiple digest sources describe TMV (Gn)13 as drought tolerant: the ORS Tindivanam release table lists it as drought tolerant; the 2006 TNAU release list gives tolerance to terminal water stress as a special feature; and the TNAU Tindivanam crop-improvement page lists it as tolerant to terminal drought. The digest also states it is tolerant to early-season and mid-season moisture stress. Conflicting evidence: a rainfed Alfisol drought screen used TMV (Gn)13 as a genetic check and found no yield superiority over VRI (Gn) 7 under stress at that location. Level set to medium because the descriptive claims are consistent but one location-specific screen did not confirm yield advantage. No quantitative drought data were found in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Late leaf spot, rust and bud necrosis: no digest evidence specific to TMV (Gn)13. pest_resistance.summary: Sucking pests and defoliators: moderately resistant, as listed in the TNAU groundnut crop-production table against TMV Gn 13 and VRI Gn 6. Leaf miner and Spodoptera: not confirmed in the digest; the digest does not cover these for this variety. The digest does not address aphid or whitefly resistance for this variety, apart from the unconfirmed neighbouring-block entry noted under disease resistance.

agronomic_details.yield: Reported values vary by source. TNAU agritech page: 1613 kg/ha rainfed and 2580 kg/ha irrigated (average). ORS Tindivanam table: 2147 kg/ha. TNAU crop-production table: 2130 kg/ha rainfed and 2700 kg/ha irrigated. Erode on-farm trial: 2,580 kg/ha. These figures conflict and are not reconciled by the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources as a stability analysis. Trial results vary across locations and seasons (see field_trials).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed and irrigated conditions (as listed in the digest's agronomic data). Specific agro-climatic zones beyond the trial locations named in the digest are Not found in searched sources.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: DARK GREEN FOLIAGE ; LESS PROMINENT BEAK ; RED TESTA. Additional values from digest sources: ORS table reports 75.5% shelling, 30 g 100-kernel weight and 51.4% oil; TNAU agritech page reports 50% oil; TNAU crop-production table reports 70% shelling, 45-50 g 100-seed weight and 49% oil; Erode trial reports 44 g 100-seed weight. These seed-trait values conflict across sources. The ORS table also gives a duration of 95 days, which conflicts with the 100-105 day range.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) ORS Tindivanam release table: 2147 kg/ha. (2) TNAU agritech page: 1613 kg/ha rainfed and 2580 kg/ha irrigated. (3) TNAU crop-production table: 2130 kg/ha rainfed and 2700 kg/ha irrigated. (4) Erode on-farm trial: 2,580 kg/ha; TMV-13 yielded 1,924.5 kg/ha in a 2014 trial where ICGV-91114 was top. (5) TMV 14 trial, TMV Gn 13 as check: 1844 kg/ha in kharif and 1727 kg/ha in rabi irrigated. (6) Rainfed Alfisol drought screen: TMV (Gn)13 as genetic check showed no yield superiority over VRI (Gn) 7 under stress at that location. (7) TNAU Tindivanam page: sown on 27.3.2019 in an ongoing station trial; no yield result given.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: TMV (Gn)13, groundnut (Arachis hypogaea)

Name check: the variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "TMV (Gn)13". Seednet itself returned no page. The variety code A0402127 appeared in no result. All findings below refer to TMV (Gn)13 under that name, and all searched sources are TNAU, journal, or research pages.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Listed as red-kernelled and drought tolerant in the TNAU Oilseeds Research Station release table. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- Tolerance to terminal water stress and basal pod setting are listed as special features in the 2006 TNAU release list. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/TNAU%20vtys_2006.pdf
- The TNAU Tindivanam crop-improvement page lists TMV Gn-13 as tolerant to terminal drought, alongside a bud-necrosis tolerance entry for CO-3. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/crop-improvement/
- A rainfed Alfisol drought screen used TMV (Gn) 13 as a genetic check, and it did not show yield superiority over VRI (Gn) 7 under stress at that location. -- https://scialert.net/fulltext/?doi=ajar.2013.35.42

DISEASE AND PEST
- The 2006 TNAU release list reports resistance to root rot disease, root knot nematode and white flies and aphids, but that entry sits under a neighbouring variety block, so treat it as needing confirmation. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/TNAU%20vtys_2006.pdf
- Moderately resistant to sucking pest and defoliators is listed in the TNAU groundnut crop-production table against TMV Gn 13 and VRI Gn 6. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/05_Groundnut.pdf
- No evidence found for rust or late leaf spot scores specific to TMV (Gn)13. The rust and late-leaf-spot resistance results found concern TMV 14 and CO 7. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Duration, yield and seed-trait values vary between sources. The ORS table gives 95 days, 2147 kg/ha, 75.5% shelling, 30 g 100-kernel weight, and 51.4% oil. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- The TNAU agritech page gives 100–105 days, with average yields of 1613 kg/ha rainfed and 2580 kg/ha irrigated, and oil content of 50%. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/agriculture/grounnut%20TMVgn%2013.html
- The TNAU crop-production table gives 2130 kg/ha rainfed and 2700 kg/ha irrigated, 70% shelling, 45–50 g 100-seed weight, and 49% oil. These figures conflict with the other sources. -- https://tnagriculture.in/dashboard/CPG/05_Groundnut.pdf
- The Erode on-farm trial reports 100–105 days, 2,580 kg/ha, and 44 g 100-seed weight for TMV-13, and records TMV-13 at 1,924.5 kg/ha in a 2014 trial where ICGV-91114 was top. -- https://sadhnahp.com/storage/articles/August2025/ZF0a19ztQfUFNrp.pdf
- As a check in the TMV 14 trial, TMV Gn 13 yielded 1844 kg/ha in kharif and 1727 kg/ha in rabi irrigated. -- https://doaj.org/article/fc2c92a9a86244b39def39f3826126e9
- The TNAU Tindivanam page records TMV 13 as sown on 27.3.2019 in an ongoing station trial. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/ongoing-schemes/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage is a pureline selection from the Pollachi red local landrace. The release paper gives the breeding line code TNAU 325. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/93-7-12-150-154.pdf
- Breeding method: pureline selection from a local population (no hybridisation). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/crop_improvement/variety_released/TNAU%20vtys_2006.pdf
- Mutagenesis study: M3 populations from a TMV (Gn)13 pureline (gamma rays and EMS) were screened for the ahFAD2A mutation. The control was 35–39% oleic acid. -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5405
- No evidence found for mapped QTL, markers, or genome resources specific to TMV (Gn)13. The CPBG staff page lists TMV(Gn) 13 among groundnut varieties, but its context is unclear. -- https://sites.google.com/a/tnau.ac.in/cpbg/manivannancv

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The 2006 release paper lists the authors as V. Muralidharan, N. Manivannan, P. Vindhiyavarman, V. Manoharan, T.S. Raveendran, G. Umapathy and P. Devagi, from the Department of Oilseeds, TNAU, Coimbatore. The paper does not name a lead breeder. -- https://masujournal.org/store_file/archive/93-7-12-150-154.pdf
- Developing institution: Department of Oilseeds, Tamil Nadu Agricultural University, Coimbatore. The Oilseeds Research Station at Tindivanam is the station that released and tests the variety. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/varieties-released/
- The Oilseeds Research Station, Tindivanam was established to evolve groundnut, sesame and castor varieties. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tindivanam (Wikipedia page, lower reliability)

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level, as no breeder contact was found)
- The Professor and Head, Oilseeds Research Station, Erayanur, Tindivanam 604 002, Villupuram district. Phone 04147 250293. E-mail arstvm@tnau.ac.in. -- https://tnau.ac.in/site/ors-tindivanam/contact-us/
- The TNAU Seed Centre, Coimbatore 641 003, handles seed-stock enquiries through the Director (Seeds). -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/TNAU%20-%20Seed%20stock%20position%20as%20on%2002.09.2022%20-%20English.pdf
- No evidence found for a personal breeder e-mail or phone for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS
- Muralidharan V, Manivannan N, Vindhiyavarman P, Manoharan V, Raveendran TS, Umapathy G, Devagi P (2006). A high yielding red kernel bunch groundnut variety TMV(Gn) 13. Madras Agricultural Journal 93(7-12): 150-154 -- https://doi.org/10.29321/MAJ.10.100742
- Parameswari K, Eevera T et al. (2023). Exploring the Storage Potential of Groundnut Var. TMV (Gn) 13 under Modified Atmospheric Storage Conditions. International Journal of Environment and Climate Change 13(10): 3982-3989 (Article IJECC.106749) -- https://journalijecc.com/index.php/IJECC/article/view/3072
- Authors not shown (year not shown). Genetic Improvement of Arachis hypogaea var TMV(Gn) 13 Through Induced Mutagenesis. Legume Research -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-5405
- No evidence found for KrishiKosh theses, AICRP reports, or QTL papers specific to this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found of TMV (Gn)13 stock quantities in the TNAU seed stock position documents. Those snippets list other groundnut varieties. -- https://agritech.tnau.ac.in/pdf/Seed%20Stock%20Position%20as%20on%2031.07.2021.pdf
- The Tindivanam ongoing

drought.details: The DOD variety table lists AK 265 as drought tolerant (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx). The supplied variety record also lists it as drought tolerant. A multi-environment drought study placed AK 265 among the less stable genotypes for pod yield and RUE under drought stress, so the drought rating is medium, reflecting conflicting evidence. The mechanisms behind the tolerance are Not found in searched sources. The name appears as "AK 265" (no hyphen) in the DOD and ICAR-DGR sources; the findings are treated as referring to this variety.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistant to foliar diseases, per the DOD variety table entry for AK 265. No specific pathogen resistance (for example late leaf spot, rust or stem rot) was found in searched sources.

pest_resistance.summary: Not found in searched sources. No specific pest resistance (for example thrips) was found.

agronomic_details.yield: Supplied variety record (not from a digest URL): average pod yield 1903 kg/ha and kernel yield 1336 kg/ha under normal conditions. The adaptation_ecology field of the same record gives kernel yield as 1136 kg/ha, which conflicts with the 1336 figure. The DOD table row for AK 265 shows the numbers 1903 and 47, but the column headers were not visible, so they are not assigned to yield or oil content (not verified).
agronomic_details.stability: AK 265 was placed among less stable genotypes for pod yield and RUE under drought stress in a multi-environment study (ResearchGate record; full text not available).
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation under rainfed conditions in southern Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh and Tamil Nadu (DOD and ICAR-DGR sources). Listed as a kharif season crop in the DOD table. Responsive to fertilizer; a basal dose of 25:50:30 kg NPK/ha plus micronutrients is suggested for higher yield, per the supplied variety record. Shelling outturn (68%), sound mature kernel (89%) and oil content (47%) are reported as highest in the supplied variety record, with no independent source in the digest.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: No multi-location or AICRP trial data specific to AK-265 was found. The one trial-type finding is a multi-environment evaluation (ResearchGate record) that placed AK 265 among less stable genotypes for pod yield and RUE under drought stress. Trial yield values are not available in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
AK-265 Groundnut: Evidence Digest

Name check: variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "AK-265". The ICAR-DGR compendium and the DOD page write it as "AK 265" (no hyphen). All findings below refer to this variety, not to AK 12-24, Akshay-54, Akshay Sweta, or other products.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Drought tolerant (DOD variety table entry for AK 265) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
- Multi-environment drought study: AK 265 was placed among less stable genotypes for pod yield and RUE under drought stress -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363586679_Multi-environment_evaluation_of_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_genotypes_for_fresh_seed_dormancy
- Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
- Resistant to foliar diseases (DOD variety table entry for AK 265) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
- Specific pathogen or pest resistance (e.g., late leaf spot, rust, stem rot, thrips): No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Recommended for kharif season (DOD variety table entry for AK 265) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
- Pod yield, maturity, oil content: a DOD table row for AK 265 shows the numbers 1903 and 47, but the column headers were not visible in the search result, so I cannot assign them to yield or oil. Not verified -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
- Maturity duration: No evidence found
- Multi-location or AICRP trial data specific to AK-265: No evidence found

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage: ICGS-11 x US-63 -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1 (third-party copy of the ICAR-DGR compendium)
- Breeding method: pedigree method (same compendium) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- Breeding-line codes, QTL/marker studies, genome resources: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: PDKV, Akola (compendium entry for AK-265) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found
- Station: the release entry names "Crop Research Unit (Oil Seeds), Dr. Panjabrao Deshmukh Krishi Vidyapeeth, Akola" (from the supplied variety record, not independently verified by search)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder contact: No evidence found
- Institute contact (PDKV Akola, Crop Research Unit Oil Seeds): no official email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL appeared in any search result. No evidence found

PUBLICATIONS
- Kumar N et al. (2019). Multi-environment evaluation of Spanish bunch groundnut genotypes for fresh seed dormancy. Journal not identified (ResearchGate record only; full text not available) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/363586679_Multi-environment_evaluation_of_Spanish_bunch_groundnut_genotypes_for_fresh_seed_dormancy
- ICAR-DGR (year not stated). Groundnut: a crop profile and compendium of notified varieties of India. Report (third-party copy) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1
- No PDKV-authored AK-265 papers, KrishiKosh theses, or AICRP reports found

SEED AVAILABILITY
- NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or private dealer listings for AK-265: No evidence found. The search returned Akshay-54 and Akshay Sweta listings, which are different products and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Southern Maharashtra, Karnataka, Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx and https://www.scribd.com/document/783262364/ICAR-DGR-Groundnut-a-Crop-Profile-and-Compendium-of-Notified-Varieties-of-India-1

No graded or quantitative drought assessment was found, so the level is a qualitative estimate. Mechanisms were not described in the digest. The name caveat applies: the digest refers to 'TG 37A' and 'TG-37A' interchangeably, and the Seednet form 'TG-37-A' does not appear verbatim in any retrieved page.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate tolerance (not full resistance) to collar rot, rust and late leaf spot (LLS) is reported for TG 37A. The release table also lists collar rot tolerance. Stem rot resistance specific to TG-37A: Not found in searched sources. The CSC record also lists 'moderately tolerant to collar rot, rust and late leaf spot', consistent with the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect or nematode resistance specific to TG-37A: Not found in searched sources. Note: the original CSC variety record (not a digest source) reports moderate tolerance to jassids, Spodoptera and leaf miner; the retrieved pages do not corroborate this, so it is not attributed here as evidence-based.

agronomic_details.yield: Digest: mean pod yield of 3375 kg/ha reported (about 55% of a comparison line); trial location and season not clearly stated, so location is unverified. The same CRSP document reports superiority over JL 24 in the rainy season (about 4425 kg/ha for the comparison, context truncated). These two figures are not internally consistent with the stated 55% ratio and should be treated with caution. Original CSC record: average yield 1200.00 to 1900.00 kg/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Multi-location adaptation is listed across Haryana, Rajasthan, Punjab, Uttar Pradesh, Gujarat, Orissa, West Bengal, Assam and North-Eastern states. No quantitative stability analysis (e.g., GxE, AMMI) was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended in the CSC record for Rajasthan, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Punjab under kharif. The 2003 PIB release identifies the variety for rabi cultivation in eastern and north-eastern states (Jharkhand, Orissa, West Bengal, Assam). Season suitability therefore differs between sources.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 110 To 115Days (CSC record). The digest found no maturity evidence for TG-37A itself.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: SEMI-DWARF PLANT HABIT (50-60 CM) ; COMPACT POD SETTING ; SMOOTH POD ; MORE NUMBER OF 3-SEEDED PODS. Digest additionally reports erect growth with sequential branching, medium leaflets, Vulgaris botanical type and Spanish bunch growth habit. Fresh seed dormancy of up to 15 days is reported.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) CRSP document RA_00417: mean pod yield of 3375 kg/ha (about 55% of a comparison line); location and season not clearly stated. (2) Same document: superiority over JL 24 in the rainy season (comparison about 4425 kg/ha, context truncated). (3) Release-table evidence (agrocrops) lists high yield and wider adaptability for TG 37A (2004). No AICRP/ICAR annual report, KrishiKosh thesis or peer-reviewed TG-37A trial paper was found.
