search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE (evidence refers to "TG 37A"/"TG-37A"; the Seednet form "TG-37-A" does not appear verbatim in any retrieved page)
- The female parent TG37A (TG 25 x TG 26) is described as high yielding, moderately tolerant to collar rot, rust and late leaf spot (LLS), drought tolerant, with fresh seed dormancy up to 15 days -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357622953_TG-37A_A_new_Trombay_groundnut_variety_with_wide_adaptation
- Release-table row lists "collar rot tolerance" and "high yield, wider adaptability" for TG 37A (2004) -- https://www.agrocrops.com/en/peanuts-quality/evolution-of-trombay-groundnut-(tg)
- Maturity: No evidence found (no maturity duration retrieved for TG-37A).
- Salinity, flood, submergence, heat: No evidence found.

DISEASE AND PEST (same name caveat as above)
- Moderate tolerance to collar rot, rust and LLS is reported for TG 37A (see stress entry above) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357622953_TG-37A_A_new_Trombay_groundnut_variety_with_wide_adaptation
- Collar rot tolerance listed in release table -- https://www.agrocrops.com/en/peanuts-quality/evolution-of-trombay-groundnut-(tg)
- Stem rot, insect or nematode resistance specific to TG-37A: No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS (evidence refers to "TG 37A")
- Growth habit: erect, sequential branching, semi-dwarf, medium leaflets -- https://eurekamag.com/research/004/339/004339984.php
- Botanical type Vulgaris, Spanish bunch growth habit -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357622953_TG-37A_A_new_Trombay_groundnut_variety_with_wide_adaptation
- Mean pod yield of 3375 kg/ha (about 55% of a comparison line) reported; the extracted text does not clearly state the trial location or season, so treat as unverified in location -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1201/1/RA_00417.pdf
- The same CRSP document reports a superiority over JL 24 in the rainy season (about 4425 kg/ha for the comparison, context truncated) -- https://oar.icrisat.org/1201/1/RA_00417.pdf
- Identified in 2003 for rabi cultivation in eastern and north-eastern states (Jharkhand, Orissa, West Bengal, Assam) -- https://archive.pib.gov.in/archive/releases98/lyr2003/rnov2003/18112003/r181120034.html
- Multi-location adaptation across Haryana, Rajasthan, Punjab, UP, Gujarat, Orissa, West Bengal, Assam and North-Eastern states is listed -- https://www.agrocrops.com/en/peanuts-quality/evolution-of-trombay-groundnut-(tg)

GENETICS AND QTL (evidence refers to "TG 37A")
- Parentage: TG 25 x TG 26 -- https://www.agrocrops.com/en/peanuts-quality/evolution-of-trombay-groundnut-(tg)
- Genomic basis: TG 26 was diversified with the Gujarat dwarf mutant to produce TG 37A, with TG 38 and TG 51 from related crosses -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357622953_TG-37A_A_new_Trombay_groundnut_variety_with_wide_adaptation
- Breeding method: mutation and recombination breeding at BARC -- https://www.agrocrops.com/en/peanuts-quality/evolution-of-trombay-groundnut-(tg)
- Breeding-line codes and marker/QTL studies specific to TG-37A: No evidence found (a QTL mention appeared in a search snippet but was not attributable to TG-37A in the retrieved text).

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION (evidence refers to "TG 37A")
- Developed by Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay -- https://archive.pib.gov.in/archive/releases98/lyr2003/rnov2003/18112003/r181120034.html
- Release authors: D M Kale, G S S Murty, A M Badigannavar (Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division, BARC) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357622953_TG-37A_A_new_Trombay_groundnut_variety_with_wide_adaptation
- Co-developer roles for Rajasthan Agriculture University, CSA University (Mainpuri) or the Trombay Nuclear Agriculture division contribution in the state release record: not verified by retrieved pages; only BARC is named as developer.

CONTACT DETAILS (evidence refers to "TG 37A")
- Name: A. M. Badigannavar (Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division, BARC) -- email anandmb@barc.gov.in -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/369817954_Advances_in_Mutation_Breeding_of_Groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L (also listed at https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/paper02.pdf)
- Institute address: Bhabha Atomic Research Centre, Trombay, Mumbai 400 085 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/236889514_Mutation_experiments_and_recent_accomplishments_in_Trombay_groundnuts
- Phone, postal contact page for the division: No evidence found.
- Not used: anandgnut@gmail.com (OSTI record) names Trombay groundnut varieties generally and not TG-37A in the retrieved text -- https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/21286520

PUBLICATIONS

Seed release note, IAN 24: 19 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357622953_TG-37A_A_new_Trombay_groundnut_variety_with_wide_adaptation (same paper indexed at https://eurekamag.com/research/004/339/004339984.php)

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
TG-51 (Groundnut). Four web searches were run. No Seednet portal page was retrieved; the sources use "TG 51" or "TG-51", so the evidence below is for the name as it appears in the sources, which matches both the CSC name and the Seednet name.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerant to stem rot and root rot, listed as suitable for the rabi-summer season -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx
Described as tolerant to stem rot and root rot and suited to rabi-summer cropping -- https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Listed as drought tolerant in an Odisha crop table (115 days, 17.0 q/ha) -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/groundnut/
Heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found

DISEASE AND PEST
Stem rot and root rot tolerance (see the two STRESS TOLERANCE sources above, which are the only TG-51-specific disease statements) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://www.agrifarming.in/high-yielding-groundnut-varieties-in-india-hybrid-cultivars-for-increased-profits
Insect pest resistance: No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Mean pod yield of 2675 kg/ha in AICRP-Groundnut Zone IV trials (rabi/summer, 2003/04 to 2005/06) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Groundnut.aspx ; https://www.researchgate.net/publication/344840903_Radiation_based_induced_mutagenesis_in_Trombay_groundnuts_Developments_and_accomplishments_In_IANCAS_Bulletin_Vol_XV_1
Zone IV AICRP trial table comparing TG 51 against checks TAG 24 and ICGS 44 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
About 90 days to maturity, with pod yield and shelling better than TG 26 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
Conflict: an Odisha table gives 115 days duration -- https://rkb-erm-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/groundnut/ (https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/groundnut/)
Summer irrigated trial, Bidhan Chandra Krishi Viswavidyalaya, West Bengal (2011 and 2012): pod yield 3320 kg/ha at 100% RDF plus 7.5 t/ha FYM -- https://arccjournals.com/journal/legume-research-an-international-journal/LR-3233
Nutrient trial: highest pod yield 2007 kg/ha with 100% RDP plus PSB plus FYM; 67.35% shelling -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
Western dry zone sowing date and NP fertilizer trial (2019 and 2020, BCKV Jhargram): TG 51 gave the highest values among TAG 24, TG 51 and TG 37A -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/273947812_Response_of_groundnut_Arachis_hypogaea_L_varieties_to_sowing_dates_and_NP_fertilizers_under_western_dry_zone_of_India
Uttarakhand hill agro-ecosystem trial (2022-23 and 2023-24): TG-51 gave higher pod yield and harvest index than TG-37A and Avtar, and matured early -- https://www.plantarchives.org/article/52%20EVALUATION-OF-GROUNDNUT-FOR-GROWTH,-YIELD-AND-SEED-QUALITY-FOR-CULTIVATION-IN-UTTARAKHAND-HILL-AGRO-ECOSYSTEM.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: TG 26 x Chico, crossed in 1998 at BARC -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
Spanish bunch type (Arachis hypogaea ssp. hypogaea), erect growth habit -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
Breeding method: mutation and recombination breeding; TG 51 is among five varieties evolved at BARC from mutants (with TG 26, TG 37A, TG 38, TPG 41) -- https://www.barc.gov.in/ebooks/9788196745349/complete.pdf
Earliness from Chico combined with the pod yield of TG 26 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
Breeding-line code before release: No evidence found
QTL, marker or genome-resource studies on TG-51: No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Authors Kale DM, Murty GSS, Badigannavar AM and Dhal JK, Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division, BARC, Trombay, Mumbai 400 085 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357204995_New_Trombay_groundnut_variety_TG_51_for_commercial_cultivation_in_India
Badigannavar AM, Murty GSS and Kale DM listed at the Nuclear Agriculture and Biotechnology Division, BARC, Trombay, Mumbai 400 085 (general TG review; TG-51 not named in the retrieved text) -- https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/21007706 (excluded from TG-51 claims)
Release notified for West Bengal, Orissa, Bihar and North Eastern States, announced by BARC's Founder's Day address (Dr. Srikumar Banerjee, 30 Oct 2009) -- https://www.barc.gov.in/presentations/fddir09.pdf
BARC Trombay groundnut variety list (TG-51 entry, pp. 9-10) -- https://www.barc.gov.in/group/66_s246.pdf

seednet_fields.Parentage: Girnar 1 x ICGS 11
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the States of West Bengal, Orissa and Manipur under Kharif rainfed condition. Early maturity - 108 days. Average Yield - 15.20 Qtl./ha.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: The proposed variety responded well to the higher than recommended doses of phosphatic fertilizers i.e. Girnar 3 (PBS 12160) gave a pod yield of 1560 Kg/ha at 90 Kg P2O5 compared to 60 Kg.ha of P2O5 was 14%.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: - Leaflet size: Small; - Leaflet shape: Elliptic; - Leaflet colour: Green; - Flowering pattern on side branches: Sequential; - Flowering on main stem: Absent; - Inflorescence: Multiple; Kernel size : small; testa colour : rose; 100-seed mass : 34 (31 to 37) g; oil content (%) : 45 (42 to 49); sound mature kernels (%) : 84 (78 to 92).
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 17-22 cm; b) DIstinguishing morphological Characters: - Growth habit: Intermediate: semi-erect to erect, decumbent-3; - Branching pattern: Irregular: without flowers on mains tem; but with flowering on n+1, n+2 branches
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Girnar 3 (PBS 12160) has low specific leaf area and high chlorophyll meter reading (SCMR) and these attributes onfer water use efficiency.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: The proposed variety was comparable with both the check and qualifying varieties for the incidences rust and late leaf spot.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: For thrips, the vector of PBND, the proposed variety, Girnar 3 (PBS 12160), has shown a lower incidence (12.8%) then that shown by national check, JL-24 (18.3%).

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: Agril. Research Station, ANGR Agril. University, Kadiri - 515 591 (A.P.)
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: Recommended for release and cultivation in the State of Karnataka and Maharashtra under timely sown irrigated condition in Rabi and Summer season. Medium maturity - 122 days, Average yield - 55.06 Qtl./ha (Pod) and 38.74 (Kernel)
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: HKW (41g) is higher than checks (37-38 g) and qualifying entry (35 g), Oil %, SMK% and Shelling % are 1% higher than qualifying entry over years and locations.
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: - Constriction: None; - Reticulation: Slight; - Shelling out turn (%): 68; - Kenel size: Medium; - Testa Colour: Rose; - 1000 Kernedl wt. (g): 41; - Oil content (%): 48; - SMK (%): 90.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: a) Plant height: 35-40 cm; b) Distinguishing morphological Characters: - Leaf shape: Lanceolate; - Leaf size: Medium; - Foliage colour: Dark green; - Growth habit: Spanish bunch (Erect); - Pod beak: Slight; - Pod size: Medium; - Kernel nature: Mostly 2 seeded
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: Evemn in severe drought years also, K 1319 gave 67% higher pod yield and 46% kernel yield over JL 24 and 62% and 38% higher pod and kernel yields in station trial and 16.5% in MLTG over 9 locations for 3 years over a drought tolerant variety Vemana.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: Multiple disease resistance for Rust, ELS, LLS 93.2 to 4.7 score), Stem rot, PSND and PBND (3.2 to 3.5%). The scores are less in K1319 when compared to all the checks and qualifying entries.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: Multiple insect pests Thrips are the carriers and vectors of many viral diseases such as PSND and PBND; K1319 is tolerant to thrips (5.4%) when compared to checks. K 1319 also showed tolerance to Spodoptera, Helicoverpa and Jassids over locations and years.

drought.details: The DOD variety record describes the variety as suited to kharif semi-spreading groundnut and as tolerant to collar rot. A news feature lists Kadiri Harithandhra among highly drought-resistant ARS Kadiri releases, alongside Kadiri 9, Dharani and Kadiri Anantha. A climate-resilience review describes it as suitable for rainfed conditions because of drought tolerance, early duration and higher pod yield. In the scarce rainfall zone trial it gave the highest pod yield among tested entries (see field_trials). The level is rated high on the strength of the repeated drought-resistance descriptions; no drought-scoring data (e.g., drought-index values or physiological traits) were found in the digest. The digest does not name the drought mechanism (e.g., escape, avoidance or tolerance).

disease_resistance.summary: Collar rot: the DOD variety record describes the variety as tolerant to collar rot. Multiple diseases (unspecified): the DOD record describes it as resistant to multiple diseases and insect pests. A varietal comparison table describes it as resistant to several diseases and pests, with a conclusion on phenotypic disease resistance; the source states this is not a formal scientific trial and gives the name as Kadiri Haritandhra. A news feature states it is resistant against drought, diseases, pests and aflatoxin, as stated for four ANGRAU groundnut varieties including this one. No specific pathogen or disease scoring (e.g., leaf spot, rust, late leaf spot, aflatoxin test values) was found for this variety in the digest.

pest_resistance.summary: Insect pests: the DOD record describes resistance to multiple insect pests, and a news feature states resistance against pests for this variety as one of four ANGRAU varieties. No pest-specific scoring (e.g., thrips, Spodoptera, Helicoverpa, jassids) was found in the digest. Fresh seed dormancy of up to about 20 days is described in the DOD record (not a pest trait). Note: a nutritive-value study and other sources in the digest were not used for pest attribution.

agronomic_details.yield: Scarce rainfall zone (rainfed red soils, Andhra Pradesh): pod yield 1155 kg/ha, about 36.4% above check K-6 (847 kg/ha). Seed-rate trial (five varieties): highest dry pod yield of 2309 kg/ha versus 1126 kg/ha for K-6. National or average yield figures were not found in the digest.
agronomic_details.stability: Performance reported across the scarce rainfall zone trial and seed-rate trial, and as not the top entry in the Godavari zone trial (see field_trials). Stability across years and locations was not quantified in the digest. Conflicting report: a nutritive-value study describes Kadiri-Harithandra as less productive in haulm yield.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Rainfed scarce rainfall zone of Andhra Pradesh (red soils), where it was credited with resistance to several biotic and abiotic stresses. The DOD record recommends it for the rabi-summer season, while also describing it as suited to kharif semi-spreading groundnut; the digest does not resolve this difference. The Godavari zone (rabi 2022-23) trial is also recorded (see field_trials).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: - Constriction: None; - Reticulation: Slight; - Shelling out turn (%): 68; - Kenel size: Medium; - Testa Colour: Rose; - 1000 Kernedl wt. (g): 41; - Oil content (%): 48; - SMK (%): 90. Additional digest detail: fresh seed dormancy of up to about 20 days (DOD record). Growth habit: semi-spreading (DOD record). Note: the morphological values above are taken from the variety record supplied with the request; the digest does not independently confirm them.
agronomic_details.field_trials: 1) Scarce rainfall zone trial (Andhra Pradesh, rainfed red soils): pod yield 1155 kg/ha, about 36.4% above check K-6 (847 kg/ha); best rainwater-use efficiency (2.33 kg/ha/mm) and benefit-cost ratio (2.44) among tested entries. 2) Seed-rate trial (name given as Kadiri Harithandra, five varieties): highest dry pod yield at 2309 kg/ha versus 1126 kg/ha for K-6; optimum seed rate of 270 kg/ha suggested. 3) Godavari zone rabi 2022-23 trial (Agricultural College Farm, Rajamahendravaram, ten entries): Kadiri Harithandhra was entry T8, but Kadiri Lepakshi outperformed it, so it was not the top entry. 4) Nutritive-value study (Dryland Andhra Pradesh): describes Kadiri-Harithandra as less productive in haulm yield. 5) A seed-quality/physical-property study on kernels and pods of four varieties is recorded, but it is not a yield trial and the digest does not clearly attribute its results to this variety, so no results are reported.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Kadiri Harithandhra (K 1319) is described as suited to kharif semi-spreading groundnut and as tolerant to collar rot -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx (DOD variety listing; the same figures appear on the earlier http://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx page)
Listed among highly drought-resistant ARS Kadiri releases, alongside Kadiri 9, Dharani and Kadiri Anantha -- https://in.thedollarbusiness.com/magazine/groundnut---time-to-not-hold-ground/22634
Described as suitable for rainfed conditions because of drought tolerance, early duration and higher pod yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388175110_Climate_Resilient_Technologies_for_Enhancing_Groundnut_Productivity_Under_Rainfed_Conditions
Scarce rainfall zone trial credits Harithandhra with resistance to several biotic and abiotic stresses (the trial itself is recorded under AGRONOMY AND TRIALS) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358749421_Evaluation_of_climate_resilient_varieties_of_groundnut_for_scarce_rainfall_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
Stable yields of about 15-20 q/ha under severe drought are attributed to "Kadiri Harithandra" on a Kadiri Lepakshi performance page; the passage is ambiguous about which variety it describes, so treat as low-confidence -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375506325_Performance_of_Kadiri_Lepakshi_K-1812_groundnut_in_Anantapuram_district_of_Andhra_Pradesh_India

DISEASE AND PEST
Described as resistant to multiple diseases and insect pests, with fresh seed dormancy of up to about 20 days -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
Described as resistant to several diseases and pests in a varietal comparison table with a conclusion on phenotypic disease resistance (name given as Kadiri Haritandhra, not a formal scientific trial) -- https://www.agrocrops.com/en/peanuts-quality/new-improved-varieties-of-peanuts
Resistant against drought, diseases, pests and aflatoxin, as stated for four ANGRAU groundnut varieties including this one -- https://in.thedollarbusiness.com/magazine/groundnut---time-to-not-hold-ground/22634
No evidence found for specific pathogen or insect scoring (e.g., leaf spot, rust, aflatoxin test values) for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity of 110-115 days in kharif season -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/375506325_Performance_of_Kadiri_Lepakshi_K-1812_groundnut_in_Anantapuram_district_of_Andhra_Pradesh_India
Recommended for rabi-summer season (DOD) -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
Scarce rainfall zone of Andhra Pradesh, rainfed red soils: pod yield 1155 kg/ha, about 36.4% above check K-6 (847 kg/ha); best rainwater-use efficiency (2.33 kg/ha/mm) and benefit-cost ratio (2.44) among tested entries -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/358749421_Evaluation_of_climate_resilient_varieties_of_groundnut_for_scarce_rainfall_zone_of_Andhra_Pradesh
Seed-rate trial (name given as Kadiri Harithandra): highest dry pod yield 2309 kg/ha among five varieties versus 1126 kg/ha for K-6; optimum seed rate of 270 kg/ha was suggested -- https://www.thepharmajournal.com/archives/2022/vol11issue4/PartN/11-4-28-230.pdf
Godavari zone rabi 2022-23 trial (Agricultural College Farm, Rajamahendravaram): Kadiri Harithandhra was entry T8 among ten, but Kadiri Lepakshi outperformed it, so it was not the top entry -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/388846242_Assessment_of_Yield_and_Economic_Performance_of_Groundnut_Cultivars_in_the_Godavari_Zone_Andhra_Pradesh_India
Conflicting report: a nutritive-value study describes Kadiri-Harithandra as less productive in haulm yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/271522352_Nutritive_Value_of_Commonly_Used_Groundnut_Varieties_in_Dryland_Areas_of_Andhra_Pradesh
Seed-quality/physical-property study on kernels and pods (not a yield trial) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/346824507_Physico-Chemical_Properties_of_Four_Selected_Groundnut_Varieties

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage given as 91/57-2 x PI-476177 in a breeder-seed production table where K 1319 (Kadiri Harithandra) is entry 37 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/357544986_Genetic_Enhancement_of_Groundnut_Current_Status_and_Future_Prospects
Note: the parentage in the source table reads PI-476177, while the record gives P146177. Likely the same accession with an OCR or transcription difference, but unconfirmed; check against the CSC notification.
Breeding method, breeding-line codes, genes, QTL or markers for this variety: No evidence found.
Genomic resources page (ICRISAT, 2016) concerns groundnut in general and does not name this variety -- discarded from this heading: https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4794498/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by Agricultural Research Station (ARS) Kadiri, ANGRAU (Acharya N. G. Ranga Agricultural University), Kadiri, as listed in the DOD variety record -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Groundnut.aspx
Institution description: ARS Kadiri, established under ANGRAU, has developed groundnut varieties and includes Kadiri Harithandhra among its popular releases -- https://in.thedollarbusiness.com/magazine/groundnut---time-to-not-hold-ground/22634
Named breeder: K.S.S. Naik, listed as Technical Secretary to the Vice-Chancellor with groundnut R&D as the profile focus; the profile lists Kadiri Harithandra among CVRC national releases. Whether he was the lead breeder for this variety is not stated -- https://angrau.ac.in/angru/K_S_S_Naik.aspx
Naik is also quoted as Principal Scientist (Groundnut) and Head, ARS Kadiri -- https://in.thedollarbusiness.com/magazine/groundnut---time-to-not-hold-ground/22634
Lead breeder for K 1319 in the original release record: No evidence found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vaibhav (RK-1418), Indian mustard / rapeseed (Brassica juncea)

Name check: variety_name "Vaibhav (RK-1418)" and seednet_variety_name "VAIBHAV (RK-1418)" are the same variety under both headings. Every finding below refers to "Vaibhav (RK-1418)" unless noted. No Seednet portal page was returned by any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists here.

Searches run: 4 (variety/release; breeder/institution; research; seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- The ICAR-DRMR AICRP achievements page lists Vaibhav among the drought donors for rapeseed-mustard, alongside RH-819, Aravali mustard and RH-30. This is a donor role in the AICRP programme, not a per-variety tolerance score. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp_achievements.php
- No evidence found for salinity, heat, frost, flood or submergence tolerance specific to this variety. The same page lists other entries for those traits, but Vaibhav is not named for them.

DISEASE AND PEST
- An aphid screening study (Lipaphis erysimi) tested Vaibhav among 20 rapeseed-mustard varieties. The susceptibility order it reports places Vaibhav behind RLM 619, Varuna and Krishan. The snippet is partial, so the full ranking and scores were not verified. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341657316_Screening_of_rapeseed-mustard_varieties_against_mustard_aphid_Lipaphis_erysimi
- No evidence found for white rust, Alternaria blight, downy mildew or Sclerotinia resistance specific to Vaibhav.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- The CSAUAT Kanpur oilseeds page describes Vaibhav (RK-1418) as a rainfed variety for Zone III, released in 1985. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
- The CSAUAT page also contains a row of trial numbers for Vaibhav, but the column headers were not captured, so no yield or maturity values are attributed here.
- An IISD trade case study lists a "Vaibhav (RK-1467)" Indian mustard with a yield range of 1,300–1,500 and a value of 38 in an adjacent column. The code is RK-1467, not RK-1418, so this is NOT attributed to this variety. -- https://www.iisd.org/system/files/publications/trade_price_case_rapeseed.pdf
- No evidence found for maturity days, oil content or seed yield specific to RK-1418 from the pages retrieved.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Donor status for drought in the AICRP programme (see STRESS TOLERANCE above). -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp_achievements.php
- Parentage (Varuna and Keshri CSU-10 as economic parents; 1B-1775, 1B-1866 and 1B-1786 as donor parents, via biparental crossing) was supplied in the request and was NOT confirmed by any retrieved page. No evidence found online for this parentage.
- No evidence found for QTL, marker studies, or genome resources for RK-1418.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The CSAUAT Kanpur oilseeds page credits R.K. Dixit, A.N. Srivastav, Lalta Prasad, S.P. Sacchan, O.S. Verma and K.P. Verma with the release. -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
- Developing institution: Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture & Technology (CSAUAT), Kanpur, Oilseeds Section, as shown on the CSAUAT page above.
- The mention of "Mathur Vaibhav" on the GBPUAT AICRP report is a researcher's name in an unrelated citation and was discarded. -- https://www.gbpuat.res.in/uploads/aicrp/11.%20AICRP-%20Rapseed%20Mustard.pdf

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute-level only: the CSAUAT Kanpur oilseeds section page (https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/) names the section and an organogram link, but no email, phone or postal address for it was captured.
- No breeder email, phone or address was found.
- Not a contact for this variety: ICAR-Indian Institute of Rapeseed-Mustard Research (ICAR-IIRMR), Sewar, Bharatpur 321303, Rajasthan, is the AICRP-RM coordinating institute and was not shown to be the developer. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/apart_adv.php

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (2020 estimated from the ResearchGate ID; not verified). Screening of rapeseed-mustard varieties against mustard aphid (Lipaphis erysimi). Annual Progress Report of AICRP on Rapeseed & Mustard (cited within the paper). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/341657316_Screening_of_rapeseed-mustard_varieties_against_mustard_aphid_Lipaphis_erysimi
- No evidence found for peer-reviewed papers, theses (KrishiKosh) or conference papers specifically on RK-1418. The KrishiKosh and journal searches were not run as separate queries within the 4-search limit.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- No evidence found. The only "Vaibhav" hit was a Jaipur company (Vaibhav Enterprises) selling yellow mustard seed, which is a similarly named business and was discarded. -- https://dir.indiamart.com/jaipur/yellow-mustard-seed.html
- No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for RK-1418 was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- U.P., M.P. and Rajasthan, per the CSAUAT page, which records the release region as "U.P., M.P. Rajasthan". -- https://csauk.ac.in/oil-seeds-section/
- The request's recommended-states field ("MADHYA PRADESH" / "UTTAR PRADESH") matches this in substance, and the CSAUAT page adds Rajasthan.

Open gaps: the Seednet portal entry (code A0403024), maturity, yield, parentage verification, and breeder contact details were not retrieved. These need a direct check of seednet.gov.in, the CSAUAT site, and KrishiKosh.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
Search coverage was incomplete. The tool quota ran out after my four web_search calls, so I could not run the separate seednet, breeder-contact, or stress-trait queries. Most headings below have no verified evidence. Snippets were also truncated, so I have not confirmed details beyond what is listed.

Variety names: "Narendra Rai (NDR-8501)" (search name, from the release minutes) and "NARENDRA RAI (NDR-8501)" (Seednet name). No search result was found on the Seednet portal, so I cannot say which name the evidence uses.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming this variety with drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence data.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page naming this variety with disease or pest resistance data was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: A 2025 Bangladesh Journal of Botany article reports field experiments on "a popular variety, Narendra Rai (NDR-8501)" conducted in 2020-21 and 2021-22 at a station that the snippet cut off. Treatments, location, and results are unverified because the snippet was truncated. -- https://www.banglajol.info/index.php/BJB/article/download/82256/53700

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): The parentage given in the input is "selection from the material collected from Atwa (U.P.)". I did not find this in any search result, so it is unverified. No QTL, marker, or genome-resource evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No breeder name was found in any result. The institution named in the input (Seed Production Unit of N.D. University of Agriculture & Technology, Narendra Nagar (Kumargan), Faizabad) is not confirmed by a search result. An NDUAT crop-variety list PDF was returned (https://nduat.org/Doc/Crop-Varieties-Developed-by-NDUAT.pdf), but the visible portion did not include this variety, so I have not attributed it to NDUAT. No evidence found on the lead breeder.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No email, phone, address, or contact page for the institute or the breeding division was returned in any search result.

PUBLICATIONS:
Bangladesh Journal of Botany, 54(2): 261-267 (2025). Field study on Narendra Rai (NDR-8501) mustard, 2020-21 and 2021-22. Full title not visible in the snippet. -- https://www.banglajol.info/index.php/BJB/article/download/82256/53700
Authors: not visible in the snippet.
Other results were discarded. A Semantic Scholar paper on nitrogen levels in mustard varieties under late sowing did not name NDR-8501 in the visible text, so I excluded it.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found on NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or dealer stock for this variety. The only result was a retail listing for generic yellow mustard seed (Amazon.in), which is a different product and was discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES: The input record lists Uttar Pradesh. I did not confirm this from any search result.

Next steps: run a Seednet/CSC notification query, a NDUAT or ICAR breeder query, and a KrishiKosh or AICRP query for NDR-8501 mustard when the quota resets.

disease_resistance.summary: Sclerotinia stem rot: Vasundhara is listed among Brassica genotypes screened under natural epiphytotic conditions, but the retrieved text does not show its reaction score. White rust and Alternaria: the CSC variety record states that artificial screening showed resistance at par with check varieties (no numeric or categorical level given). Major foliar diseases: the CSC record states the variety was observed to be fairly tolerant under field conditions. The digest itself has no independent confirmation of the CSC disease statements.

pest_resistance.summary: Mustard aphid: the CSC variety record states that resistance was observed at par with check varieties. The digest reports no evidence found for aphid or other pest resistance, so this statement is not independently confirmed. No other pests were documented.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vasundhara (CSC minutes name "Vasundhara"; Seednet name "VASUNDHARA"; variety code A0403049). Crop: Indian mustard / Brassica juncea (Seednet category: Indian rapeseed and mustard, yellow sarson). Name variants in the sources: "Vasundhra" (DRMR breeder seed indent), "Vasundara" (slide deck). Searches were run for variety/release, breeder/institute, research papers, and seed availability. Pages about other products, companies, places, or other RH lines were discarded.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The drought study on RH-725, RH-761, RH-30 and RH-749 does not name Vasundhara, so it was discarded -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s00344-025-11887-1

DISEASE AND PEST: Vasundhara is listed among Brassica genotypes screened against Sclerotinia stem rot under natural epiphytotic conditions, but the retrieved text does not show its reaction score -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394415974_Screening_of_Brassica_Spp_Genotypes_Against_Sclerotinia_Stem_Rot_under_Natural_Epiphytotic_Conditions
No evidence found for aphid or other pest resistance.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found for maturity, yield or trial data specific to Vasundhara. The DRMR 2020-21 Project Coordinator's report lists "Vasundhra" among entries in a trial list, but the yield and location context is not visible in the retrieved text -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL: Parentage is given as RH 839 x RH 30 in a genetic diversity study's abstract table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394482025_Multivariate_Analysis_of_Genetic_Diversity_in_Brassica_Species_for_Yield_and_Agronomical_Traits
The same parentage entry also appears in the Sclerotinia screening paper's table -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394415974_Screening_of_Brassica_Spp_Genotypes_Against_Sclerotinia_Stem_Rot_under_Natural_Epiphytotic_Conditions

A slide deck lists "Vasundara" among newly released mustard varieties, without a breeder or institute -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seed-production-technology-of-rapeseed-and-mustard/275557298
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The "Oilseed Section, Department of Genetics and Plant Breeding, CCSHAU" reference in the drought paper concerns other genotypes and was not attributed to Vasundhara.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: NRCDR-02 (variety_name and seednet_variety_name both "NRCDR-02"; crop Indian rapeseed and mustard, yellow sarson per Seednet)

Search coverage note: Four web_search queries ran, one per topic, and returned snippets only (about 300 characters each for the first batch). A second batch of calls hit the tool's server-side use limit, so I could not open the full pages. Several headings below therefore have no evidence, which may reflect the snippet-only retrieval rather than an absence of information. Treat this as a partial record.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page that states drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for NRCDR-02. The stability-analysis paper (below) reports trait data, not stress tolerance.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page in the results named NRCDR-02 together with a disease or pest reaction.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Stability analysis in Indian mustard [Brassica juncea (L.) Czern & Coss.] varieties, which lists 'NRCDR 02' among the varieties assessed for branching, seeds per siliqua, 1000-seed weight, siliquae per plant and seed yield per plant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750572_Stability_analysis_in_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_varieties (snippet only; the yield values and stability conclusions were not visible, so no yield figure is recorded here)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found for parentage (MDOC 43 x NBPGR 36, as supplied in the variety record), breeding method, or genome resources. The "Genomic Designing for Nutraceuticals in Brassica juncea" page (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/372382335_Genomic_Designing_for_Nutraceuticals_in_Brassica_juncea_Advances_and_Future_Prospects) was discarded because it does not name NRCDR-02.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No named breeder was found for NRCDR-02. The review "Hundred years of rapeseed-mustard breeding in India: Accomplishments and future strategies" lists NRCDR 02 among released varieties, which places it in the national breeding record, but the snippet gives no developing scientist (https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279554671_Hundred_years_of_rapeseed-mustard_breeding_in_India_Accomplishments_and_future_strategies). The institution in the variety record is the National Research Centre on Rapeseed-Mustard, Sewar, Bharatpur; this comes from the supplied record, not from a search result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No email, phone, postal address or institute contact page was returned by the searches. The supplied institution name is NATIONAL RESEARCH CENTRE ON RAPESEED MUSTARD, SEWAR, BHARATPUR; its contact page URL is not verified.

PUBLICATIONS
- Chauhan J S, Singh K H and Kumar A (2006). Hundred years of rapeseed-mustard breeding in India: Accomplishments and future strategies (review listing NRCDR 02 among varieties; full author list not confirmed in snippet). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/279554671_Hundred_years_of_rapeseed-mustard_breeding_in_India_Accomplishments_and_future_strategies
- Stability analysis in Indian mustard [Brassica juncea (L.) Czern & Coss.] varieties (authors, year and journal not confirmed in snippet). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/230750572_Stability_analysis_in_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_Coss_varieties

AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses and seednet.gov.in entries were not returned by the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The Seednet-oriented query returned no seed-agency, KVK, SAU or dealer page for NRCDR-02.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found in the searches for the states listed in the variety record (Delhi, Haryana, Punjab, Rajasthan). The supplied record gives these states, but no search result confirmed them. The general AICRP-RM overview (https://www.gcirc.org/fileadmin/documents/Bulletins/B25/B25_06Rapeseed.pdf) was discarded as it does not name this variety.

Suggested follow-up when the search limit resets: the seednet.gov.in variety page, the NRCRM (Bharatpur) website, the CSC release notification for 2007, and KrishiKosh for NRCDR-02 theses.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Agrani (SEJ-2), Indian rapeseed and mustard (yellow sarson)

Name check: the CSC name "Agrani (SEJ-2)" and the Seednet name are identical. The retrieved sources use "Pusa Agrani (SEJ-2)" or "Pusa Agrani (SEJ 2)", and I treated these as the same variety.

Search limit: the tool-call budget ran out during my second code run, so I could not open the full pages. Findings below come from the search snippets I could read, so several headings are thin. Where I could not confirm a point, I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No resistance data for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Pusa Agrani (SEJ-2) is described as the first early-maturing Indian mustard variety, at about 110 days, and as a substitute for toria. Source: IARI news item of 20 July 2023 -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-agrani-sej-2/
Pusa Agrani is listed among Indian mustard cultivars in an agronomic management overview. This is a general list, not variety-specific data. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258384157_Advances_in_Agronomic_Management_of_Indian_Mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czernj_Cosson_An_Overview
Multi-location yield or trial results: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Origin: a 1998 early mutant of Brassica juncea, described as a synthetic amphidiploid, is listed for Pusa Agrani (SEJ 2). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234143403_Assessment_of_seed_quality_and_oil_content_in_different_branches_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_cultivars_at_different_storage_intervals
Parentage as recorded in the CSC input: a derivative of a cross between an early-maturing B. juncea strain from North-Eastern India and a synthetic amphiploid of B. campestris var. toria × B. nigra. This comes from the supplied record, not from a search source.
Breeding-line codes, QTL and marker studies: No evidence found.
Variety code A0403106 is from the supplied record. No search source confirmed it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: IARI, New Delhi. Supported by the IARI news item (July 2023) and the supplied record, which lists the Division of Genetics, IARI, New Delhi-110012. -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-agrani-sej-2/
Lead breeder or scientist name(s): No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. No IARI Division of Genetics email, phone or contact-page URL was returned by the searches.
Postal address from the supplied record only: Division of Genetics, Indian Agricultural Research Institute, New Delhi-110012.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors not available (year not available). Assessment of seed quality and oil content in different branches of Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) cultivars at different storage intervals. Journal/report not confirmed from the snippet -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234143403_Assessment_of_seed_quality_and_oil_content_in_different_branches_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_cultivars_at_different_storage_intervals
This paper names Pusa Agrani (SEJ 2) among the cultivars studied. I did not confirm that it is a primary study of this variety.
No KrishiKosh, AICRP or ICAR annual report entries were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. The CSC record gives "Unknown". The searches returned no notification or state recommendation for this variety.

Suggested next steps: check the Seednet portal entry for A0403106, the CSC release minutes for the 2021 notification, and the IARI Division of Genetics page for breeder names and contacts. KrishiKosh and the AICRP rapeseed-mustard annual reports should also be searched directly.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
The search tool hit its usage limit during a repeat call, so I completed only the four initial searches. I reviewed only the first ~400 characters of each result, so some headings may be under-covered. Under the strict relevance rule, most headings have no supporting page in what I reviewed. Both variety names were searched; "Pusa Mustard 22 (LET-17)" and "Pusa Mustard 22 LET 17" appear in the same results. The Seednet name "Pusa Mustard 22 (LET - 17)" was not separately confirmed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches returned no page describing drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No page on disease or pest resistance for this variety was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Suitable for timely-sown irrigated conditions, with under 2% erucic acid, per a July 2023 IARI-linked news item on the variety -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-22-let-17/
Described as highly suitable for cultivation in the National Capital Region of Delhi (same page) -- https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-22-let-17/
Yield, maturity and multi-location trial data: No evidence found in the reviewed content.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage PUSA BARANI x ZEM-2 is from the input record only; no search page confirmed it -- input record, not verified.
Breeding-line code LET-17 appears in the variety name on the sources above; no other breeding-line detail was found.
Genome resources and QTL/marker studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Institution per input record: Indian Agricultural Research Institute (IARI), New Delhi -- input record, not verified by search. The July 2023 IARI-linked item (https://www.global-agriculture.com/seed-industry/pusa-mustard-22-let-17/) names IARI as the source.
Lead breeder or scientist names: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute postal address from input record: IARI, New Delhi-110 012 -- input record, not verified.
Email, phone, and institute contact page: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. The research search returned no paper, report or thesis specific to this variety. Pages on other mustard varieties (for example, Pusa Mustard 30) were excluded.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found for state-level recommendation. The input record lists "Unknown."
The DAC&FW Rapeseed-Mustard page lists Pusa mustard 22 (LET 17) among recommended varieties, and it includes a state-wise table of varieties notified under the Seed Act from 2008 to 2019. The state entries were cut off in the content I reviewed, so this variety's states remain unconfirmed -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Rapeseed.aspx

Recommended follow-up searches (not run): the CSC/AICRP release notification for the 2008 release, the SAU or IARI seed portal listing, and a KrishiKosh or Google Scholar search for "LET-17" with "Brassica juncea".

Searches run: 4 (variety/recommendation, breeder, research papers, seed availability). Neither "Sheela (LCK 9211)" nor "SHEELA (LCK 9211)" returned a Seednet page, so every finding below refers to the variety name as written in the CSC/record name, and only where the page names Sheela or LCK-9211 alongside linseed.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no variety-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Sheela. A water-stress study on three linseed varieties names none of them as Sheela. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4912539/ (checked, not relevant)

DISEASE AND PEST
Sheela appears in a linseed rust evaluation table (Frontiers review, which cites an AICRP linseed annual report for 2019-20). The table lists "Sheela" among genotypes evaluated for rust; no resistance rating is given. -- https://www.frontiersin.org/journals/nutrition/articles/10.3389/fnut.2023.1165580/full
Resistance to wilt, rust and powdery mildew is stated for "LC 2023" in several pages. These statements are not attributed to Sheela and are not used here. -- https://www.apnikheti.com/en/pn/agriculture/crops/oilseeds/linseed-flax

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for Sheela-specific yield, maturity, oil content or multi-location trial data. Generic crop guidance (seed rate, sowing depth, fertiliser doses) appears in pages that list Sheela only as one of several varieties, so it is not attributed to the variety. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/390872850_SCIENTIFIC_CULTIVATION_OF_LINSEED_AND_ITS_NUTRITIONAL_BENEFITS
The Odisha AICRP linseed trial (2021-22) used three unnamed check varieties, so it cannot be tied to Sheela. -- https://horizonepublishing.com/index.php/PST/article/view/10589

Parentage (LCK-9211 as a progeny selection from Gaurav × Janki) comes only from the supplied record. No search result confirmed it. No evidence found for QTL, marker or genome studies on Sheela.

drought.details: The CSC record describes NL-97 as tolerant to drought, based on high productivity in rainfed breeding and agronomy trials, and states that it yielded higher than Kiran under rainfed conditions. The digest reports that the variety is suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions in Vidarbha. Its rainfed sowing window is the last week of October, with irrigated sowing in the first week of November. The digest found no quantitative drought data (for example, yield under defined moisture-stress levels or stress indices) for NL-97. The level is therefore based on qualitative tolerance claims, not measured stress data, and the digest's own search found no drought data.

heat.details: No heat-stress data for NL-97 were found in the searched sources.

salinity.details: No salinity data for NL-97 were found in the searched sources.

flood.details: No flood data for NL-97 were found in the searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Alternaria blight: moderately resistant (AICRP varieties table; PDKV Nagpur page). Powdery mildew (Oidium lini): moderately resistant (AICRP varieties table; PDKV Nagpur page). NL-97 was one of 294 genotypes screened for powdery mildew in Odisha, but the snippet gives no reaction score, so no Odisha-based rating is available. Fusarium oxysporum wilt: tolerant (PDKV Nagpur page describes tolerance to wilt; a linseed health and breeding review lists NL-97 as tolerant to Fusarium oxysporum wilt). The CSC record also states tolerance to wilt.

pest_resistance.summary: Bud fly: moderately resistant (AICRP varieties table; PDKV Nagpur page). Entomology pages that mention bud fly screening and economic threshold work do not name NL-97, so they are excluded as general programme information and not variety-specific evidence. No other pest resistance data for NL-97 were found.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: 588 kg/ha seed yield. PDKV Nagpur page: average yield 600-1200 kg/ha. AICRP table: 800-1000 kg/ha. These figures conflict and are reported as published. In a sowing-date trial, PKV-NL-97 gave 8.44 q/ha (844 kg/ha), below PKV-NL-260 at 8.85 q/ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources (no multi-environment stability analysis was found). The CSC record states the variety is suitable for both rainfed and irrigated conditions.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Suitable for linseed-growing areas of Maharashtra in the rabi season under rainfed conditions (CSC). Suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions in Vidarbha (digest). Listed among varieties for Marathwada and Vidarbha districts in the ICAR-CRIDA contingency plan. Sowing window conflict: CSC gives the 2nd week of October; the PDKV Akola page gives the last week of October for rainfed and the first week of November for irrigated sowing. Seed rate 12-15 kg/ha (CSC) versus 25 kg/ha (PDKV Nagpur page). Spacing 30 cm between rows. Fertilizer 25 kg N + 25 kg P2O5/ha basal (CSC) versus 25:25:00 NPK kg/ha (PDKV Nagpur page). Non-lodging (CSC and PDKV Nagpur genotype table).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: FLOWERS-BLUE FLOWERED; MEDIUM TALL (50-55 CM); MATURITY:EARLY (115 DAYS). Also reported: 6-7 branches per plant, 59 capsules per plant, 1000-seed weight 6.8 g, oil content 42.1% (CSC and AICRP table) versus 44% (PDKV Nagpur page), erect habit, pale blue flowers and brown seed (genotype trait table). Duration conflict: a PDKV Akola page gives an average of 105 days (range 115-120), which the digest flags as needing checking.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Sowing-date trial with three linseed varieties: PKV-NL-97 gave 8.44 q/ha seed yield, below PKV-NL-260 at 8.85 q/ha. Location, year and authors were not shown in the snippet. (2) Nagpur-based sowing-date trial that included PKV-NL-97 alongside PKV-NL-260 and JLS-73; no NL-97 results were shown in the digest. (3) CSC record: NL-97 yielded higher than Kiran under rainfed conditions in breeding and agronomy trials; no numerical values were given. (4) Odisha powdery mildew screening of 294 genotypes including NL-97; no score for NL-97 was given. (5) ICAR-CRIDA contingency plan lists NL-97 for Marathwada and Vidarbha; this is a listing, not a trial result.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Genomic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers were developed from NL-97 DNA using next-generation sequencing. The analysis produced 2,183 contigs and 1,442 microsatellite-containing sequences from 8.8 Mb of data. A genomic library was also built from NL-97 using four restriction enzymes, with microsatellite-enriched clones captured. Individual marker names, positions and chromosome locations were not found in the digest.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: NL-97 (linseed)

Name note: the CSC minutes name and the SeedNet name are both NL-97. Akola and sowing-date sources write the same variety as PKV-NL-97, and the AICRP table writes it as NL 97. Findings below refer to that variety.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Suited to timely-sown rainfed conditions in the Vidarbha region; no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for NL-97 were found in the search results -- https://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm
- Its rainfed sowing window is the last week of October, and irrigated sowing is the first week of November -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4536

DISEASE AND PEST
- Rated moderately resistant to Alternaria blight, powdery mildew and bud fly in the AICRP varieties table -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- A PDKV Nagpur page describes it as moderately resistant to Alternaria and tolerant to wilt, with the same bud fly and powdery mildew resistance -- https://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm
- A review on linseed health and breeding lists NL-97 as tolerant to Fusarium oxysporum wilt -- https://justagriculture.in/wp-content/uploads/2024/12/44.-The-Multifaceted-Health-Benefits-of-Linseed-Nutritional-Components-and-Therapeutic-Implications-and-its-Breeding-Perspectives.pdf
- NL-97 was one of 294 genotypes screened for powdery mildew (Oidium lini) in Odisha; the snippet gives no reaction score for it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/302554772_Field_screening_of_linseed_genotypes_for_resistance_to_powdery_mildew_Oidium_lini_Skoric_in_the_north_central_plateau_zone_of_Odisha
- Entomology pages mention bud fly screening and economic threshold work, but do not name NL-97 -- https://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm (general programme; not variety-specific)

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Plant height 50-55 cm, blue flowers, 6-7 branches, 59 capsules per plant, 115-120 days duration, medium maturity -- https://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm
- Duration is also given as an average of 105 days (range 115-120) -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4536 (this conflicts with the 115-120 figure above and needs checking)
- Spacing 30 cm rows, 7-8 lakh plants/ha, seed rate 25 kg/ha, fertilizer 25:25:00 NPK kg/ha, 1000-seed weight 6.8 g, oil 44%, average yield 600-1200 kg/ha -- https://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm
- AICRP table gives yield 800-1000 kg/ha and oil 42.1% -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/ (conflicts with the 600-1200 kg/ha and 44% figures above)
- A sowing-date trial with three linseed varieties found NL-97 (as PKV-NL-97) gave 8.44 q/ha seed yield, below PKV-NL-260 (8.85 q/ha) -- https://www.academia.edu/81965424/Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_on_Yield_Attributes_Yield_and_Economics_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties (the trial's location, year and authors were not shown in the snippet)
- A Nagpur-based sowing-date trial also used PKV-NL-97 alongside PKV-NL-260 and JLS-73 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- ICAR-CRIDA contingency plan lists NL-97 among varieties for Marathwada and Vidarbha districts -- https://www.icar-crida.res.in/assets/img/Books/2005-06/Linseed.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL
- Parentage R-7 x RLC-4, breeding method pedigree -- https://www.pdkvacn.ac.in/aicrp-linseed.htm ; https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4536
- Conflicting parentage on a PDKV Akola page: "Seeta x RW-351" is listed with the NL-97 entry, and the same page also lists R-7 x RLC-4 -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4536
- Table of genotype traits lists NL-97 with parentage R-7 x RLC-4, Nagpur origin, erect habit, non-lodging, pale blue flowers, brown seed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354123394_Delineating_multivariate_divergence_heritability_trait_association_and_identification_of_superior_omega-3-fatty_acid_specific_genotypes_in_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L
- Genomic simple sequence repeat (SSR) markers were developed from NL-97 DNA by next-generation sequencing: 2,183 contigs and 1,442 microsatellite-containing sequences from 8.8 Mb of data -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/223995460_Development_of_genomic_simple_sequence_repeat_markers_for_linseed_using_next_generation_sequencing_technology
- A genomic library was built from NL-97 using four restriction enzymes, with microsatellite-enriched clones captured -- https://isor.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/vol-33-1.pdf

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The variety was released by the AICRP on Linseed at the College of Agriculture, Nagpur, under Dr. PDKV Akola -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4536
- Earlier the AICRP was at Akola (1985), moved to Nagpur in 1987 -- https://www.pdkv.ac.in/?page_id=4536
- Beena Nair is listed as Linseed Breeder and Incharge at Dr. PDKV, Nagpur -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed (no individual is named as NL-97's developer in the results)

CONTACT DETAILS
- Dr. Beena

disease_resistance.research_summary: Alternaria blight: moderately resistant (AICRP varieties table; PDKV Nagpur page). Powdery mildew (Oidium lini): moderately resistant (AICRP varieties table; PDKV Nagpur page). NL-97 was one of 294 genotypes screened for powdery mildew in Odisha, but the snippet gives no reaction score, so no Odisha-based rating is available. Fusarium oxysporum wilt: tolerant (PDKV Nagpur page describes tolerance to wilt; a linseed health and breeding review lists NL-97 as tolerant to Fusarium oxysporum wilt). The CSC record also states tolerance to wilt.

drought.details: The CSC record states Garima is tolerant to moisture stress. The level 'medium' is an interpretation of that statement, not a graded result. The digest found no independent tolerance evidence. A dryland study in eastern UP reports only agronomic response (100% RDF with a 30 kg/ha seed rate recommended), not tolerance, so it does not confirm the CSC claim. The CSC record also states the variety performs well with sowing up to one month late (to October 20), and that under rainfed conditions it responds best to 40 kg N/ha.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources. No flood tolerance evidence specific to Garima was returned.

disease_resistance.summary: Per the CSC record (user-supplied ground truth, not confirmed by any digest source): resistant to linseed rust; moderately resistant to powdery mildew, black tip (Alternaria blight) and wilt. The digest cites a review of a disease-loss study across six linseed genotypes, including Neelum, Garima and Chambal, with losses of 18.2 to 38.80%. The review does not give Garima's individual loss, so this cannot be attributed to Garima alone. No digest source independently confirms the rust, powdery mildew, Alternaria or wilt reactions.

pest_resistance.summary: CSC record: being early, Garima escapes linseed budfly (D. lini) attack. The digest's sowing-date bud-fly trial recorded a mean infestation of about 28.97% for Garima, behind Shubhra at 32.82%, which indicates moderate susceptibility in that trial. These two findings conflict and are reported as such. A paira-cropping trial over two seasons, which included Garima, recorded no pests or diseases in the varieties tested.

agronomic_details.yield: CSC record: average yield 1228.00 to 1491.00 kg/ha. Digest trial results: 315.78 and 337.56 kg/ha (2010-11 and 2011-12) and 326.65 kg/ha pooled in a paira-cropping trial, where Garima gave the lowest seed yield of the varieties tested. In a bud-fly sowing-date trial it gave 1366.39 kg/ha on one date and 726.87 kg/ha mean across dates, second-lowest after Shubhra. The trial yield figures conflict with the CSC range and are reported as found.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The CSC record states a linear response to nitrogen up to 90 kg N/ha under irrigation, and a best response at 40 kg N/ha under rainfed conditions. Performance under delayed sowing is reported in the CSC record only.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for general cultivation across the linseed growing areas of Uttar Pradesh (excluding Bundelkhand), Bihar, West Bengal and Assam under irrigated conditions. The variety withstands frost well and resists lodging. The digest found dryland trial work in eastern UP, but no adaptation claim from it.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CSC record: erect and medium dwarf in height, resists lodging, withstands frost well, capsules are non-dehiscent. Digest sowing-date trial: Garima had the highest plant height at all growth stages among four varieties tested. Digest NPK and sulphur trial: matured in about 117.4 days versus 121.1 days for Shekhar.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Paira-cropping trial, 2010-11 and 2011-12: lowest seed yield of the varieties tested (315.78 and 337.56 kg/ha; 326.65 kg/ha pooled). Two seasons with no pests or diseases recorded. (2) Sowing-date trial with four varieties: highest plant height at all growth stages; seed yield lower than Shekhar and Neelam; net return and B:C ratio ranked Shekhar, then Neelam, Garima, then T-397. (3) NPK and sulphur trial on irrigated linseed: Garima matured in about 117.4 days (Shekhar 121.1 days); the highest seed yield in that trial was 16.52 q/ha, but the source does not name the variety. (4) Bud-fly sowing-date trial: 28.97% mean infestation (second to Shubhra at 32.82%); 1366.39 kg/ha on one date and 726.87 kg/ha mean, second-lowest after Shubhra. (5) Dryland trial in eastern UP (2005-07): 100% RDF (40:20:20:20 NPKS kg/ha) with a 30 kg/ha seed rate recommended for higher growth and yield. (6) Ten-variety quality study: Garima had the highest reported value for some traits and the lowest protein content (0.32 g/16 g N).

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: RAPD markers (primers SBSB-01, -02, -04, -05, -06, -11) distinguished Garima from other cultivars. Primer SBSB-04 amplified bands in only Garima. Garima fell in a separate cluster with Gaurav, Sharda, Sweta, Shikha and Padmini. No SSR or SNP data with positions was found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Garima (LHCK-39), Linseed
Variety name (CSC minutes) and Seednet name are the same apart from capitalisation: "Garima (LHCK-39)" / "GARIMA (LHCK-39)". Findings below refer to "Garima" linseed, which the sources name either as Garima or Garima (LHCK-39). Where a source gives only "Garima", I say so.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Garima in these results. Garima was grown under dryland conditions in eastern UP, but the page reports only agronomic response, not tolerance -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258698873_Production_performance_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_to_fertility_levels_and_seed_rates_in_dryland_conditions_ofeastern_Uttar_Pradesh

DISEASE AND PEST
- Garima showed about 28.97% mean bud fly infestation, behind Shubhra (32.82%) in a sowing-date trial, so it was moderately susceptible in that trial -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376046405_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Preliminary_Screening_of_Linseed_Genotypes_for_Bud_Fly_Infestation
- A review cites a disease-loss study across six linseed genotypes, including Neelum, Garima and Chambal, with losses of 18.2 to 38.80%. The page does not give Garima's individual loss, so this is not attributed to Garima alone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345995217_Linseed_Linnum_usitatissimum_L_-_An_Oilseed_Crop_with_Potential_to_be_Used_in_Many_Ways_Review_Article
- A paira-cropping trial recorded no pests or diseases in the varieties tested over two seasons, which included Garima -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278301732_Performance_of_different_linseed_varieties_in_'paira'_cropping_system

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- In a paira-cropping trial (2010-11 and 2011-12), Garima gave the lowest seed yield of the varieties tested, 315.78 and 337.56 kg/ha, and 326.65 kg/ha pooled -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/278301732_Performance_of_different_linseed_varieties_in_'paira'_cropping_system
- In a sowing-date trial with four varieties, Garima had the highest plant height at all growth stages, but lower seed yield than Shekhar and Neelam. Net return and B:C ratio were highest in Shekhar, followed by Neelam, Garima and T-397 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- In an NPK and sulphur trial on irrigated linseed, Garima matured in about 117.4 days, earlier than Shekhar at 121.1 days. The highest seed yield recorded in that trial was 16.52 q/ha, though the page does not say which variety gave it -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/280935615_Influence_of_NPK_S_and_variety_on_growth_yield_and_quality_of_irrigated_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum
- Garima gave 1366.39 kg/ha on one sowing date in the bud-fly trial and 726.87 kg/ha mean across dates, which was second-lowest after Shubhra -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376046405_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Preliminary_Screening_of_Linseed_Genotypes_for_Bud_Fly_Infestation
- In a dryland trial in eastern UP (2005-07), Garima at 100% RDF (40:20:20:20 NPKS kg/ha) with a 30 kg/ha seed rate was recommended for higher growth and yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/258698873_Production_performance_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_to_fertility_levels_and_seed_rates_in_dryland_conditions_ofeastern_Uttar_Pradesh
- Quality data in a ten-variety study: Garima had the highest reported value for some traits and the lowest protein content (0.32 g/16 g N) -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2018/vol6issue5/PartJ/6-5-16-982.pdf (Academia.edu summary of the same study: https://www.academia.edu/Documents/in/Linseed_Development)

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (LHCK-39 as a selection from T 126 x Neelum) comes from the user-supplied record. No independent source in these results confirms it -- No evidence found.
- RAPD markers (primers SBSB-01, -02, -04, -05, -06, -11) distinguished Garima from other cultivars, and SBSB-04 amplified bands in only Garima. Garima fell in a separate cluster with Gaurav, Sharda, Sweta, Shikha and Padmini -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290577544_Genetic_diversity_in_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_cultivars_based_on_RAPD-analysis
- No QTL, marker-assisted or genome-resource study naming Garima was found -- No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder name or developing scientist for Garima (LHCK-39) was found in the search results -- No evidence found.
- Garima (LHCK-39) is listed among varieties developed through the AICRP on oilseeds programme -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/linseed-crop/122816675
- The institution named in the CSC record, CSAUT Kanpur (Scientist Oilseeds Breeding), is not confirmed by any search result -- No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found. No breeder, institute or station email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for Garima was returned.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Evidence refers to "Shubhra" (the variety_name spelling without the LHCK-21 code; the Seednet name "SHUBHRA (LHCK-21)" was never returned by any search).
- Listed as resistant to rust, lodging, frost and moisture stress, suited to irrigated and rainfed land, in a Scribd copy of an OSPS-13 linseed booklet (source not verified as ICAR) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/163516304/Linseed
- Used as the salt-tolerant check in a multi-environment salinity study. Seed yield per plant 6.34 g, salt tolerance index 0.81, versus 1.01 to 1.63 for the 15 best accessions tested against it -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0926669025002146
- Drought/heat/flood/submergence: No evidence found for this variety specifically. The only drought result (Kenya water-stress study) concerns three other, unnamed varieties -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC4912539/

DISEASE AND PEST
- Named among linseed varieties recommended for tolerance in a review of Indian linseed diseases (Journal of Oilseeds Research, vol. 34 no. 2) -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137694 (the snippet is truncated, so the exact disease tolerance was not confirmed; the ISOR copy is at https://isor.in/wp-content/uploads/2022/10/vol-34-2.pdf)
- Bud fly (Dasyneura lini): in a Kanpur 2012-13 bud-structure study, Shubhra had the highest mean bud fly infestation of the varieties tested (32.82%) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345959723_Bud_structure_of_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_in_relation_to_incidence_of_bud_fly_Dasyneura_lini_Barnes_in_Central_Uttar_Pradesh
- Same bud-fly result repeated in a sowing-date screening study, where Shubhra also gave the lowest seed yield (584.49 kg/ha) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/376046405_Effect_of_Sowing_Dates_and_Preliminary_Screening_of_Linseed_Genotypes_for_Bud_Fly_Infestation
- Rust resistance: see Stress Tolerance (Scribd booklet).

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Maturity 125 to 140 days; yield about 11 to 14 q/ha; seed oil about 44.5% (Scribd OSPS-13 booklet) -- https://www.scribd.com/document/163516304/Linseed
- Sowing-date trial at BHU Institute of Agricultural Sciences (2011-12) with Shubhra, SLS-67 and LCK-1101: Shubhra had the best stand, height, branching, dry matter and capsule number (53.63 per plant) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- A later study of the same design reports the same results, but places the trial at R.B.S. College, Bichpuri, Agra (2024-25). The two site and year details conflict -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/287425713_Effect_of_sowing_date_on_some_growth_characters_in_linseed
- Seed-quality study (Ten varieties, 2016): Shubhra protein 22.60%, methionine 0.41, tryptophan 0.37, lysine 0.90 g/16 g N -- https://www.chemijournal.com/archives/2018/vol6issue5/PartJ/6-5-16-982.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: a cross between Mukta and K-2 (Scribd booklet, spelled "Mukhta and K2") -- https://www.scribd.com/document/163516304/Linseed
- Breeding-line code LHCK-21 appears only as "Subhara (LHCK-21)" in a list of varieties in an ICAR organic-linseed PDF. The state grouping in that list is garbled, so no state assignment is taken from it -- https://icar.org.in/sites/default/files/inline-files/Organic-linseed-Tisi-Farming.pdf
- Breeding method, genes, QTL and marker studies: No evidence found for this variety.
- Genome resources: No evidence found for this variety.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No variety-specific breeder name was found. The institution-level linseed contact list at ICAR IIOR shows Nalini Tewari as Linseed Breeder at CSAUA&T, Kanpur, UP. This is an institutional role, not a credit for Shubhra -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
- The Journal of Oilseeds Research review lists the authors Jyoti Singh, P K Singh and R L Srivastava as ICAR-Project Coordinating Unit (Linseed) at CSAUA&T Campus, Kanpur. Institutional authors only, not breeders of Shubhra -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137694
- Developing institution: Chandra Shekhar Azad University of Agriculture & Technology, Kanpur (from the variety record). The ICAR-PCU (Linseed) at the Kanpur campus is the relevant unit.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Institute postal address (institution-level, from ICAR-PCU Linseed author affiliation): CSAUA&T Campus, Kanpur-208 002, Uttar Pradesh -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/137694

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Binwa (KL-210), Linseed

Name note: the CSC release-minutes name and the Seednet name are both "Binwa (KL-210)" (Seednet uses uppercase BINWA). No Seednet portal page was retrieved, so all evidence below refers to the name "Binwa (KL-210)" in general sources. Parentage in the input is not confirmed by any retrieved web page.

STRICT RELEVANCE NOTE: Several results were discarded because they named other varieties or other crops, including wheat KRL 210, HD3086, and generic flax accessions. Pages that mention Binwa only as a parent of another line are kept only where stated.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. Searches for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance returned only generic linseed studies or other varieties (e.g., KRL 210 in wheat, which is a different crop and variety). -- https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s10681-025-03539-y (heat-stress study, no Binwa named); https://www.researchgate.net/publication/364182368_Varietal_led_ecological_resilience_through_KRL_210_in_salt_stressed_wheat (discarded, wheat)

DISEASE AND PEST
The IIOR annual report snippet links Binwa (KL-210) to a Metarhizium rileyi study, but the extracted text is garbled and does not establish disease or pest resistance for Binwa. No confirmed resistance reaction was found. -- https://www.scribd.com/document/738239893/56-Annual-Report-IIOR-AR-2022

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
A field experiment was conducted to evaluate the performance of different linseed varieties (Binwa, Himani, Baner and Nagarkot) during different time of sowing (last week of October, first week of November and last week of November). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225600166_Genetic_analysis_of_quantitative_traits_across_environments_in_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L
Yield, maturity days and multi-location yield data for Binwa: No evidence found.

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage: the input states KL-210 is a progeny selection of the cross FLAK-1 and SPS-47/7-10-3. No web page confirmed this parentage. -- (input record only)
Breeding use: significant values were obtained in nine female viz., KL-223, Chambal, Nagarkot, Binwa, LCK-9816, Parvati, Himalini, KL-168, where Binwa is listed among lines with significant general combining ability. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/225600166_Genetic_analysis_of_quantitative_traits_across_environments_in_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L
Molecular diversity: Binwa is placed in a mixed cluster with other linseed lines in a RAPD and ISSR marker study of fibre and oil content. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/316043878_Genetic_diversity_analysis_using_RAPD_and_ISSR_markers_revealed_discrete_genetic_makeup_in_relation_to_fibre_and_oil_content_in_Linum_usitatissimum_L_genotypes

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Indira Alsi-32 (RLC-81), Linseed

Search note: The four searches ran in one batch and returned results. A later verification call hit the tool-use limit, so no further pages could be opened. Findings below come from search snippets only, not full pages. Both names were searched. The Seednet name and the CSC/release name are the same here, "Indira Alsi-32 (RLC-81)", so no separate results were needed.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- Partial. A ResearchGate paper titled "Seasonal incidence of major insect pests in linseed" names Indira Alsi-32 as a sown entry in a field trial, but the snippet does not report pest or disease resistance results. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329733283_SEASONAL_INCIDENCE_OF_MAJOR_INSECT_PESTS_IN_LINSEED

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Partial. The same ResearchGate paper reports a field trial with this variety sown in the second week of a month (the month is cut off in the snippet). It gives no yield or trial figures. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329733283_SEASONAL_INCIDENCE_OF_MAJOR_INSECT_PESTS_IN_LINSEED

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found in search results. Parentage "KIRAN X RLC 29" and variety code A0404053 come from the task record only, not from any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No breeder name found in search results. The institution "NSP Unit, Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, KGKV, Raipur" comes from the task record only. The AICRP release listing names the variety but no breeder. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No email, phone, address or contact page for the breeder or the institute appeared in search results. Nothing is recorded here beyond the institution name in the task record, so I have not invented any contact.

PUBLICATIONS -- Partial. Only one item is linked to this variety, and the snippet gives no authors, year or journal.
- Title: "Seasonal incidence of major insect pests in linseed" (ResearchGate PDF; authors, year and journal not shown in snippet). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/329733283_SEASONAL_INCIDENCE_OF_MAJOR_INSECT_PESTS_IN_LINSEED

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The seed-availability search returned only the AICRP release listing. No NSC, state seed corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing appeared. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

RECOMMENDED STATES -- The AICRP release listing (CVRC 2005, rainfed and irrigated) names Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Karnataka and Orissa. This conflicts with the task record's raw list (Chandigarh, Maharashtra, Odisha). Chandigarh and Karnataka are not corroborated by each other, so the discrepancy should be checked against the CVRC notification before the record is finalised. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/

Recommended next steps: open the AICRP release page and the ResearchGate paper in full to get authors, year, trial data and pest results. Check the CVRC 2005 notification for the state list. Find the breeder and contact via KGKV Raipur or the NSP Unit, and check seed sources on the Seednet portal.
