disease_resistance.summary: Powdery mildew: moderately resistant per the AICRP-Linseed release table and the original variety record (natural and artificial conditions); the PMC special-features entry describes Sharda as resistant to powdery mildew. Wilt: moderately resistant per the original variety record (natural and artificial conditions); no independent digest source confirms this. Alternaria blight: Not found in searched sources (no Sharda-specific rating found).

pest_resistance.summary: Linseed bud fly: moderately resistant per the AICRP-Linseed release table and the original variety record. No other pest ratings found in searched sources.

agronomic_details.yield: Average yield 762.00 to 780.00 kg/ha, per the original variety record (CSC ground truth). No yield values from the digest's own trials were found.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. The original variety record states that being early maturing gives better yield under rainfed conditions and suitability for late-sown conditions, but no multi-environment stability data was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation under rainfed conditions in Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Maharashtra and Odisha, per the original variety record. The AICRP-Linseed listing shows rainfed status, extra early maturity, and recommendation for Andhra Pradesh instead of Odisha. The digest records this as a discrepancy with the input. Odisha corresponds to Orissa. The CSC list is used as ground truth. Suitable for late-sown conditions per the original variety record.
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Dwarf stature; does not lodge; non-shattering (non-dehiscent) capsule; early maturing, extra early per AICRP (original variety record and AICRP list). A RAPD study descriptor (partly garbled text) gives early maturity, small funnel-shaped white flowers, semi-dwarf, non-dehiscent, brown seed, medium seed size and high oil value. The PMC special-features entry gives blue flower and brown seed, so flower colour is inconsistent between sources and is not resolved. Sharda is a DUS reference variety for time of flowering and corolla size at the Jabalpur co-nodal centre.
agronomic_details.field_trials: Sowing-date trial, rabi 2021-22, two varieties (Sharda vs Lenata): Lenata outperformed Sharda on the measured growth and yield traits. No other field trial results for Sharda were found in the digest.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: Not found in searched sources. No Sharda-specific SSR, SNP or RAPD marker data with positions were retrieved. A RAPD descriptor row exists for Sharda in a CSAUAT diversity study, but no marker band or position data is reported in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Sharda (IC0523807) was included in a multi-locus GWAS of 220 linseed accessions that identified QTNs for flowering time, maturity and plant height. Sharda-specific QTN effects and positions are not reported in the digest.
genetics_and_breeding.molecular_mechanisms: The Sharda (IC0523807) transcriptome was used to study candidate genes for flowering and plant height. Sharda was also used as the early-flowering reference in a flowering-regulator transcriptome study. No specific named genes or pathways for Sharda are reported in the digest.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- Rainfed-condition variety list includes Sharda (LMS-4-27); this is a cultivation-suitability listing, not a stress trial. -- https://www.mdpi.com/2073-4425/14/7/1461
- No Sharda-specific drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data found. Drought and salinity hits concerned other linseed genotypes or non-linseed crops and were discarded. -- No evidence found (searched in Search 1 and Search 3)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Special-features entry for Sharda (LMS-4-27): blue flower, brown seed, resistant to powdery mildew. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- AICRP-Linseed release table: Sharda is moderately resistant to powdery mildew and bud fly, and is extra early. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- No Sharda-specific Alternaria blight or wilt rating found. -- No evidence found

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- AICRP-Linseed lists Sharda as a rainfed variety, maturity extra early. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/linseed/varieties-released/
- Sowing-date trial (rabi 2021-22, two varieties, Sharda vs Lenata): Lenata outperformed Sharda on the measured growth and yield traits. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328336019_Growth_Yield_Nutrient_Uptake_and_Quality_of_Linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_L_Varieties_as_Affected_by_Varying_Sowing_Dates
- Descriptor row for Sharda in a CSAUAT RAPD study (early, small funnel-shaped white flowers, semi-dwarf, non-dehiscent, brown seed, medium size, high oil value; partly garbled text). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290577544_Genetic_diversity_in_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_cultivars_based_on_RAPD-analysis
- Sharda is a reference variety for time of flowering and corolla size in DUS testing (Jabalpur co-nodal centre). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/eannual-report-15-16.pdf and https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/eannual-report-16-17.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Breeding-line code LMS-4-27 is the name used for Sharda in the review tables. Parentage SHUBHRA/J1//J1/KIRAN is not found in any retrieved source; it comes only from the input record. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC10379177/
- Sharda corresponds to NGB accession IC0523807 (ICAR-NBPGR). It was used as the early-flowering reference in a flowering-regulator transcriptome and genome resequencing study. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC13056945/
- Sharda (IC0523807) transcriptome was used to study candidate genes for flowering and plant height in a multi-locus GWAS of 220 accessions, identifying QTNs for flowering time, maturity and plant height. -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC9237403/
- Breeding method and genome-level data for Sharda not found. -- No evidence found

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Sharda is among released varieties from C.S. Azad University of Agriculture and Technology, Kanpur, used in a RAPD diversity study; the institution is named, not an individual breeder. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/290577544_Genetic_diversity_in_linseed_Linum_usitatissimum_cultivars_based_on_RAPD-analysis
- Lead breeder for Sharda not identified. The ICAR IIOR linseed page names a CSAUA&T Kanpur linseed breeder (Nalini Tewari), but it does not link her to Sharda, so she is not attributed to this variety. -- https://iior.icar.gov.in/linseed
- Developing institution: C.S. Azad University of Agriculture and Technology, Kanpur-208 002 (UP), per the input record. Station not confirmed by search.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Birsa Niger-1 (variety_name "Birsa Niger-1"; seednet_variety_name "BIRSA NIGER-1"; crop Niger / Guizotia abyssinica; code A0405001)

Name note: the only pages that name this variety use "Birsa Niger-1" in mixed case. No page was found using the Seednet spelling "BIRSA NIGER-1", and no evidence was found for the code A0405001. Four searches were run.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The searches returned no page that reports drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response for Birsa Niger-1. The only Birsa Niger-1 mention was a trait-free table row (gray seeds). Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11) is described as drought tolerant, but that is a different variety and was discarded.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. The leaf-spot screening paper (ResearchGate, "Screening of Niger Cultivars/Genotypes for Resistance to Leaf Spot Disease Under Natural Conditions", https://www.researchgate.net/publication/393367222_Screening_of_Niger_Cultivars_Genotypes_for_Resistance_to_Leaf_Spot_Disease_Under_Natural_Conditions) covers Birsa Niger-2 and Gujarat Niger-1, not Birsa Niger-1, so it was discarded.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Birsa Niger-1 table row: uplands of Bihar and MP; 95–100 days to maturity; 36–38% oil; 550–600 kg/ha average yield; gray seeds -- https://www.sciencedirect.com/topics/agricultural-and-biological-sciences/open-pollination (a book-chapter table, Table 8.6, "Characteristics of Indian Niger Varieties"; the chapter's author and year were not visible in the retrieved text).
No multi-location trial or AICRP result naming Birsa Niger-1 was found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "COMPOSITE (CH-26, N-122 ... RCR-2)" from the input record: no independent source found. Breeding method (composite/selection), breeding-line codes, QTL, marker and genome studies: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand is the institution named in the input record and the BAU site describes it as a state government university -- https://bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/ (this page is about eleven other varieties and does not mention Niger or Birsa Niger-1).
Lead breeder or scientist name for Birsa Niger-1: No evidence found.

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only, from the BAU Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand location line on https://bauranchi.org/bau-releases-high-yielding-seeds-after-years-long-research/. No email, phone, postal address or contact-page URL for the Niger breeding scheme was found in the retrieved text. Breeder contact: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No peer-reviewed paper, AICRP/ICAR report, KrishiKosh thesis or conference paper naming Birsa Niger-1 was returned. Discarded: the Niger country reports from VU Amsterdam, PPIAF and others (other countries/topics); the Sumit Mishra ResearchGate precision-breeding abstract (unrelated topic).

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for Birsa Niger-1 seed from NSC, the Jharkhand State Seed Corporation, KVKs, BAU sales or private dealers. Discarded: a commodity mandi-price page for Niger seed (https://www.commodityonline.com/mandiprices/niger-seed-ramtil) and an IndiaMART listing (https://dir.indiamart.com/impcat/niger-seeds.html), which are not variety-specific.

RECOMMENDED STATES

I could not finish the research. My fourth search call hit the tool's usage limit during a follow-up request, so I have only the first-pass snippets. Several headings below have no usable evidence, and I have not filled them from memory or from the input record.

EVIDENCE DIGEST: JNC-6 (Niger, Guizotia abyssinica)
Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "JNC-6", so one set of evidence applies to both. No Seednet page was returned by any search, so the Seednet record (variety code A0405003) is unverified.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page on JNC-6 drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence response.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page on JNC-6 disease or pest resistance was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No JNC-6 yield, maturity or trial page was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL: No evidence found. The parentage in the input record (NO. 5 + DN-36 + UN-4 + BNS-1 + NO.71 + CHH-7 + PHULE-4 + RCR-238) is unverified by any search result.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: Partial. The Vikaspedia Niger cultivation page lists JNC-6 among Niger varieties, but its snippet names no breeder. The PIB press release (https://www.pib.gov.in/PressReleasePage.aspx?PRID=1796578) says JNKVV developed three Niger varieties released at the 87th meeting of the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties. The visible snippet does not name JNC-6 among them, so I cannot attribute those releases to it. The breeder name and station come only from the input record, not from a search result.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder name, email, phone or address was found for JNC-6 or for the AICRPO Niger centre at Chandagaon. Do not treat the input's postal line as verified.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The searches returned no paper, AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI for JNC-6. One search returned an unrelated hydroxychloroquine trial in Niger the country, which I discarded.

SEED AVAILABILITY: No evidence found. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for JNC-6 was returned.

RECOMMENDED STATES: Partial, and unconfirmed. The Vikaspedia page (https://en.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/niger-oilseeds-1/niger-cultivation-practices) lists Niger-growing states including Madhya Pradesh, Chhattisgarh, Maharashtra, Odisha and others. It does not say JNC-6 is recommended for any of them. The input's "Unknown" stands.

Gaps to close next: search seednet.gov.in directly for JNC-6 and variety code A0405003; search KrishiKosh and the AICRP Niger reports for the JNC-6 release notification and trial data; and check the JNKVV and Chhindwara AICRPO pages for the breeder's contact details.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: JSN-9 (Niger, Guizotia abyssinica)

Name check: The release-minutes name (JSN-9) and the Seednet name (JSN-9) are the same, so every search used both. No page names JSN-9 with Niger except one possible match noted below. Four searches were run, one per topic. Release, stress and agronomy were covered by the first search, so no separate query was run for stress, disease or genetics.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no page giving drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for JSN-9. Results were generic niger pages (Springer 2026 diversity study, ResearchGate germination and allelopathy papers) that do not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. No page on JSN-9 resistance was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. No JSN-9 yield, maturity or trial data were returned. The only agronomy hit is a generic farming guide (see SEED AVAILABILITY and RECOMMENDED STATES).

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- No evidence found. The parentage in the record ("selection from Mandla local") was not confirmed by any retrieved page. The ResearchGate EST-SSR and Springer diversity hits concern niger generally and were discarded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Jawaharlal Nehru Krishi Vishwa Vidyalaya (JNKVV), Jabalpur, is the developing institution named in the release notice: a PIB release states JNKVV developed three niger varieties released at the 87th meeting of the Central Sub-Committee on Crop Standards, Notification and Release of Varieties, notified by S.O. 8(E) dated 24 December 2021 -- https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1796578. The PIB text retrieved is truncated and does not name the three niger varieties, so JSN-9 is not confirmed as one of them. No breeder name was found for JSN-9. The Chhindwara station is a JNKVV unit at Chandangaon (see CONTACT DETAILS).

CONTACT DETAILS -- No breeder contact was found for JSN-9. Institute-level contacts found:
- JNKVV Jabalpur, institute history page -- https://www.jnkvv.org/short-history
- JNKVV KVK Chhindwara at Chandangaon, a JNKVV unit; the page gives its establishment as 1983 -- https://www.jnkvv.org/about-krishivigyan-details/chhindwara. A different site gives 1984 -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/agriculture-spots/krishi-vigyan-kendra-chandangaon-chhindwara. These conflict and this is a KVK, not the niger breeding unit.
- JNKVV telephone directory lists a "Zonal Agricultural Research Station, Chhindwara, Chandangaon Chhindwara (PIN 480001)" entry -- https://www.jnkvv.org/public/file/1756984461.TelephoneDirectory.pdf. The extracted text is jumbled: the phone number and email (9425461748, coh.chhindwara@gmail.com) appear beside a Dean, College of Horticulture entry, not the research station, so I have not attributed them to the station or to any niger breeder.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found for JSN-9. The niger papers returned (ResearchGate germination study, Springer 2026 genetic diversity study, ResearchGate Ethiopian niger improvement study, PeerJ 2025 ensiling study) were not about JSN-9 and were discarded. The Springer 2026 study was not opened to check whether it names JSN-9. No AICRP report, KrishiKosh thesis or DOI was retrieved.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found from NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK or SAU seed sales for JSN-9. The searches returned only commodity mandi prices and retail niger seed listings (Indiamart, Amazon, Everayu), which do not name this variety. One guide lists "JNS 9" among high-yielding ramtil varieties -- https://subsistencefarming.in/en/niger-seed-farming/. This may be a spelling variant of JSN-9 but is unverified, so I have not treated it as a match.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record field reads "Unknown". The PIB release says the JNKVV niger varieties were tested under state agro-climatic conditions through AICRP trials, but it names no state and does not name JSN-9 -- https://www.pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1796578.

Record discrepancy: the record gives a 2006 release year, but the only retrieved notification for JNKVV niger varieties is the December 2021 gazette notice. JSN-9 is not confirmed for either date. The 2006 year should be checked against the CSC minutes before the record is finalised.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Brisa Niger-1 (BNS-10). The searches returned only Birsa Niger-3 (BNS-11), which is a different variety, so I excluded it. Other results were crop-level or vendor pages and did not name this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
BNS-10 (Pooja-1) is listed with the note "Resistant to pests, diseases," with no specific pathogen or pest named. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
No pathogen- or pest-specific resistance data for this variety was found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
BNS-10 (Pooja-1): duration 95-100 days, shining black seed, oil content 36-38%, yield potential 650-700 kg/ha. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
No multi-location trial results, AICRP data or field-trial records naming this variety were found.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage "LOCAL SELECTION" comes only from the record supplied with the query and was not confirmed by any search result.
No QTL, marker, gene, breeding-line code or genome-resource evidence for this variety was found.
The only genetic material returned was crop-level (Guizotia abyssinica, 2n=30) and did not name this variety. Source: https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/niger-breedingcrop-improvement/245214403

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Name used in evidence: BNS-10 (Pooja-1) (the DOD table). No Seednet page was found, so no Seednet-name evidence exists.
The released centre is listed as BAU, Ranchi. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
Lead breeder or scientist name: No evidence found.
Birsa Agricultural University is an agricultural university at Kanke, Ranchi, in the Indian state of Jharkhand. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University

CONTACT DETAILS
Institute-level only (no breeder contact found):
Birsa Agricultural University, Kanke, Ranchi, Jharkhand (postal code 834006 is from the query record and was not verified by search) -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University
Website: www.bauranchi.org -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birsa_Agricultural_University
Official email: No evidence found.
Phone: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
No evidence found. No paper, thesis, AICRP/ICAR report or conference paper naming BNS-10 or Brisa Niger-1 was returned. The ScienceDirect niger chapter (https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/chapter/edited-volume/abs/pii/B9780128013090000082) and a KrishiKosh niger sowing-date thesis (https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/dbc9f861-9dec-4ccd-b889-8c93db275eba/content) are crop-level only and do not name this variety, so I excluded them.

SEED AVAILABILITY
BNS-10 is one of several niger varieties described as promising, and non-availability of seed of promising varieties is noted as a constraint. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/niger-breedingcrop-improvement/245214403
No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or dealer listing for this variety was found. The seller listings returned were generic niger seed and not variety-specific, so I excluded them.

RECOMMENDED STATES
Notified under the Seed Act, 2008-2019 (BNS-10 / Pooja-1 appears): Jharkhand -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx
The same DOD table also lists BNS-10 for Bihar, Chhattisgarh, Karnataka, Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Odisha, Rajasthan and West Bengal (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx). Andhra Pradesh does not appear in that table, although the record lists it.
Jharkhand: Jharkhand: Birsa Niger-1, Birsa Niger-2, BNS-10 -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/cultivation-of-niger-a-great-feed-for-milch-cattle/ (this page lists Birsa Niger-1 separately, so I have not treated it as the same variety).

RELEASE YEAR DISCREPANCY
The query record gives 2008. The DOD characteristics table gives 2009 (https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Niger.aspx). This should be checked against the CSC minutes.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Vasundhra (RH 9304), Indian mustard (Brassica juncea, Raya)

Name used: The CSC/release name and the Seednet name are both "Vasundhra (RH 9304)", so every finding below refers to that same name. Four searches were run. Most of the requested topics returned no direct evidence for this variety, and the results are reported as such.

STRESS TOLERANCE
No evidence found. The four searches returned no drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data for Vasundhra (RH 9304). The results that named other mustard varieties were not used.

DISEASE AND PEST
No evidence found. No Vasundhra (RH 9304) resistance or susceptibility data was returned. A seed-characters study lists RH9304 among 20 Indian mustard varieties, but its only plausibly relevant row is a seed-trait table entry, not a disease or pest result, so I have not recorded it as a disease finding. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353452944_Seed_characters_based_identification_key_for_important_varieties_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_and_Coss

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
No evidence found for yield, maturity, or multi-location trial performance specific to this variety. The AICRP Project Coordinator's report for 2020-21 lists "Vasundhra (RH 9304)" among varieties in the mustard programme's breeder seed and trial material, but it gives no yield or maturity values for it. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Note: the same report also writes "Vasundra" and "RH-30" as separate entries. I have not assumed "Vasundra" refers to this variety.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage and release year: a table of Indian mustard varieties gives Vasundhra (RH 9304) as released in 2003, from the cross RH 839 x RH 30, developed at CCS HAU, Hisar. This matches the parentage in the record ("RH 839xRH 30"). -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234143403_Assessment_of_seed_quality_and_oil_content_in_different_branches_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_cultivars_at_different_storage_intervals
Breeding method: the same table indicates a cross-derived line, consistent with a biparental cross, but no breeding-line code or selection history was found.
QTL, markers, and genome resources: No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developing institution: CCS Haryana Agricultural University (CCS HAU), Hisar, per the parentage table above. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234143403_Assessment_of_seed_quality_and_oil_content_in_different_branches_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_cultivars_at_different_storage_intervals
Lead breeder name(s): No evidence found. The searches did not return any breeder's name for this variety.
Breeding station or division: Oilseeds Section, Department of Plant Breeding, CCS HAU, Hisar, as stated in the variety record provided (not independently verified by search).

CONTACT DETAILS
No breeder contact found. Institute-level details taken from the variety record provided by the user (not verified by search):
- Head, Oilseeds Section, Department of Plant Breeding, CCS HAU, Hisar-125 004.
- Email, phone and institute contact page URL: No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
Authors (2010s-era table, year not stated on page). Seed quality and oil content in different branches of Indian mustard (Brassica juncea) cultivars at different storage intervals. Journal/report not identified on the indexed page -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/234143403_Assessment_of_seed_quality_and_oil_content_in_different_branches_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_cultivars_at_different_storage_intervals
Authors and year not identified (conference or journal). Seed characters based identification key for important varieties of Indian mustard (Brassica juncea L. Czern and Coss). The page lists RH9304 among 20 varieties studied, using seed characters from 2016 trials. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/353452944_Seed_characters_based_identification_key_for_important_varieties_of_Indian_mustard_Brassica_juncea_L_Czern_and_Coss
No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report chapter with variety data, or DOI for this variety was found.

SEED AVAILABILITY
Registration: Vasundhra (RH 9304) appears in the PPV&FR Act compendium of registered varieties (crop: mustard/rapeseed). -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/compendiumfinal27oct2018.pdf
Notified/extant listing: Vasundhra (RH 9304) appears in the PPV&FR compendium of extant notified varieties. -- https://plantauthority.gov.in/sites/default/files/envcompendium.pdf
Seed chain: The 2020-21 AICRP report lists the variety in the breeder-seed chain. -- https://www.drmr.res.in/aicrp2021/DRMR-PC-Report-2021.pdf
Lok Sabha answer: a parliamentary reply lists Vasundhra (RH 9304) among rapeseed-mustard varieties under an ICAR initiative. -- https://eparlib.sansad.in/bitstream/123456789/513205/1/14177.pdf
Dealers: No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU seed sales or private dealers selling this variety. The "Vasundhra" seed traders found on IndiaMART (Ujjain; Hyderabad) deal in soybean, wheat, gram and vegetables, not mustard, and are not linked to this variety.

RECOMMENDED STATES
No evidence found. "Unknown" in the record remains unresolved. The Tribune and other news pages returned were about RH 1975 and other HAU mustard releases, and were discarded as not about this variety.

Discarded results (not about this variety): RH 1975 news items (Tribune, Drishti, Utkarsh, farmingcosmos); a Haryana mustard hybrid article; a metabolome paper on Brassica juncea varieties (PMC11350069) and an SSR diversity paper (PMC9417036), whose variety names were not confirmed as Vasundhra; unrelated "Vasundhara"/"Vasundhra" companies and a medical paper by an author named Vasundhra.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I used all four permitted searches, but the evidence is thin. The final tool call hit the server's usage limit while I was re-reading results, so I could not open the full pages. Everything below comes from search snippets only.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- Partial evidence only. The GCIRC Rapeseed-Mustard overview lists RGN-13 among Indian mustard varieties, under a heading about high-temperature tolerance. The snippet does not clearly tie RGN-13 to that trait, so I have not attributed it. Drought, salinity, flood and submergence: No evidence found. -- https://www.gcirc.org/fileadmin/documents/Bulletins/B25/B25_06Rapeseed.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- No evidence found. Maturity, yield and multi-location trial data were not in the retrieved snippets.

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources) -- Parentage RH-30 x Varuna is from the variety record you supplied, not from a search result. The PMC SSR diversity paper (PMC9417036) names "RGN-13" in a variety table with a developing-institution field, but the snippet was cut off before the institution, parentage or marker data. Full text needed. -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9417036/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Institution from your record: Agricultural Research Station, Sriganganagar (Rajasthan). No breeder name was found in any retrieved text. The PMC9417036 page is the lead to check.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute email, phone, address or contact-page URL was retrieved. Suggested next step: the Agricultural Research Station, Sriganganagar and Sri Karan Narendra Agriculture University (SKNAU) contact pages, which I could not reach.

PUBLICATIONS -- No verified publication for RGN-13 was retrieved. The PMC9417036 paper (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9417036/) is a candidate, but its authors, year and journal were not in the snippet, so I have not formatted a citation.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. The search for seed sources returned only an unrelated tomato product ("Raya Rey", Dave's Seed), which I discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found. The record lists "Unknown", and no retrieved page gave a notification or recommendation for RGN-13.

Name check: "RGN-13" and "seednet_variety_name" are identical, so both searches refer to the same name. The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved.

drought.details: The AICRP safflower success-story entry describes the variety as tolerant to moisture stress. The ICAR-IIOR cultivar listing gives 2000-2200 kg/ha potential under irrigation and 1200-1500 kg/ha under rainfed conditions, with 1100 kg/ha average. The 'high' rating rests on the qualitative 'tolerant to moisture stress' claim; no physiological mechanism was documented for this variety. The general statement that safflower is drought-resistant and grown on residual soil moisture is crop-level and was not counted as variety evidence. CSC record also lists the variety as recommended for rainfed as well as irrigated conditions.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRUCTURE NOTE: Four web_search queries were run (variety/release, breeder/institution, research papers, seed/contact). The seednet.gov.in portal page was not retrieved, so the Seednet name and code A0408028 are unverified.

NAME CHECK: Sources spell the variety "Phule Kusuma (JLSF-414)" and "Phule Kusum (JLSF-414)" interchangeably; the AICRP page uses "Phule Kusum (JLSF-414)". Both spellings are treated as referring to the same variety, since the JLSF-414 code and the Oilseeds Research Station, Jalgaon origin match. No evidence was found under the Seednet name "Phule Kusum (JLSF-414)" on seednet.gov.in itself.

STRESS TOLERANCE
AICRP safflower success-story entry describes this variety as tolerant to moisture stress, with 1200-2200 kg/ha yield, 125-140 days to maturity and 28-29% oil -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
ICAR-IIOR cultivar listing gives 2000-2200 kg/ha potential under irrigation and 1200-1500 kg/ha under rainfed conditions, with 1100 kg/ha average -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/index.php/technology/cultivars/safflower
Safflower is generally described as drought-resistant and grown on residual soil moisture; this is crop-level, not variety-specific, so it is not counted as evidence for this variety -- https://agrosiaa.com/agronomy/detail/safflower
No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance for this variety.

DISEASE AND PEST
A sowing-date study on Alternaria blight included Phule Kusum among three safflower cultivars, but reports disease intensity and yield by sowing date, not a resistance rating for this variety -- https://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/12_1946-1951.pdf
The ICAR-IIOR cultivar listing and AICRP success-story entry do not give a disease or pest resistance rating for this variety. An aphid-tolerance phrase appears on the AICRP page, but it is attached to a different entry, so it is not attributed here -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
No evidence found for specific resistance to wilt, Alternaria, Ramularia or aphids for this variety.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Listed as a spiny-type variety in an agronomy listing with other varieties; spiny type is not a trait claim for this variety specifically -- https://agrosiaa.com/agronomy/detail/safflower
Diversity-study table lists a genotype named "phulekusum" with about 124 days to 50% flowering, about 157 days to maturity, and the lowest seed yield (about 765 kg/ha) among the entries tested. This is a possible match to JLSF-414 but the source does not give the code, so it is uncertain -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321081240_Assessment_of_genetic_diversity_in_safflower_Carthamus_tinctorius_L_genotypes_through_morphological_and_SSR_marker
Sowing-date and Alternaria trial data (see DISEASE AND PEST) -- https://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/12_1946-1951.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Pedigree JLSF-103 x GMU 216 (a) -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/index.php/technology/cultivars/safflower ; https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/ (AICRP writes "GMU -216 (a)")
Breeding method: selection; propagation: self-pollination -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/index.php/technology/cultivars/safflower ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dhare-sl-safflower-presentatation-pdfpdf/257732987
Species chromosome number 2n=24 (species-level, not variety-specific) -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dhare-sl-safflower-presentatation-pdfpdf/257732987
Breeding-line code: JLSF-414 (from the variety name; no separate line history found) -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/index.php/technology/cultivars/safflower
QTL or marker mapping for this variety: No evidence found. The 2025 GigaScience safflower genome/core-collection paper does not name this variety in the retrieved text -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12888819/
Genome resources: the Safflower Genome Resource described there is species-level, not specific to this variety -- https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/pmc/articles/PMC12888819/

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by: AICRP (Safflower) centre, Oilseeds Research Station, Jalgaon, Mahatma Phule Krishi Vidyapeeth, Rahuri -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/index.php/technology/cultivars/safflower ; https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dhare-sl-safflower-presentatation-pdfpdf/257732987
AICRP success-story table lists the breeder as "Safflower Breeder, ARS, MPKV Jalgaon" -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
Lead breeder name: No evidence found. The breeder names that appear in the same AICRP and related pages (NARI Phaltan, Nimbkar) belong to other varieties and are not attributed here.

CONTACT DETAILS (institute-level; no breeder contact found)
Oil Seed Research Station, Jalgaon (MPKV) -- Contact 0257-2250888; Email orsjalgaon@gmail.com -- https://mpkv.ac.in/Research/ResearchCentralZone ; https://www.indiacustomercare.com/mahatma-phule-krishi-vidyapeeth-agri-univ-rahuri
Address: Nimkhedi Road, Old Highway No. 6, Distt. Jalgaon-425001 (Maharashtra) -- https://www.indiascienceandtechnology.gov.in/allstinstitutions/oil-seed-research-station-jalgaon-0
Note: the same directory page lists +91-11 phone numbers that appear to belong to a Delhi office, so they are not attributed to the station here.

Official MPKV site: https://mpkv.ac.in/

PUBLICATIONS
Sowing-date and Alternaria study including Phule Kusum; authors and year not retrieved. Research Journal article -- https://researchjournal.co.in/upload/assignments/12_1946-1951.pdf
Genetic diversity study (SSR and morphology) with a "phulekusum" genotype; authors and year not retrieved in the snippet; ResearchGate record -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/321081240_Assessment_of_genetic_diversity_in_safflower_Carthamus_tinctorius_L_genotypes_through_morphological_and_SSR_marker

No KrishiKosh thesis, AICRP annual report entry or DOI for this variety was found in the searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
No evidence found for current seed stocks of this variety from NSC, the Maharashtra State Seed Corporation, KVKs, SAU seed sales or private dealers. The IIPR seed hub result returned was for mungbean (a different crop) and was discarded -- https://iipr.icar.gov.in/iiprseedportal/seed_availabilty.php
The Directorate of Oilseeds Development safflower list of notified varieties (2008-2019) for Maharashtra does not include this variety, which is a gap to check -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Safflower.aspx

RECOMMENDED STATES
Central-level release; recommended region given as All India in ICAR-IIOR and AICRP records. Notification: S.O. 122(E), dated 2/2/2005 -- https://www.icar-iior.org.in/index.php/technology/cultivars/safflower

drought.details: The digest contains no drought-tolerance rating for PBNS-40. A rainfed Vertisol study (2009/10-2011/12) reported seed yields lower than spiny checks. Under reduced soil moisture at three depths, PBNS-40 had the lowest oil concentration (about 20%) and oil yield (about 94 kg/ha) among the non-spiny and spiny cultivars tested; the source states this describes performance under water limitation and is not a drought-tolerance rating. The original CSC record gives a drought tolerance efficiency of 81.2 under normal plant density conditions; this value is from the input record, not from the digest, and no mechanisms were identified in the digest.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderately tolerant to Alternaria leaf blight and fusarium wilt (AICRP success stories; the Vertisol study table gives the same moderate-tolerance profile for wilt and Alternaria leaf blight). The AICRP major achievements list also places PBNS-40 among varieties with moderate tolerance to Alternaria, wilt and aphid. A VNMKV seminar slide lists the variety as resistant to anthracnose; this is stronger than the moderate-tolerance wording and is unverified, so it should not be relied upon without confirmation. The CSC record also states moderate tolerance to Alternaria and fusarium wilt.

pest_resistance.summary: Moderately tolerant to safflower aphid (AICRP success stories and AICRP major achievements). A VNMKV seminar slide lists the variety as resistant to aphids; this is stronger than the moderate-tolerance wording and is unverified. A field study of insecticides against safflower aphid (Uroleucon compositae) used PBNS-40 as the test cultivar, but full text was not available, so no resistance outcome is confirmed from that study.

agronomic_details.yield: About 1500 kg/ha (DOD variety table; trade listing, non-official). AICRP success stories give 1500-1600 kg/ha (All India). CSC record gives 1500.00 to 1600.00 kg/ha. In the rainfed Vertisol trial, seed yields were lower than spiny checks.
agronomic_details.stability: Non-spiny group seed yield was about 50% below spiny cultivars (digest source). No multi-environment stability analysis for PBNS-40 was found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Recommended for release and cultivation in safflower-growing areas under irrigated and rainfed conditions (CSC record). Advisory bulletin for Marathwada (October 2017) lists PBNS-40 among varieties to select for the rabi season. Responsive to 1-2 irrigations (CSC record).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Unknown
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Rainfed Vertisol trial over 3 seasons (2009/10-2011/12): 100-seed weight 4.1 g and maturity 118-128 days; seed yields lower than spiny checks. (2) Reduced soil moisture study at three depths: PBNS-40 had the lowest oil concentration (about 20%) and oil yield (about 94 kg/ha) among the non-spiny and spiny cultivars tested. (3) Non-spiny group, including PBNS-40, had seed yield about 50% below spiny cultivars. (4) DOD variety table and AICRP success stories report yield of about 1500 kg/ha (AICRP range 1500-1600 kg/ha) and oil about 27%. (5) Insecticide field study on safflower aphid used PBNS-40 as the test cultivar; no outcome for PBNS-40 was confirmed.

genetics_and_breeding.genetic_markers: RAPD markers were used to assess genetic similarity among parental lines, and PBNS-40 is one of the parental genotypes in that cluster analysis. No marker names, positions or SNP/SSR details were found.
genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. No QTL studies for PBNS-40 were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
Non-spiny PBNS-40 is listed as moderately tolerant to Alternaria leaf blight, wilt and aphid -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
Same moderate-tolerance profile (wilt, Alternaria leaf blight, aphid) in a rainfed Vertisol study table -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/agj2.21581
Under reduced soil moisture at three depths, PBNS-40 had the lowest oil concentration (about 20%) and oil yield (about 94 kg/ha) of the non-spiny and spiny cultivars tested. This describes performance under water limitation, not a drought-tolerance rating -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/agj2.21581
Seed yield of the non-spiny group, including PBNS-40, was about 50% below the spiny cultivars. No heat, salinity, flood or submergence evidence found for PBNS-40 -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/agj2.21581
Name note: the search results used "PBNS-40" without "(Non-Spiny)". Both the CSC and Seednet names were searched; all evidence above refers to PBNS-40.

DISEASE AND PEST
Moderately tolerant to Alternaria, wilt and aphid, per AICRP success stories -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
Listed as resistant to aphids and resistant to anthracnose in a VNMKV seminar slide on genetic improvement. This is stronger than the "moderately tolerant" wording above and should be verified -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360016522_Presentation_on_Genetic_improvement_of_Qualitative_and_Quantitative_traits_in_safflower
A field study of insecticides against safflower aphid (Uroleucon compositae) used PBNS-40 as the test cultivar. Full text not available, so only the cultivar use is confirmed -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/288288482_Bio-efficacy_of_different_insecticides_against_safflower_aphids_Uroleucon_compositae_Theobald
AICRP achievements list PBNS-40 among varieties with moderate tolerance to Alternaria, wilt and aphid -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/major-achievements/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Yield potential about 1500 kg/ha and oil about 27%, per the DOD variety table -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Safflower.aspx
AICRP success stories give yield 1500-1600 kg/ha, maturity 118-128 days and oil 27%, "All India" -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
Rainfed Vertisol trial (3 seasons, 2009/10-2011/12) with 100-seed weight 4.1 g and maturity 118-128 days; seed yields were lower than spiny checks -- https://acsess.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/10.1002/agj2.21581 (also https://www.researchgate.net/publication/380536131_Water_use_and_yield_response_of_rainfed_safflower_Carthamus_tinctorius_L_in_Vertisols_with_varying_soil_depths)
Advisory bulletin for Marathwada (October 2017) lists PBNS-40 among varieties to select for the rabi season -- http://wamis.gmu.edu/countries/india/Bulletin_27.10.2017_FINAL.pdf
Trade listing gives yield potential about 1500 kg/ha and 27% oil (non-official) -- https://pisumfoods.com/oilseeds/safflower

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
Parentage: irrigated material from C-40 Pro.3 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
Pedigree C-40-Pro.3, breeding method mutation breeding, self-pollinated -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dhare-sl-safflower-presentatation-pdfpdf/257732987
Mutation origin is also referenced in the Dhare presentation's pedigree and method slide (same source as above)
RAPD markers used to assess genetic similarity among parental lines; PBNS-40 is one of the parental genotypes in that cluster analysis -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360016522_Presentation_on_Genetic_improvement_of_Qualitative_and_Quantitative_traits_in_safflower
No QTL, marker-assisted or genome-resource studies for PBNS-40 found
No breeding-line code for PBNS-40 found beyond the variety code A0408029 given in the input record

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
Developed by the AICRP (Safflower) centre, Vasantrao Naik Marathwada Krishi Vidyapeeth (VNMKV, formerly MAU), Parbhani -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/dhare-sl-safflower-presentatation-pdfpdf/257732987
Listed as developed and released by MAU, Parbhani -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Variety/Safflower.aspx
AICRP success stories credit the Safflower Breeder, Department of Botany, MAU Parbhani for PBNS-40 -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/safflower/success-stories/
Dr. S.B. Ghuge is named as Officer Incharge and Safflower Breeder, AICRP on Safflower, VNMKV Parbhani, in a PhD thesis acknowledgement. The thesis does not confirm him as PBNS-40's developer, so this is an institutional link only -- https://krishikosh.egranth.ac.in/server/api/core/bitstreams/e6e5c7ae-cfd7-4689-88a3-5e7571395dfa/content

drought.details: The AICRP sesame achievements table attributes drought hardiness to this line. The variety record also states tolerance against drought. No quantitative drought trial data or mechanism was found in the digest, so the level is rated medium on qualitative attribution only. The variety record describes the variety as well suited to arid and semi-arid areas of Rajasthan. A rainfed kharif 2018 study ranked RT-127 second among ten varieties for yield-related performance, behind only JCSDT-26, but the digest does not state that this trial measured drought stress specifically.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources.

salinity.details: A salt-stress seedling study classed RT-127 among the salt-tolerant cultivars. It showed higher superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and lower malondialdehyde (MDA) than RT-125. Evidence is from seedling-stage screening only, so the level is medium.

flood.details: Not found in searched sources.

disease_resistance.summary: Macrophomina stem and root rot: highly tolerant per the variety record. Also described as resistant to Macrophomina in a general variety listing, and named among tolerant Rajasthan varieties for stem and root rot. Charcoal rot (Macrophomina) field screen in the USA: rated moderately resistant, one of seven varieties. Powdery mildew: highly tolerant per the variety record, resistant per a general variety listing, and attributed tolerance in the AICRP table. Bacterial leaf spot: highly tolerant per the variety record and attributed tolerance in the AICRP table. Phyllody: highly tolerant per the variety record. In a phyllody screen, RT-127 had minimum phyllody incidence and was rated resistant on the phyllody scale. Disease-tolerance gene/QTL table: RT-127 is listed among genotypes resourced for disease tolerance, with no specific resistance gene named.

pest_resistance.summary: Leafhopper (phyllody vector): lowest leafhopper population of the lines tested (0.62 per leaf) in the same phyllody screen. Gallfly and mites: the variety record states less percent infestation against gallfly and mites. No digest source independently confirms the gallfly and mite statement.

agronomic_details.yield: Seed yield 750-850 kg/ha per the AICRP achievements table. The variety record gives 600.00 to 900.00 kg/ha. Both are reported; the AICRP range is narrower.
agronomic_details.stability: RT-127 was classed as one of the most stable genotypes for seed yield under graded fertilizer doses (phenotypic stability analysis). It was also used as a benchmark in a phenotypic stability study of 15 varieties and advance lines at ARS Mandor. Stability across environments beyond these studies was not found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Well suited to arid and semi-arid areas of Rajasthan (variety record). Rainfed performance was assessed in kharif 2018 (digest). Seed oil content is 50-52% per the AICRP table and 50.6% per the variety record. Seeds are described as shiny and bold, with better export avenues (variety record).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: CAPSULES ARE ALTERNATELY PLACED, NON-HAIRY AND MEDIUM LONG.;ITS PLANT BEARS LONG BRANCHES COMPARATIVELY EMERGING FROM LOWER SIDE.
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Adaptive trial: RT-127 was the check; RT 346 yielded 19.4% above it (360 kg/ha at farmers' fields). (2) Rainfed conditions, kharif 2018: RT-127 ranked second among ten varieties for yield-related performance, behind only JCSDT-26. (3) Graded fertilizer doses: phenotypic stability analysis classed RT-127 as one of the most stable genotypes for seed yield. (4) Stability study of 15 varieties and advance lines at ARS Mandor: RT-127 used as benchmark. (5) Line x tester combining-ability study: RT-127 used as tester; the cross with VRI 3 gave significantly positive SCA effects. (6) Field screens: phyllody screen (minimum phyllody incidence, lowest leafhopper population); charcoal rot field screen in the USA (moderately resistant). Trial yield values beyond those listed were not found. The maturity discrepancy is noted: the AICRP table gives 82-86 days, while the variety record gives 75-84 days.

genetics_and_breeding.qtl_information: Not found in searched sources. RT-127 is listed in a disease-tolerance gene/QTL table among genotypes resourced for disease tolerance. No QTL names or effects were given.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
RT-127 SESAME DIGEST

Name check: the CSC name (RT-127) and the Seednet name (RT-127) are identical. The Seednet portal was not returned by any search, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists here. All evidence below refers to the name RT-127 and to sesame.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Drought hardiness and tolerance to bacterial leaf spot and powdery mildew are attributed to this line in the AICRP sesame achievements table. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
A salt-stress seedling study found RT-127 among the salt-tolerant cultivars, with higher superoxide dismutase activity and lower MDA than RT-125 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/345942699_THE_DYNAMICS_OF_SESAME_Sesamum_indicum_L_GROWTH_TYPE
Under rainfed conditions in kharif 2018, RT-127 ranked behind only JCSDT-26 among ten varieties for yield-related performance -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/JOR/article/view/136587

DISEASE AND PEST
RT-127 is described as resistant to several diseases, including Macrophomina and powdery mildew. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/boost-sesame-yields-with-these-disease-resistant-varieties-ideal-for-rajasthans-dry-conditions
RT-127 was among the lines with minimum phyllody incidence and was rated resistant on the phyllody scale -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2023/Dec/19-Dec-23/2023_IJPSS_110446/Revised-ms_IJPSS_110446_v1.pdf
RT-127 had the lowest leafhopper population (0.62 per leaf) in the same phyllody screen -- https://sdiopr.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/2023/Dec/19-Dec-23/2023_IJPSS_110446/Revised-ms_IJPSS_110446_v1.pdf
In a charcoal rot (Macrophomina) field screen in the USA, RT-127 was one of seven varieties rated moderately resistant -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/394791571_Evaluation_of_sesame_germplasm_cultivars_for_resistance_against_charcoal_rot
A stem and root rot tolerance listing names RT-127 among tolerant Rajasthan varieties -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311776143_Safe_sesame_Sesamum_indicum_L_production_Perspectives_practices_and_challenges_SAFE_SESAME_PRODUCTION_PERSPECTIVES_PRACTICES_AND_CHALLENGES

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Seed yield is listed as 750-850 kg/ha, oil content 50-52%, and maturity 82-86 days for RT-127. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
Phenotypic stability analysis under graded fertilizer doses classed RT-127 as one of the most stable genotypes for seed yield -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/373555806_Stability_Analysis_in_Sesame_Sesamum_indicum_L_under_different_Doses_of_Fertilizers
RT-127 was a check in an adaptive trial where RT 346 yielded 19.4% above it (360 kg/ha at farmers' fields) -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jor1-26-2-021
RT-127 was used as a benchmark in a phenotypic stability study of 15 varieties and advance lines at ARS Mandor -- https://www.bioinfopublication.org/include/download.php?id=BIA0004225

GENETICS AND QTL
Parentage (SI-3500 x Patan-64) as given in the variety record: No evidence found. No search result named this cross for RT-127.
Breeding history: the search returned a 1996 cross of RT 127 with HT 24, pedigree-selected, which produced RT 346. This shows RT-127 as a parent of a different variety, not its own pedigree -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jor1-26-2-021
RAPD and morphological clustering placed RT-127 with RT-125 and RT-103 as a Mandor group -- https://www.isgpb.org/journal/index.php/IJGPB/article/download/1142/2438
RT-127 was used as a tester in a line x tester combining-ability study, and a cross with VRI 3 gave significantly positive SCA effects -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/336601852_Combining_ability_analysis_in_sesame_Sesamum_indicum_L
Disease-tolerance gene/QTL table lists RT-127 among genotypes resourced for disease tolerance -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9763032/
Genome resources specific to RT-127 (marker maps, sequences): No evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
RT-127 was released by the AICRP sesame centre at Mandor (released 1999 per the RT 351 paper) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/297275465_Rt_351_-_A_multicapsular_high_yielding_white_seeded_sesame_variety
The Mandor station is Agricultural Research Station, Rajasthan Agricultural University, Mandor, Jodhpur 342 304 -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/297275465_Rt_351_-_A_multicapsular_high_yielding_white_seeded_sesame_variety
Dr. S.R. Kumhar is listed as Sr. Breeder at ARS Mandor on the AICRP sesame cooperating-unit page. This identifies him as the station's sesame breeder, not confirmed as the RT-127 developer -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/cooperating-unit/
Release year discrepancy: the AICRP table gives 2001; the RT 351 paper and the variety record give 1999.

Charcoal rot (Macrophomina) field screen in the USA: rated moderately resistant, one of seven varieties. Powdery mildew: highly tolerant per the variety record, resistant per a general variety listing, and attributed tolerance in the AICRP table. Bacterial leaf spot: highly tolerant per the variety record and attributed tolerance in the AICRP table. Phyllody: highly tolerant per the variety record. Disease-tolerance gene/QTL table: RT-127 is listed among genotypes resourced for disease tolerance, with no specific resistance gene named.

drought.details: No variety-specific drought evidence was found in the digest. The only source retrieved (NIFTEM processing PDF) gives general statements that sesame does not grow well under drought or heavy rain, and does not name PKDS-11. The original variety record lists drought tolerance and a degree of water-stress tolerance, but this is not supported by the digest and is therefore not scored.

heat.details: Not found in searched sources. The original variety record lists heat tolerance as Unknown.

salinity.details: Not found in searched sources. The digest reports no evidence for salinity tolerance.

flood.details: No variety-specific flood or excess-water evidence was found in the digest. The original variety record describes lodging and excess-water tolerance, but this is unverified by the digest and is not scored.

disease_resistance.summary: Moderate resistance to Macrophomina (charcoal rot) is reported for PKDS-11 (Jawahar Til-11, Venkat), which was released in 2006. Evidence: Krishi Jagran source. The AICRP achievements table gives no separate disease rating for PKDS-11. The original variety record also states that the summer season is relatively free of disease; this is not confirmed by the digest. No evidence was found for powdery mildew, Phytophthora or Alternaria tolerance in PKDS-11. The AICRP table credits those traits to TKG-306, a different variety, and that attribution was discarded.

pest_resistance.summary: No evidence was found in the digest for PKDS-11 insect pest resistance. The capsule borer tolerance reported in the Krishi Jagran source belongs to PKDS-8, a different variety, and was discarded. The original variety record states moderate resistance to leaf borer and capsule borer, but the digest does not confirm this.

agronomic_details.yield: AICRP national table: 650-700 kg/ha for Jawahar Til-11 (PKDS-11-Venkat). Original variety record: 680-739 kg/ha under normal conditions. The two ranges differ and both are reported.
agronomic_details.stability: Not found in searched sources. No multi-environment stability data for PKDS-11 were found.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Original variety record: recommended for release and cultivation in Andhra Pradesh, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal and Madhya Pradesh. agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: Krishi Jagran source: compact plant structure suited to mechanized harvesting. Early maturity at 82-85 days per the AICRP table. Seed colour is dark brown per the AICRP table. Maturity days conflict between the original record (73-77) and the AICRP table (82-85). Both are reported. Shattering: the original record says the variety matures uniformly, which avoids shattering; this is not confirmed by the digest.
agronomic_details.field_trials: No trial results specific to PKDS-11 were found in the digest. The only quantitative value is the AICRP national table entry (650-700 kg/ha, 46-50% oil, 82-85 days, dark brown seed). The AICRP fertilizer and cropping-system findings name other varieties or no variety and were not attributed to PKDS-11. The original record gives fertilizer guidance of N 60, P 40, K 20 kg/ha and ZnSO4 20 kg/ha; the digest does not attribute these to a PKDS-11 trial.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Jawahar Til PKDS-11 (Venkat) / Seednet name JAWAHAR TIL PKDS-11(VENKET), sesame

Name note: The searches used both names. Every retained page refers to the variety as "Jawahar Til-11 (PKDS-11-Venkat)" or "PKDS-11". The Seednet portal itself was not retrieved, so no evidence comes from Seednet directly.

STRESS TOLERANCE
- Moderate resistance to Macrophomina (charcoal rot) is reported for this variety. PKDS-11 (Jawahar Til-11 – Venkat) is released in 2006 and shows resistance to Macrophomina. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-more-earn-more-improved-sesame-varieties-and-practices-for-mp-chhattisgarh-farmers/
- Drought, heat, salinity, flood and submergence tolerance: No evidence found. The searches returned only general statements that sesame does not grow well under drought or heavy rain. -- https://niftem.ac.in/newsite/pmfme/wp-content/uploads/2022/08/seasameprocessing.pdf

DISEASE AND PEST
- Macrophomina resistance is listed in the Krishi Jagran source above (3-5). The AICRP table gives no separate disease rating for PKDS-11. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- Insect pest resistance (capsule borer and others): No evidence found for PKDS-11. Capsule borer tolerance was reported for PKDS-8, a different variety, and was discarded. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-more-earn-more-improved-sesame-varieties-and-practices-for-mp-chhattisgarh-farmers/
- Powdery mildew, Phytophthora and Alternaria tolerance: No evidence found for PKDS-11. The AICRP table credits those traits to TKG-306, which was discarded. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Yield potential and seed traits (AICRP national table): 650–700 kg/ha, 46–50% oil, 82–85 days, dark brown seed. Jawahar Til-11 (PKDS-11-Venkat) is listed at 650-700 with 46-50 oil, 82-85 days and dark brown seed. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- Maturity and plant type: The variety matures early at 82–85 days, and its compact plant structure suits mechanized harvesting. -- https://krishijagran.com/agripedia/grow-more-earn-more-improved-sesame-varieties-and-practices-for-mp-chhattisgarh-farmers/
- Field-trial or multi-location results specific to PKDS-11: No evidence found. The AICRP fertilizer and cropping-system findings name other varieties or no variety, and were not attributed. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage (Bichua local improved × pure-line selection), breeding-line code, and breeding method: No evidence found in the retrieved pages. The parentage in the user record is unverified. Only a generic description of pure-line breeding was seen, and it does not name PKDS-11. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/378343755_A_Brief_Review_on_Sesame_Crop_Production_and_Insect_Pest_Management
- QTL, marker and genome-resource studies: No evidence found naming PKDS-11. The SSR diversity study on 41 Indian sesame genotypes was retained as a general source, but the snippet does not show PKDS-11 among its genotypes. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-77-2-011

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- Developing institution: The Sesame varieties developed by JNKVV list includes JT 11 (PKDS-11), released in 2005 by JNKVV. The release year in this source conflicts with 2006 in other sources. -- https://www.slideshare.net/slideshow/seasame-breeding-crop-improvement-kharif/239907924
- Release year confirmed by ICAR as 2006: Gujarat Til 10 and Jawahar Til PKDS 11 were released in 2005 and 2006, respectively. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309405535_Seed_production_of_field_crops_in_India_Quality_assurance_status_impact_and_way_forward
- Station: ZARS, Powarkheda (JNKVV) is the institution in the user record. This station is named in notification data for PKDS-12 and PKDS-8, not for PKDS-11. -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx
- Lead breeder name: No evidence found. No named scientist was found for PKDS-11.

CONTACT DETAILS
- Breeder name, role and direct email or phone: No evidence found.
- Institute-level address (AICRP on Sesame and Niger, coordinating unit): the AICRP on Sesame and Niger is at JNKVV Campus, Jabalpur, 482 004. This is an institute-level address only, with no phone or email. -- https://indianjournals.com/article/ijgpb-77-2-011
- ZARS Powarkheda postal address, phone and email: No evidence found.
- Official institute contact page URL (JNKVV or ZARS): No evidence found.

PUBLICATIONS
- J. Jawahar Lal, H.H. Kumaraswamy, A.R.G. Ranganatha (2015). Quality seed production technology in sesame. ICAR-Directorate of Oilseeds Research, Hyderabad (report/extension publication; the journal is not stated) -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311776080_Quality_seed_production_technology_in_sesame
- Authors not shown in the retrieved text (year not shown). Seed production of field crops in India: Quality assurance, status, impact and way forward. This paper lists PKDS 11 among released varieties with breeder seed indents. Journal not stated -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309405535_Seed_production_of_field_crops_in_India_Quality_assurance_status_impact_and_way_forward
- Peer-reviewed or thesis papers naming PKDS-11: No evidence found. KrishiKosh was not returned by the searches.
- AICRP Sesame and Niger annual reports: No evidence found for PKDS-11 specifically. The AICRP achievements page is the only AICRP source retrieved. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Breeder-seed demand: PKDS 11 was one of five sesame varieties that together made up 58.6% of the total breeder seed indent. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/309405535_Seed_production_of_field_crops_in_India_Quality_assurance_status_impact_and_way_forward
- Public seed agencies (NSC, SFCI, SSC, SAU) handle the formal supply chain. This is general, not PKDS-11-specific. -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/311776080_Quality_seed_production_technology_in_sesame
- Dealer listing with variety "PKDS 11": weak and unverified. The listing is for a golden natural sesame sold for cooking, not certified seed. -- https://dir.indiamart.com/delhi/sesame-seed.html

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
I used all four permitted searches, and the tool then stopped further calls, so several headings have no evidence. The digest below uses only snippets I actually read. Search snippets were short and I did not open the full pages, so treat the figures as unverified until checked against the source pages.

EVIDENCE DIGEST

Name check: The variety_name and seednet_variety_name are both "Nirmala (OS-Sel-164)". I did not search the Seednet portal directly, so no Seednet-page evidence was found. The variety code A0409062 did not appear in any result.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- The AICRP sesame achievements table lists Nirmala (OS-Sel-164) with 2003 release, white seed, and tolerance to bacterial leaf spot, powdery mildew and Alternaria. No drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence data was found. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

DISEASE AND PEST -- The same AICRP achievements entry records tolerance to bacterial leaf spot, powdery mildew and Alternaria. No pest-resistance data was found. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- The AICRP achievements table has a Nirmala row with numeric columns of 800-900, 42-44 and 80-85. The column headings were not captured, so I cannot say which trait each figure represents. -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- An Odisha rice-based cropping systems page lists Nirmala (OS-Sel-164) with a duration of 88 days, average yield of 7.0 q/ha and oil content of 45%. -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/sesame/

GENETICS AND QTL -- No evidence found. The parentage "Mutant of B 67 (Tilottama)" comes from the task input, not from any search result. Breeding-line codes, method, QTL and genome resources: no evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- No evidence found. No result named a lead breeder or scientist for this variety. The institution given in the task (AICRP on Oilseeds (Sesamum), Department of Plant Breeding and Genetics, OUAT, Bhubaneswar) is not confirmed by any search result.

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder, institute, email, phone or address was found for this variety.

PUBLICATIONS -- No evidence found. The searches returned no papers, theses, AICRP reports or KrishiKosh records for this variety.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- No evidence found. A Vikaspedia sesame package-of-practices page lists Nirmala among white-seeded varieties, but gives no seed source or availability. -- https://agriculture.vikaspedia.in/viewcontent/agriculture/crop-production/package-of-practices/oilseeds/sesame-1?lgn=en

RECOMMENDED STATES -- No evidence found for an official recommendation. The input gives "Unknown". The Odisha page suggests Odisha-based use but does not state a formal recommendation. The Vikaspedia page lists the variety, but the snippet does not clearly tie it to any state.

Limitations: The searches were run once each, so later steps (such as checking the Seednet entry, the KrishiKosh archive or the OUAT contact page) were not done. The "Nirmala" name is generic, so every finding above was checked against the sesame context, but the Seednet and breeder records still need direct checking.

drought.details: A biochemical study of drought response classifies Prachi among the drought-sensitive sesame genotypes, based on SOD, CAT and GPX markers. The original variety record lists drought as 'TOLERANT' (agronomic features), which conflicts with this study. The digest contains no field-based drought trial for Prachi, so the conflict is unresolved. The 'low' level reflects only the marker-based study.

heat.details: No evidence found for heat tolerance specific to Prachi. Searches returned only general crop-temperature information.

salinity.details: No evidence found for salinity tolerance specific to Prachi.

flood.details: No evidence found for flood tolerance specific to Prachi.

disease_resistance.summary: Cercospora leaf spot: tolerant (AICRP achievements table). Powdery mildew: tolerant (AICRP achievements table). Crop-agronomy compendium (Orissa row) describes Prachi (ORM17) as pest- and disease-resistant, but this statement is generic and names no specific disease. No quantitative resistance scores (e.g., percent disease or resistance grade) were found for Prachi. Other diseases listed in the original variety record (phyllody, stem and root rot, blight, bacterial leaf spot) were not confirmed by any digest finding.

pest_resistance.summary: Leaf webber and capsule borer (Antigastra catalaunalis): incidence was recorded on Prachi from early August in a field study of sucking-insect response across sesame genotypes. This study records incidence only and gives no resistance rating, so no resistance is confirmed. Sucking-insect counts were recorded weekly on Prachi, but no resistance score was reported. search_metadata.evidence_digest:
STRESS TOLERANCE
- AICRP sesame achievements table lists Prachi (ORM-17), released 2004, as black-seeded and tolerant to Cercospora and powdery mildew -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- A biochemical study of drought response lists Prachi among the drought-sensitive sesame genotypes (judged by SOD, CAT and GPX markers) -- https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC9120847/
- No evidence found for heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance specific to Prachi. The searches returned only general crop-temperature information.

DISEASE AND PEST
- AICRP achievements table: tolerant to Cercospora and powdery mildew -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- Crop-agronomy compendium (Orissa row): Prachi (ORM17) described as black-seeded and pest- and disease-resistant -- http://krishi.info/uploads/Sesame.pdf
- Field study of sucking-insect response across sesame genotypes: insect counts were recorded on the Prachi variety each week, and leaf webber and capsule borer (Antigastra catalaunalis) incidence was noted from early August -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371349455_Study_the_response_of_different_genotypes_of_sesame_against_major_sucking_insect_pests
- No quantitative resistance scores (e.g., percent damage or resistance grade) were found for Prachi.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Rice-based cropping systems page for Odisha: Prachi (ORM 17), duration 90 days, average yield 7.5 q/ha, oil content 45% -- https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/sesame/
- AICRP achievements table row for Prachi shows three unlabelled figures (800-900, 42-45, 85-90). These are probably yield (kg/ha), oil % and duration, but the labels are not stated on the page -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- Rainfed upland trial in the N-E Ghat zone of Odisha: Prachi and OSSel 84 each gave average seed yield above 4.0 q/ha and were rated most suitable for that zone -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328073756_Performance_of_sesamum_varieties_under_rainfed_upland_conditions_in_the_N-E_ghat_zone_of_Odisha
- Organic-management trial at Tadong, Sikkim (2019-20 and 2020-21), ten cultivars including Prachi, RCBD with three replications. The abstract shown does not give Prachi-specific yield figures -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360082042_Productivity_and_profitability_of_sesame_varieties_under_organic_management_condition_in_terraces_land_of_Sikkim_Himalayas
- Agronomy compendium: Prachi recommended for Orissa; the page gives no yield or duration figures for it -- http://krishi.info/uploads/Sesame.pdf
- Indian Farming (Feb 2026) on ICAR Nagaland Centre work: Prachi was identified as a high-yielding, short-duration variety suited to the region, and it recorded the highest seed yield in a comparison with Amrit -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/167197/66232/527955

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- SSR fingerprinting of 18 Indian sesame varieties: Prachi and Nirmala were reported as developed from the same parent, a mutant of B-67, and they share common parentage. This matches the parentage in the request ("mutant of Tilottama (B-67)"), but the page itself does not name Tilottama -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335056590_SSR-based_DNA_fingerprinting_of_18_elite_Indian_varieties_of_sesame_Sesamum_indicum_L
- DNA fingerprinting paper (about CUMS 17/Suprava, not Prachi): the lowest genetic distance among the genotypes tested was between Prachi and Nirmala -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335601654_DNA_Fingerprinting_of_CUMS_17_Suprava_A_Newly_Developed_Variety_of_Sesame
- No breeding-line code, QTL, marker-trait association or genome resource specific to Prachi (ORM-17) was found. The variety code A0409070 was not confirmed by any page.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- No breeder name was found for Prachi (ORM-17) in any result. The AICRP achievements page gives the release year and states but no breeder name -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- Institution as given in the request: All India Co-ordinated Research Project on Oil Seeds, Dept. of Plant Breeding & Genetics, OUAT, Bhubaneswar. The searches did not verify this from an independent page.
- No evidence found for the lead breeder or scientist name(s).

CONTACT DETAILS
- No evidence found for an official email, phone number or institute contact page for this variety.
- Address as given in the request (not verified by search): AICRP on Oil Seeds, Department of Plant Breeding & Genetics, OUAT, Bhubaneswar-751 003.
- Seednet portal (seednet.gov.in) was not retrieved, so no Seednet contact or record was checked.

PUBLICATIONS
- Authors not captured (year not captured). SSR-based DNA fingerprinting of 18 elite Indian varieties of sesame. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/335056590_SSR-based_DNA_fingerprinting_of_18_elite_Indian_varieties_of_sesame_Sesamum_indicum_L
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Performance of sesamum varieties under rainfed upland conditions in the N-E Ghat zone of Odisha. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/328073756_Performance_of_sesamum_varieties_under_rainfed_upland_conditions_in_the_N-E_ghat_zone_of_Odisha
- Authors not captured (2019-21 field seasons). Productivity and profitability of sesame varieties under organic management condition in terraces land of Sikkim Himalayas. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/360082042_Productivity_and_profitability_of_sesame_varieties_under_organic_management_condition_in_terraces_land_of_Sikkim_Himalayas
- Authors not captured (year not captured). Study the response of different genotypes of sesame against major sucking insect pests. Journal not captured -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/371349455_Study_the_response_of_different_genotypes_of_sesame_against_major_sucking_insect_pests
- Indian Farming (2026). Sesame seed production and capacity-building article (ICAR Nagaland Centre). Journal not captured -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/167197/66232/527955
- AICRP sesame achievements compendium (variety table). Authors/year not captured -- https://aicrp.icar.gov.in/sesame/achievements/major-achievements/
- No KrishiKosh thesis or DOI-level paper specifically on Prachi was found in these searches.

SEED AVAILABILITY
- Indian Farming (2026): breeder seed production of Prachi was carried out at an ICAR research farm in kharif, and seed production of Prachi and Amrit took place at Beisumpuikam village, Peren -- https://epubs.icar.org.in/index.php/IndFarm/article/download/167197/66232/527955
- No evidence found for NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU or private-dealer stock of Prachi sesame seed. Commercial results for "Prachi" were for bitter gourd, onion and similar products and were discarded.

RECOMMENDED STATES
- Odisha: supported by the Odisha rice-based cropping page (https://rkb-odisha.in/oilseed-crops-in-odisha/sesame/) and the agronomy compendium (http://krishi.info/uploads/Sesame.pdf).
- Andhra Pradesh, Kerala and Tamil Nadu (from the request): No evidence found in the searches. The AICRP achievements page has a state-wise release table, but the rows retrieved did not show these states for Prachi.
