search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: Rajasthan Til-346 (RT 346), Sesame

Search budget note: the four permitted searches ran, and a fifth call to read full pages was refused by the tool limit. Findings below come only from the search snippets, so several headings are thin.

NAME NOTE: The release-minutes name "Rajasthan Til-346 (RT 346)" was used for the searches. No Seednet portal page under "Rajasthan Til -346 (RT 346)" or variety code A0409092 was returned, so no Seednet-specific evidence exists here. Evidence below refers to the RT 346 name as it appears in the DOD and journal sources.

STRESS TOLERANCE -- No evidence found. The searches returned no stress-tolerance data for RT 346 (drought, heat, salinity, flood, waterlogging).

DISEASE AND PEST -- No evidence found. The searches returned no disease or pest resistance data for RT 346.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS -- Journal article describes RT 346 as a high-yielding white, bold-seeded sesame variety for National Zone-I, with a table comparing its important characteristics against checks for 2005 to 2007 -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jor1-26-2-021 (the snippet did not show the yield figures or maturity values).

GENETICS AND QTL -- Parentage "RT 127 x HY 24" is from the supplied record only; no search source confirmed it. No QTL, marker, or breeding-line code evidence found.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION -- Journal article lists S.R. Kumhar, Z.S. Solanki, T.S. Rajpurohit, N.I.M. Sundria and M.S. Chandawat as authors. Their roles (breeders, or otherwise) are not stated in the snippet. The supplied record names the AICRP on Sesame Agricultural Research Station, Rajasthan Agricultural University, Mandor, Jodhpur as the institution; the search returned no separate confirmation of that station page -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jor1-26-2-021

CONTACT DETAILS -- No evidence found. No breeder email, phone, postal address, or institute contact page was returned. The supplied record gives only the institution name and "Mandor - 342 304, Jodhpur", which is not verified by a search source.

PUBLICATIONS --
Kumhar, S.R., Solanki, Z.S., Rajpurohit, T.S., Sundria, N.I.M., and Chandawat, M.S. (year not shown in snippet). Rajasthan Til 346: A high yielding white and bold seeded sesame, Sesamum indicum L. variety for National Zone-I of India. Journal (volume 26, issue 2 per URL; journal name not shown in snippet) -- https://indianjournals.com/api/article-view/jor1-26-2-021
No other peer-reviewed papers, AICRP/ICAR annual reports, KrishiKosh theses, or conference papers were returned.

SEED AVAILABILITY -- Directorate of Oilseeds Development page lists RT-346 among recommended sesame varieties notified under the Seed Act from 2008 to 2019 -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx. No NSC, State Seed Corporation, KVK, SAU, or private dealer listing was found.

RECOMMENDED STATES -- DOD page shows RT-346 in the state-wise notification table, with the Gujarat row listing RT-346 among its varieties -- https://oilseeds.dac.gov.in/Sesame.aspx. The same page's notes also list "Rajasthan, Gujarat, UP" as recommended states/regions, but the snippet does not clearly tie that line to RT-346. The supplied record lists Gujarat, Haryana, Himachal Pradesh, Karnataka, Maharashtra, Punjab, and Rajasthan; only Gujarat (and possibly Rajasthan) is supported by search evidence.

seednet_fields.Institution Responsible for developing B: BREEDER AICRP ON SOYABEAN, RAK COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE, AGRICULTURE, SEHORE (MP).
seednet_fields.Parentage: J.S. 78-77 (KALITUR X P.S. 73-22) X J-S 71-05.J.S. 78-77 IS A DERIVATIVE OF KALITUR AND P.S. 73-22. IT HAS GOOD GERMINATION & SEED VIABILITY FROM KALITUR AND EARLINESS FROM P.S. 73-22. (AN EXTRA EARLY MATURING SELECTION MADE AT PANTNAGAR).  J.S. 71-05 IS AN EARLY MATURING SELECTION MADE AT JABALPUR IN 1971 FROM D. 64-8707 (LEE TYPE) RECEIVE FROM USA HAVING BOLD SEED SIZE, POOR SEED VIABILITY & GERMINATION BUT HAVING RESISTANCE/TOLERANCE TO.
seednet_fields.Adaptation and recommended ecology: RECOMMENDED FOR FRLEASE & CULTIVATION IN GUJARAT, RAJASTHAN, NORTHERN AND WESTERN PARTS OF MAHARASHTRA. MP, EXCLUDING NORTHEN PARTS OF MADHYA PRADESH. IT IS SUITABLE FOR TIMELY SOWING, IRRIGATED AND RAINFED CONDITIONS.
seednet_fields.Agronomic Features: 1. JS 335 IS RESISTANT TO LODGING UNDER NORMAL PLANT POPULATION. 2. JS. 335 DOES NOT SHATTER FOR ABOUT 10 DAYS AFTER MATURITY. 3. RESPONSIVENESS OF JS. 335 TO OPTIMUM DOSE OF 20 KG.N/HA. 60-80 KG P2O5/HA AND 20 K2O KG/HA. 4. JS 335 MAINTAINS YIELD SUPERIORITY BOTH UNDER RAINFED & IRRIGATED CONDITIONS. 5. SOWING DATE OF JS. 335  CAN BE DEVIATED BY 15 DAYS FROM THE NORMAL SOWING DATE. 6. SEED RATE REQUIREMENT OF JS.335 IS 80 TO 100 KG/HA. OPTIMUM PLANT POPULANTION IS 4 TO 6 LAKH/HA. 7. FIELD GERMINATION IS GOOD
seednet_fields.Specific Morphological Characteristics: 1. PROTEIN CONTENT 36.92%, 2. OIL 17.3 TO 18.8%.,3. 100 SEED WEIGHT 11.2 TO 11.9 GM.
seednet_fields.General Morphological Characteristics: PLANT HEIGHT : MEAN 46.0 CM RANGE 20-72 CM. 1. SEMI-DETERMINATE HABIT 2.SHARSE PUBESCENCE ON LEAVES, STEM & PODS, BROWN IN COLOUR 2. SEED YELLOW ROUND WITH BLACK HILUM. 4. LEAVES DARK GREEN AT FLOWERING. 5. FLOWER PURPLE.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Stress: TOLERANT TO MOISTURE STRESS CONDITIONS SINCE JS. 335  RECORDED HIGHEST YIELD BOTH UNDER RAINFED & IRRIGATED CONDITIONS.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Diseases: 1. JS 335 IS RESISTANT TO BACTERIAL PUSTULES, BACTERIAL BLIGHT, GREEN MOSAIC & ALTERNARIA LEAF SPOT. 2. JS 335 IS MODERATELY SUSCEPTIBLE TO POD BLIGHT. 3. JS 335 IS TOLERANT OT BUD BLIGHT.
seednet_fields.Reaction to Major Pests: 1. JS 335 IS TOLERANT TO STEM FLY (MELANAGROMYZA SOZAE) 2. JS 335 IS MODERATELY SUCEPTIBLE TO JASSIDS. 3. AS REGARDS OTHER PESTS, JS 335 IS AT PAR WITH OTHER VARIETIES.

drought.details: Moisture-stress tolerance is claimed on two seller pages (skbseeds.com and samratseedsindia.com); the digest notes these are not peer-reviewed or official sources. The CSC record states JS 335 is tolerant to moisture stress because it recorded the highest yield under both rainfed and irrigated conditions. No independent field data on drought mechanisms was found in the digest. Level is medium because the evidence is seller claims plus the CSC record, with no official or peer-reviewed confirmation.

disease_resistance.summary: Resistance or tolerance claims (CSC record, not linked to a digest URL): resistant to bacterial pustules, bacterial blight, green mosaic and Alternaria leaf spot; moderately susceptible to pod blight; tolerant to bud blight. Seller pages: tolerant to bacterial blight and yellow mosaic virus (YMV) (yashodaseeds.com); resistance to bacterial pustule, bacterial blight, bud blight and Alternaria leaf blight (kisaanhelpline.com, Hindi-language page). Contrary evidence: the AICRP Soybean Annual Progress Report 2024-25 records the highest MLS severity at 77 percent on JS 335 at Sehore, and lists JS 335 as a susceptible check in disease screening. JNKVV states JS 335 is now susceptible to many biotic stresses. A Business Standard report says JS-335 seed lost disease and pest resistance over time because of a low seed replacement ratio of about 10-12 percent. Overall, the resistance claims are inconsistent with the official and press evidence.

pest_resistance.summary: Stem fly: tolerance or resistance claimed on seller pages (girdle beetle and stem fly); CSC record states tolerance to stem fly (Melanagromyza sojae). AICRP stem fly screening (kharif 2022 and 2023, RBD, 21 genotypes, JS 335 as susceptible check) reports a check-entry stem fly infestation of 19.25 percent and seedling mortality of 5.62 percent for JS 335, which does not support a strong resistance rating. Girdle beetle: resistance claimed on seller pages only. Jassids: CSC record states moderately susceptible. Other pests: CSC record states at par with other varieties. Business Standard reports farmers in Madhya Pradesh abandoned JS-335 due to frequent pest attacks.

agronomic_details.yield: Seller claims (inconsistent units and values): 10-12 quintal/acre (fuleseeds.com); 25-30 quintal/ha (skbseeds.com); 30-35 quintal/ha potential (yashodaseeds.com); 30 quintal/ha (samratseedsindia.com). Sowing-window trial (Journal of Soils and Crops): mean seed yield about 3383 kg/ha. DSSAT simulation (1988-2018 weather): simulated average grain yield 1487 kg/ha across North Interior Karnataka, and 1655 kg/ha on red soils. CSC average_yield: Unknown.
agronomic_details.stability: CSC record states JS 335 maintains yield superiority under both rainfed and irrigated conditions and recorded the highest yield in both. It is resistant to lodging under normal plant population and does not shatter for about 10 days after maturity. Business Standard reports low yield and frequent pest attacks led farmers in Madhya Pradesh to abandon JS-335. The digest also reports lost disease and pest resistance linked to a low seed replacement ratio.
agronomic_details.adaptation: CSC record: recommended for cultivation in Gujarat, Rajasthan, northern and western parts of Maharashtra, and Madhya Pradesh excluding northern parts; suitable for timely sowing under irrigated and rainfed conditions. Sowing date may deviate by 15 days from normal. Seed rate 80-100 kg/ha; optimum plant population 4-6 lakh/ha; field germination reported as good (CSC record). The sowing-window trial reports the highest seed yield at the second sowing date.
agronomic_details.maturity_days: 88 To 107Days (CSC record). Digest sources vary: 90-95 days (fuleseeds.com); 90-100 days (skbseeds.com); 100-105 days (yashodaseeds.com); 115-120 days (swarajseeds.in); 113-121 days across sowing dates (Journal of Soils and Crops trial).
agronomic_details.plant_characteristics: 1. PROTEIN CONTENT 36.92%, 2. OIL 17.3 TO 18.8%.,3. 100 SEED WEIGHT 11.2 TO 11.9 GM. (CSC record). Seller catalogues (fuleseeds.com; indiamart.com): purple flowers, glabrous stems and pods, yellow seed, dark brown hilum, dark green leaves, 14.43 g test weight. Hypocotyl anthocyanin pigmentation is present in JS-335 but absent in most RILs tested (ResearchGate).
agronomic_details.field_trials: (1) Sowing-window trial (Journal of Soils and Crops, Dec 2020): maturity 113-121 days across sowing dates; highest seed yield at the second sowing date; mean seed yield about 3383 kg/ha. (2) DSSAT crop simulation (not a field trial) using 1988-2018 weather: simulated average 1487 kg/ha across North Interior Karnataka; 1655 kg/ha on red soils. (3) Front-line demonstration at Phek district, Nagaland (KVK Porba with AICRP Soybean, 2020-21 and 2021-22, 20 farmers) using JS 335 as the demonstration variety; no yield result stated in the digest. (4) Comparative economics study of JS-335 and MAUS-71 farms (farm survey data, IJCMAS): reports labour and input use for JS-335 growers; no yield result stated. (5) AICRP stem fly screening, kharif 2022 and 2023 (RBD, 21 genotypes, JS 335 as susceptible check): check-entry stem fly infestation 19.25 percent; seedling mortality 5.62 percent. (6) AICRP Soybean Annual Progress Report 2024-25: highest MLS severity 77 percent on JS 335 at Sehore; JS 335 listed as a susceptible check in disease screening and among entries in an indent.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
VARIETY NAME CHECK: Both names are covered. Every result refers to "JS 335" or "JS-335" from seed-seller, journal, or AICRP pages. No result shows the Seednet name "JAWAHAR SOYBEAN-335 (JS-335)" or variety code A0410001, so no evidence was found under the Seednet name itself.

STRESS TOLERANCE
Tolerance to moisture stress is claimed on seed-seller pages, not in a peer-reviewed or official source -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/soybean-js-335
Tolerance to moisture stress is also claimed on a second seller page, which adds that it is good at germinating and lasting in storage -- https://samratseedsindia.com/soybean-seed.html (https://www.samratseedsindia.com/soybean-seed.html)
JNKVV's own site says JS 335 is now "susceptible to many biotic stresses" and that newer JNKVV varieties were released to break its monoculture -- https://www.jnkvv.org/
A Business Standard report says JS-335 seed lost disease and pest resistance over time because of a low seed replacement ratio of about 10-12 percent -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/mp-farmers-change-soy-seed-over-low-yield-106042601110_1.html
A seller page lists the variety as tolerant to bacterial blight and yellow mosaic virus (YMV) -- https://yashodaseeds.com/product/notified-soybean-seeds/js-335
A Hindi-language seller page lists resistance to bacterial pustule, bacterial blight, bud blight and Alternaria leaf blight -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/crops/product/5_JS–335Soybean
No official evidence of drought, heat, salinity, flood or submergence tolerance was found beyond the moisture-stress claims above.

DISEASE AND PEST
Resistance to girdle beetle and stem fly is claimed on seller pages -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/soybean-js-335 ; https://swarajseeds.in/product/js-335-soybean-seeds/ (see also https://indiamart.com/proddetail/js-335-soybean-seeds-27369009730.html)
AICRP Soybean stem fly screening (kharif 2022 and 2023, RBD, 21 genotypes, JS 335 used as susceptible check) reports a check-entry stem fly infestation of 19.25 percent and seedling mortality of 5.62 percent for JS 335 -- https://arccarticles.s3.amazonaws.com/OnlinePublish/Final-article-attachemnt-with-doi-LR-5312-6089603e9087340b9bdcbbb1.pdf
The AICRP Soybean Annual Progress Report 2024-25 records the highest MLS (megalocytivirus-like/ leaf-spot severity, as listed) at 77 percent on JS 335 at Sehore -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
The same report lists JS 335 among entries in an indent for varieties, and JS 335 as a susceptible check in disease screening; no resistance rating beyond these entries was found -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
A Business Standard report says farmers in Madhya Pradesh were abandoning JS-335 because of years of low yield and frequent pest attacks -- https://www.business-standard.com/article/markets/mp-farmers-change-soy-seed-over-low-yield-106042601110_1.html

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
Maturity is inconsistent across sources: 90-95 days on a seller catalogue -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/js-335/ ; 90-100 days on another -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/soybean-js-335 ; 100-105 days on another -- https://yashodaseeds.com/product/notified-soybean-seeds/js-335 ; 115-120 days on another -- https://swarajseeds.in/product/js-335-soybean-seeds/
A sowing-window trial reports JS-335 maturing in 113-121 days across sowing dates, and it recorded the highest seed yield at the second sowing date -- https://www.journalofsoilsandcrops.com/Download/dec2020issue/28.pdf
The same trial reports a mean seed yield of about 3383 kg/ha for JS-335 -- https://www.journalofsoilsandcrops.com/Download/dec2020issue/28.pdf
A simulation study (DSSAT, 1988-2018 weather) gives a simulated average grain yield of 1487 kg/ha across North Interior Karnataka, with 1655 kg/ha on red soils -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/354047958_PERFORMANCE_OF_SOYBEAN_VARIETY_JS-335_UNDER_CURRENT_CLIMATE_IN_DIFFERENT_DISTRICTS_OF_NORTH_INTERIOR_KARNATAKA
Seller yield claims vary: 10-12 quintal/acre -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/js-335/ ; 25-30 quintal/ha -- https://www.skbseeds.com/product/soybean-js-335 ; 30-35 quintal/ha potential -- https://yashodaseeds.com/product/notified-soybean-seeds/js-335 ; 30 quintal/ha -- https://www.samratseedsindia.com/soybean-seed.html
A front-line demonstration in Phek district, Nagaland (KVK Porba with AICRP Soybean, 2020-21 and 2021-22, 20 farmers) used JS 335 as the demonstration variety -- https://indianjournals.com/article/jkv-11-2-049
A comparative economics study of JS-335 and MAUS-71 farms, using farm survey data, reports labour and input use for JS-335 growers -- https://www.ijcmas.com/9-3-2020/Babasaheb%20R.%20Gunjale,%20et%20al.pdf
Plant morphology claims (purple flowers, glabrous stems and pods, yellow seed, dark brown hilum, dark green leaves, 14.43 g test weight) come from a seller catalogue -- https://fuleseeds.com/products/js-335/ ; https://indiamart.com/proddetail/js-335-soybean-seeds-27369009730.html

Parentage (J.S. 78-77 x J.S. 71-05; J.S. 78-77 = Kalitur x P.S. 73-22; J.S. 71-05 selected at Jabalpur in 1971 from D. 64-8707) is supplied only by the record provided; no independent source was found -- no independent URL found
Hypocotyl anthocyanin pigmentation is present in JS-335 but absent in most of the RILs tested -- https://www.researchgate.net/publication/391835595_Phenotypic_Diversity_and_Trait_Analysis_of_Soybean_Recombinant_Inbred_Lines
JS 335 is used as a parent in crosses in the AICRP Soybean 2024-25 report (for example JS 335 x NRC 136 and JS 335 x NRC 128) -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
Derived crosses JS 20-29 x JS 335 are reported in the same AICRP report -- http://icar-nsri.res.in/pdfdoc/AicrpsAR2024-25.pdf
No QTL, marker, genome-resource or breeding-line

official_quote.quote: JS 335 IS RESISTANT TO BACTERIAL PUSTULES, BACTERIAL BLIGHT, GREEN MOSAIC & ALTERNARIA LEAF SPOT

disease_resistance.research_summary: Resistance or tolerance claims (CSC record, not linked to a digest URL): resistant to bacterial pustules, bacterial blight, green mosaic and Alternaria leaf spot; moderately susceptible to pod blight; tolerant to bud blight. Seller pages: tolerant to bacterial blight and yellow mosaic virus (YMV) (yashodaseeds.com); resistance to bacterial pustule, bacterial blight, bud blight and Alternaria leaf blight (kisaanhelpline.com, Hindi-language page). Contrary evidence: the AICRP Soybean Annual Progress Report 2024-25 records the highest MLS severity at 77 percent on JS 335 at Sehore, and lists JS 335 as a susceptible check in disease screening. JNKVV states JS 335 is now susceptible to many biotic stresses. A Business Standard report says JS-335 seed lost disease and pest resistance over time because of a low seed replacement ratio of about 10-12 percent. Overall, the resistance claims are inconsistent with the official and press evidence.

official_quote.quote: JS 335 IS TOLERANT TO STEM FLY (MELANAGROMYZA SOZAE) 2

pest_resistance.research_summary: Stem fly: tolerance or resistance claimed on seller pages (girdle beetle and stem fly); CSC record states tolerance to stem fly (Melanagromyza sojae). AICRP stem fly screening (kharif 2022 and 2023, RBD, 21 genotypes, JS 335 as susceptible check) reports a check-entry stem fly infestation of 19.25 percent and seedling mortality of 5.62 percent for JS 335, which does not support a strong resistance rating. Girdle beetle: resistance claimed on seller pages only. Jassids: CSC record states moderately susceptible. Other pests: CSC record states at par with other varieties. Business Standard reports farmers in Madhya Pradesh abandoned JS-335 due to frequent pest attacks.

drought.details: The CSC variety record (ground truth) describes MACS-450 as tolerant to moisture stress. The evidence digest found no independent drought-tolerance evidence specific to this variety. The only related digest item (kisaanhelpline.com) is cultivation advice: one or two light irrigations if soil moisture is short during pod filling in kharif. That item is not a tolerance rating. The level is medium because it rests on the CSC statement alone, which the digest could not corroborate. No mechanisms were found.

search_metadata.evidence_digest:
EVIDENCE DIGEST: MACS-450 (soybean)

Name check: the CSC name and the Seednet name are both "MACS-450". The search index returned no Seednet portal page, so every Seednet-related finding below comes from other sources and is marked as such. Several sources also write the name as "MACS 450" (no hyphen), and I treated these as the same variety. "Bragg x MACS 111" refers to this variety's parentage and was not checked against other MACS lines. Search queries run: 4 (release/agronomy, breeder/institute, research/publications, seed availability).

STRESS TOLERANCE
- No evidence found for drought, heat, salinity, flood, or submergence tolerance specific to MACS-450. The only related result was a general statement that the kharif crop needs only one or two light irrigations if soil moisture is short during pod filling, which is cultivation advice and not a tolerance rating. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/soybean-macs-450 (secondary site, not an official source)

DISEASE AND PEST
- Secondary-site listing says MACS-450 is resistant to leaf spot, bud blight, yellow mosaic, soybean mosaic, and bacterial pustule, and is highly resistant to stemfly and defoliators. This is an unverified commercial listing, not a trial report. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/soybean-macs-450
- An intechopen chapter's table places MACS 450 among the defoliator-resistant varieties. -- https://www.intechopen.com/chapters/1173727

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS
- Station trials gave an average seed yield of 3422 kg/ha, the coordinated breeding trials 2361 kg/ha, and the varieties-cum-plant-population trial 2215 kg/ha. -- https://inis.iaea.org/records/ajgcg-dm117
- Farmer-field frontline demonstrations recorded 4076 kg/ha (1998) and 3582 kg/ha (1999) on an all-India basis. -- https://inis.iaea.org/records/ajgcg-dm117
- The secondary listing gives 25–40 quintals/ha yield, a 90–95 day duration, and a semi-determinate, medium-tall habit with purple flowers and yellow seed with black hilum. -- https://www.kisaanhelpline.com/variety/soybean-macs-450
- Annual Report 2011-12 records nine frontline demonstrations in Baramati taluka, Pune, comparing MACS 450 with other varieties. The report does not give a separate yield figure for MACS 450. -- https://aripune.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/ARI-2011-12-English.pdf

GENETICS AND QTL (genes, parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources)
- Parentage: selected from the Bragg x MACS 111 cross by pedigree selection. -- https://inis.iaea.org/records/ajgcg-dm117
- MACS 111 is a mutant line derived from the indigenous black-seeded 'Kalitur' variety treated with gamma irradiation plus ethyleneimine (as written in the source). -- https://inis.iaea.org/records/ajgcg-dm117
- The Ijrar paper reports that MACS 450 seed was subjected to gamma-ray and EMS mutagenesis, and it reports trait correlations among the resulting mutants. -- https://www.ijrar.org/papers/IJRAR1BSP022.pdf
- No QTL, marker, gene, or genome-resource study naming MACS-450 was found. Results for QTL studies in other soybean lines were excluded.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION
- The 2000 conference paper names Raut, V.M., Taware, S.P., Halvankar, G.B., and Varghese, Philips, from the Division of Plant Sciences, Agharkar Research Institute, Pune. -- https://www.osti.gov/etdeweb/biblio/20186647
- The ARI Genetics and Plant Breeding page lists MACS 450 among eight soybean varieties developed by that centre. The page does not name a breeder for MACS 450. -- https://aripune.res.in/genetics-and-plant-breeding
- Santosh Jaybhay and Abhinandan S. Patil appear on ARI pages, but no source ties either to MACS-450, so I have not attributed the variety to them.
- Institution: MACS-Agharkar Research Institute (ARI), Pune, an autonomous institute of the Department of Science and Technology (DST), Government of India. -- https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Agharkar_Research_Institute

- Institute-level contacts from a PIB press release (about MACS 1407, not MACS-450, but the same institute): Santosh Jaybhay, sajaybhay@aripune.org, 020-25325036, Genetics & Plant Breeding Group; Dr P.K. Dhakephalkar, Director, director@aripune.org, pkdhakephalkar@aripune.org, 020-25325002. -- https://pib.gov.in/Pressreleaseshare.aspx?PRID=1714852

Agarkar Road," which matches. -- https://aripune.res.in/wp-content/uploads/2017/03/ARI-2011-12-English.pdf
- Institute website: https://www.aripune.org (per Wikipedia), and https://aripune.res.in (the site where the genetics pages sit).

disease_resistance.summary: Per the variety record (CSC ground truth; not confirmed by digest search results): moderately resistant to collar rot, bacterial pustule, pod blight and bud blight-like syndrome diseases. No digest evidence confirms this.

pest_resistance.summary: Per the variety record (CSC ground truth; not confirmed by digest search results): moderately resistant to stemfly and leaf miner insect pests. No digest evidence confirms this.

agronomic_details.yield: Per the variety record (CSC ground truth; not confirmed by digest search results): average yield 3500.00 to 4000.00 Kg/Ha.
agronomic_details.stability: Per the variety record only: non-lodging under optimum plant population; non-shattering up to 10 days after harvest maturity; better than JS 335; suitable for both normal and late sown conditions; consistently high yields over years under abnormal weather. No digest evidence confirms these.
agronomic_details.adaptation: Per the variety record only: recommended for rainfed conditions with variable rainfall in Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra (Vidarbha and Marathwada), Rajasthan and the Bundelkhand region of Uttar Pradesh. Search status: Four web_search queries ran in the first pass. A second pass to pull full page text for keyword matches hit the tool-use limit, so the findings below come only from the first-pass snippets. Several headings are therefore thin, and the record needs a manual check of the pages listed as leads.

Name check: The CSC name is "Ahilya-4 (NRC-37)" and the Seednet name is "AHILYA-4 (NRC-37)". Neither search returned a page that names this variety, so no finding below is attributed to either name.

STRESS TOLERANCE: No evidence found. The searches returned no page naming Ahilya-4 (NRC-37) with stress-tolerance data.

DISEASE AND PEST: No evidence found. No page naming this variety with disease or pest reaction data was returned.

AGRONOMY AND TRIALS: No evidence found. No page naming this variety with maturity, yield or multi-location trial data was returned.

GENETICS AND QTL (parentage, breeding-line codes, breeding method, genome resources): No evidence found. The parentage given in the variety record (GAURAV X PUNJAB-1) was not confirmed by any search result. Only the variety record itself states it.

BREEDER AND INSTITUTION: No evidence found. The variety record gives the institution as National Research Centre for Soybean, Indore-452017. No search result named a breeder or developing scientist for this variety.

CONTACT DETAILS: No evidence found. No breeder or institute contact details were confirmed for this variety. Lead only: the ICAR-Indian Institute of Soybean Research varieties page (https://iisrindore.icar.gov.in/varieties.html) lists earlier NRC soybean releases, including Ahilya 1, 2 and 3. The snippet I saw was cut off before any Ahilya-4 entry, so I did not confirm that this variety appears on that page. Check that page's full table and its contact page directly.

PUBLICATIONS: No evidence found. The research search returned no paper, report, thesis or KrishiKosh record naming this variety. One SOYCON-2014 proceedings PDF on climate change and soybean production (https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Ivsrinivasa-Reddy/publication/357734965_IMPACT_OF_CLIMATE_CHANGE_ON_SOYABEAN_PRODUCTION/links/61dd0a5b4e4aff4a6432bdb0/IMPACT-OF-CLIMATE-CHANGE-ON-SOYABEAN-PRODUCTION.pdf) came up, but its snippet did not name this variety, so I have excluded it.

RECOMMENDED STATES: No evidence found in search results. The variety record lists Madhya Pradesh, Maharashtra, Rajasthan and Uttar Pradesh, with Madhya Pradesh repeated. That list is unverified and comes from the input record only.
